summary:
Le, Le Hung, Levin and Morra prove, for generic tame data, the three-dimensional analogues of Breuil's lattice conjecture, the weight part of Serre's conjecture and the geometric Breuil–Mézard conjecture. For a CM field F/F⁺ unramified at all finite places, p unramified in F⁺ with every place above p split, and a definite unitary group G, Theorem 5.3.5 shows that for r : G_F → GL3(E) potentially crystalline of Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0), minimally ramified and with r̄ 10-generic and semisimple at p, the lattice cut out in a 13-generic tame type by completed cohomology depends only on r at the places above p. Along the way: Theorem 5.3.3 (W(r̄) = Herzig's W^?), Theorem 5.3.4 (mod p multiplicity one), Theorem 5.3.1 (automorphy lifting), Theorem 3.5.2 (numerical Breuil–Mézard for weak minimal patching functors) and Proposition 3.6.1 (geometric Breuil–Mézard). The local inputs are the shape charts of LLHLM18 and explicit ideal computations (Tables 3–4); the representation-theoretic input is Theorem 4.1.9, a complete description of the reductions of lattices with irreducible cosocle in a generic Deligne–Lusztig representation of GL3 over a finite field (distance in the extension graph equals radical depth, predicted extension graphs, rigidity), proved with the modular representation theory of GL3 (Frobenius kernels, injective envelopes, Weyl modules). Section 6 corrects 25 points of LLHLM18.

The extraction has 593 items: 6 in the libraries, 25 planned and 562 missing. Almost nothing is planned: no layer has affine Weyl group and alcove combinatorics, Deligne–Lusztig representations, Jantzen's modular representation theory, Serre weights for GL3 or patching functors. The missing items keep the checkpoint's routes: a Part II of Tau Ceti's Reductive algebraic groups roadmap for the modular representation theory (§§1.4, 2.1, 2.3, 4), a Part II of Algebraic modular forms, reduction and Serre weights for the Serre weights, patching and lattices (§§2.2, 3.4–3.5, 5), and sources of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (shapes and the explicit rings of §3), DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra, CompletedCohomologyPartII and SchemeAndStackFoundations; the sibling extraction of LLHLM23 shares both Part II ids.

The paper was read in full, proofs included, and 132 mistakes are recorded (8 errors and 4 gaps reaching a stated result among them), 25 of them the authors' own corrections to LLHLM18 printed in §6. None changes a main theorem as used, but several statements are false or unproved as printed: Proposition 3.4.2 without the shape hypothesis, Proposition 4.2.9, the table entries of Table 3 (identity row) and Table 4 (γαγ row), and Theorem 5.3.1, whose proof defers to LLHLM18 Theorem 7.4, whose proof §6(16) says was omitted. No erratum exists.

conventions.coefficients: p>3; E/Q_p finite and sufficiently large for all embeddings, tame types and constituent fields of definition; O its integers, varpi a uniformizer, F its residue field. p and varpi are distinct symbols. Finite O-module means finitely generated, not necessarily torsion. Unless explicitly specified, type rings impose parallel Hodge–Tate weights eta=(2,1,0), with cyclotomic character of weight +1.
conventions.local: K_v/Q_p is unramified in the main numerical/GL3 assertions; k_v has p^f_v elements and J is the disjoint union of its embeddings, f=sum f_v. Distinguish the algebraic restriction-of-scalars GL3 group, its finite group of rational points, and G1T. Genericity is measured via lowest-alcove presentations and D01. Semisimplicity of a Galois representation is an independent hypothesis, not implied by inertial genericity.
conventions.notation: sigma(tau)^sigma denotes the O-lattice with irreducible residual cosocle sigma, not a power. Rbar means reduction modulo varpi. Graph arrows run from quotient to subobject. Radical grades start at zero; soc_-1=0. The lattice exponent in Theorem 4.1.9(5) is a power of p after unramified descent, even if E is ramified.

global.field: F/F+ is CM with F+≠Q; F/F+ is unramified at every finite place, p is unramified in F+, and each p-place of F+ splits in F. Fix a lift v-tilde in F of every relevant split place.
global.group: G/F+ is the definite unitary outer form of GL3 used in §5.3: compact at every real place and quasi-split at finite places, split by F. Fix the integral model and split-place identifications iota_v with GL3(O_Fv)..
global.residual: The continuous residual rbar is automorphic, has split ramification and satisfies D21; at all p-places it is semisimple, and at the chosen lifts it is 10-generic. Automorphic means nonzero localized finite-level algebraic automorphic forms for some coefficients; level lowering supplies the fixed minimal choices below.
global.level: Choose the auxiliary place v1 as in CEG+16 §2.3 (.). U^p is hyperspecial at split v≠v1, the inverse image of upper triangular matrices at v1, and hyperspecial at inert v. Sigma0 contains precisely the ramified away-p places. W is a fixed O-lattice in the product of their minimal types as in CHT08 Definition 2.4.14.
global.hecke: Use the paper’s dual convention: det(1−rbar^dual(Frob_w)X)=sum_(j=0)^3 (−1)^j Norm(w)^(j(j−1)/2) alpha(T_w^(j)) X^j. m is the kernel of alpha; lambda is the characteristic-zero eigensystem of the lift. Keep the distinguished v1 Hecke operator and omitted finite places as in §5.3.
global.lift: For T48/T49, r is continuous, absolutely irreducible, almost everywhere unramified, r^c≅r^dual epsilon^−2, potentially crystalline of type ((2,1,0),tau_v) at chosen p-places, with the residual automorphic K-type condition of T48. T49 additionally requires a 13-generic tame p-type and minimal ramification away from p in the exact CHT sense. The conclusion is locality up to homothety.

items.name: §1.1 — global setup for Breuil's lattice conjecture (completed cohomology H̃, eigensystem λ, tame type σ(τ))
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F/F⁺ a CM extension (F a totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real field F⁺) unramified everywhere, and r : G_F → GL₃(Q̄_p) a Galois representation. Let λ be the Hecke eigensystem corresponding to r, which appears in the cohomology of a U(3)-arithmetic manifold. Choose a place v|p of F⁺ which splits in F and let H̃ be the integral p-adically completed cohomology with infinite level at v. Suppose r is tamely potentially crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0) at each place above p; in §1 r is assumed unramified away from p (the results hold if r is minimally split ramified). Assume every place v|p of F⁺ splits in F and fix a place ṽ|v for all v|p. Let σ(τ) be the tame type corresponding under the inertial local Langlands correspondence to the Weil–Deligne representations associated with r|_{G_{F_ṽ}} for all v|p; throughout §1, σ(τ) is assumed sufficiently generic.
items.note: Informal setup of the introduction; the precise global setting is §5.3 (Theorem 5.3.1 hypotheses, weak minimal patching functors of §3.5). 'Sufficiently generic' is made precise in the body (13-generic in Theorem 5.3.5). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: §1.1 — σ(τ) occurs with multiplicity one in H̃[λ][1/p] (classical local–global compatibility)
items.statement: In the setup of §1.1, if r is modular, then H̃[λ][1/p] contains σ(τ) with multiplicity one.
items.note: Stated as a consequence of 'classical local–global compatibility'; not proved in the paper. It is what makes σ(τ)⁰ := σ(τ) ∩ H̃[λ] a well-defined lattice up to homothety (Theorem 1.1.1). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Theorem 1.1.1 — Breuil's lattice conjecture for GL₃ (introduction form of Theorem 5.3.5)
items.statement: In the setup of §1.1 (r tamely potentially crystalline of Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0) at all places above p, unramified outside p, every v|p split in F, σ(τ) sufficiently generic, r modular), assume that p is unramified in F⁺, that r̄ satisfies the Taylor–Wiles hypotheses and is semisimple at places above p, and that the level of H̃ outside p is minimal with respect to r. Then the lattice σ(τ)⁰ := σ(τ) ∩ H̃[λ] ⊂ σ(τ) depends only on the collection {r|_{G_{F_ṽ}}}_{v|p}.
items.note: Introduction restatement; proved as Theorem 5.3.5 (13-generic tame type, r minimally ramified, as in Theorem 5.3.1). Analogue of [EGS15, Theorems 8.2.1, 10.2.1] in dimension two; for p split in F⁺ and r̄ irreducible above p proved in [Le18]. The paper proves σ(τ)⁰ is 'purely local' without an explicit description. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Theorem 1.1.2 — mod p multiplicity one for lattices with irreducible upper alcove cosocle
items.statement: Keep the assumptions of Theorem 1.1.1, and let H̄ be the mod p reduction of H̃ (the mod p cohomology with infinite level at places above p of a U(3)-arithmetic manifold). Let σ(τ)^σ be a lattice in σ(τ) such that its mod p reduction σ̄(τ)^σ has an irreducible upper alcove cosocle σ. Then Hom_{K_p}(σ̄(τ)^σ, H̄[λ]) is one-dimensional.
items.note: Here H̄[λ] means the eigenspace for the reduction of λ, i.e. H̄[𝔪] in the body (Theorem 5.3.4 uses [𝔪]); K_p = ∏_{v|p} GL₃(O_{F_ṽ}). Key input: Theorem 5.1.1 (the minimal patched module M_∞(σ(τ)^σ) is free of rank one over R_∞(τ) when σ is upper alcove in every embedding). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: §1.2 — Herzig/Gee–Herzig–Savitt Serre weight prediction W_v(r̄) = W^?(r̄|_{I_{F_ṽ}}) (conjecture, cited)
items.statement: Let r̄ : G_F → GL₃(F) be a mod p Galois representation whose Hecke eigensystem 𝔪 appears in the mod p cohomology with infinite level at v of a U(3)-arithmetic manifold, and let W_v(r̄) be the set of Jordan–Hölder factors of the GL₃(O_{F_ṽ})-socle of H̄[𝔪] (H̄[𝔪] is a smooth representation of G(F_v⁺), identified with a GL₃(O_{F_ṽ})-representation through ι_ṽ : G_v(O_{F_v⁺}) ≅ GL₃(O_{F_ṽ})). If r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}} is tamely ramified, the conjecture predicts W_v(r̄) = W^?(r̄|_{I_{F_ṽ}}), where W^?(r̄|_{I_{F_ṽ}}) is the explicit set of Definition 2.2.7.
items.note: Conjecture of [Her09, GHS18]; stated, not proved in this form (Theorem 1.2.1 proves it under hypotheses). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Theorem 1.2.1 — the weight part of Serre's conjecture for GL₃ (introduction form of Theorem 5.3.3)
items.statement: In the setting of §1.2 (r̄ : G_F → GL₃(F) with Hecke eigensystem 𝔪 appearing in the mod p cohomology with infinite level at v), assume that p is unramified in F⁺ and that r̄ satisfies the Taylor–Wiles hypotheses, has split ramification, and is semisimple and sufficiently generic at places above p. Then W_v(r̄) = W^?(r̄|_{I_{F_ṽ}}).
items.note: Body version Theorem 5.3.3 is stated for all places above p at once with finite level K = ∏ GL₃(O_{F_ṽ}) (W(r)∘∏ι_ṽ = W^?(ρ̄_S)), r̄ automorphic and ρ̄_ṽ 10-generic. [LLHLM18] proved it when p splits in F⁺; the new ingredient is the combinatorics of §2 (Corollary 2.3.11, Corollary 2.3.13). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Theorem 1.2.2 — geometric Breuil–Mézard for potentially crystalline deformation rings of weight (2,1,0) (introduction form of Proposition 3.6.1)
items.statement: Assume that r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}} is semisimple and sufficiently generic. There is a unique assignment σ ↦ 𝔭(σ) taking Serre weights σ ∈ W^?(r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}}) to prime ideals of the unrestricted framed deformation ring R^□_{r̄|G_{F_ṽ}} such that the special fibre Spec(R̄^τ_{r̄|G_{F_ṽ}}) of the potentially crystalline framed deformation ring R^τ_{r̄|G_{F_ṽ}} of Hodge–Tate weight (2,1,0) and tame type τ is the reduced underlying subscheme of ⋃_{σ ∈ W^?(r̄|_{I_{F_ṽ}}) ∩ JH(σ̄(τ))} Spec(R^□_{r̄|G_{F_ṽ}}/𝔭(σ)). Moreover, this is compatible with any patching functor.
items.note: Τ ranges over all tame types (body: 'for any tame type τ'). Proved via the numerical Breuil–Mézard conjecture and connectedness of generic fibres, using a globally constructed patching functor (cf. [EG14]). In the body (3.6) the equality Spec(R̄^τ) = ⋃ Spec(R^□/𝔭(σ)) is with the reduced scheme structure on the right, and the image of 𝔭(σ) in R̄^τ is a minimal prime. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Theorem 1.3.1 — cosocle filtrations and saturated inclusions of lattices in generic Deligne–Lusztig representations (introduction form of Theorem 4.1.9)
items.statement: Assume that R is a sufficiently generic Deligne–Lusztig representation of GL₃(F_q) (in particular the Jordan–Hölder factors of R̄ occur with multiplicity one). For σ ∈ JH(R̄) let R^σ be the unique lattice (up to homothety) with cosocle σ. If σ, σ' ∈ JH(R̄) and d_gph(σ, σ') = d, then: (1) σ' is a direct summand of the d-th layer of the cosocle filtration of R̄^σ; (2) if σ'' ∈ JH(R̄) satisfies d_gph(σ, σ'') = d+1 and d_gph(σ', σ'') = 1, then R̄^σ has a subquotient isomorphic to the unique nonsplit extension of σ' by σ''; (3) if R^{σ'} ⊆ R^σ is a saturated inclusion of lattices, then p^d R^σ ⊆ R^{σ'} is also a saturated inclusion.
items.note: Proved in §4 (Theorem 4.1.9, 13-generic): first (1),(2) for lower alcove weights of defect zero (Definition 2.3.8, Theorem 4.2.16) via Weyl modules and restriction to rational points (Proposition 4.2.10); then (3) for d = 1 (Proposition 4.3.7, using [LLHLM18] deformation rings, §3 combinatorics and Taylor–Wiles patching, following [EGS15, §B.2]); (3) implies (1),(2) (Proposition 4.3.16); an induction proves (3). The parts are proved together, hence one item. d_gph is Definition 2.1.8; 'extension of σ' by σ''' has σ'' as sub and σ' as quotient. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — unramified K/Q_p, the Kummer extension L = K(π) and the character ω̃_π
items.statement: Let p > 3 be a prime. For f > 0, K is the unramified extension of Q_p of degree f, with residue field k (of cardinality q = p^f) and ring of integers O_K = W(k). For r ≥ 1 set e_r := p^{fr} − 1 and fix a compatible system of roots π_r := (−p)^{1/e_r} ∈ K̄; write e := e₁ and π := π₁. Put L := K(π) and Δ₀ := Gal(L/K). The character ω̃_π : Δ₀ → W(k)^×, g ↦ g(π)/π, has associated residual character ω_π. For f = 1, ω_π is the mod p cyclotomic character, denoted ω.
items.note: Standard Kummer-theoretic set-up (as in [LLHLM18]); e = p^f − 1, so L/K is tamely totally ramified of degree e. The standing hypothesis p > 3 is fixed here. Planned: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.4 plans Breuil–Kisin modules over the Kummer tower, including descent data.

items.name: §1.4 — normalisation of local class field theory
items.statement: If F_w/Q_p is a finite extension and W_{F_w} ≤ G_{F_w} is the Weil group, Artin's reciprocity map Art_{F_w} : F_w^× → W_{F_w}^{ab} is normalised so that uniformizers are sent to geometric Frobenius elements.
items.note: Convention. Planned: Tau Ceti's ClassFieldTheory Layer 7 plans the local Artin map and its normalizations.

items.name: §1.4 — embeddings σ_i = σ₀∘φ^{−i} and the niveau-f fundamental character ω_f
items.statement: Fix an embedding σ₀ : K ↪ E; it induces O_K ↪ O and k ↪ F, all denoted σ₀. Let φ be the p-th power Frobenius on k and set σ_i := σ₀ ∘ φ^{−i}. The choice of σ₀ gives ω_f := σ₀ ∘ ω̃_π : I_K → O^×, a fundamental character of niveau f.
items.note: Ω_f is the Teichmüller-valued (O^×-valued) fundamental character, I_K acting through I_K ↠ Δ₀. The index convention σ_i = σ₀∘φ^{−i} fixes the direction of the Frobenius action π on X^*(T̲) (π(λ)_i = λ_{i−1}). Planned: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1 plans the tame inertia (fundamental) characters.

items.name: §1.4 — the Kummer tower K_∞ = ⋃ K(p_n)
items.statement: Fix once and for all a sequence p̲ := (p_n)_{n∈N} with p_n ∈ Q̄_p, p_{n+1}^p = p_n and p₀ = −p. Put K_∞ := ⋃_{n∈N} K(p_n) and G_{K_∞} := Gal(Q̄_p/K_∞).
items.note: Convention (used for étale φ-modules and Kisin modules in §3). Planned: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.4 plans Breuil–Kisin modules over the Kummer tower, including descent data.

items.name: §1.4 — labelled Hodge–Tate weights HT_σ(ρ) and 'ρ has Hodge–Tate weights μ'
items.statement: Let ρ : G_K → GL_n(E) be a p-adic de Rham Galois representation. For σ : K ↪ E ⊂ Q̄_p, HT_σ(ρ) is the multiset of σ-labelled Hodge–Tate weights of ρ, that is, the set of integers i such that dim_E (ρ ⊗_{σ,K} C_p(−i))^{G_K} ≠ 0 (usual notation for Tate twists). With this convention the cyclotomic character has Hodge–Tate weight 1 for every embedding σ : K ↪ E. For μ = (μ_j)_j ∈ X^*(T̲), ρ has Hodge–Tate weights μ if HT_{σ_j}(ρ) = {μ_{1,j}, μ_{2,j}, …, μ_{n,j}} for all j.
items.note: As a multiset, i occurs with multiplicity dim_E (ρ ⊗_{σ,K} C_p(−i))^{G_K}. X^*(T̲) is only introduced on p. 9 (forward reference). Printed 'Hodge–Tate weighs' (E18). Planned: LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 plans fixed labeled Hodge-type and inertial-type potentially semistable deformation rings in every rank, with bounded-height lattice moduli and minimally ramified conditions; LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3 plans Kisin's potentially semistable deformation rings with fixed Hodge and inertial type and their dimension.

items.name: §1.4 — inertial type of ρ, inertial types, and type (μ, τ)
items.statement: The inertial type of ρ is the isomorphism class of WD(ρ)|_{I_K}, where WD(ρ) is the Weil–Deligne representation attached to ρ as in [CDT99, Appendix B.1] (ρ ↦ WD(ρ) is covariant). An inertial type is a morphism τ : I_K → GL_n(E) with open kernel which extends to the Weil group W_K of G_K. ρ has type (μ, τ) if ρ has Hodge–Tate weights μ and inertial type (the isomorphism class of) τ.
items.note: Convention; cited construction of WD(ρ) from [CDT99]. Planned: LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 plans fixed labeled Hodge-type and inertial-type potentially semistable deformation rings in every rank, with bounded-height lattice moduli and minimally ramified conditions; LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3 plans Kisin's potentially semistable deformation rings with fixed Hodge and inertial type and their dimension.

items.name: §1.4 — the group G = GL₃/F, its diagonal torus T, root datum and root lattice
items.statement: G := GL_{3/F}, T ⊆ G the torus of diagonal matrices, X^*(T) the character group of T identified with Z³ in the usual way; R (resp. R^∨) the set of roots (resp. coroots) of G and Λ_R ⊆ X^*(T) the root lattice.
items.note: The checkpoint's statement described Mathlib's RootPairing/RootDatum carriers (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Defs.lean), which is not paper content: the paper only uses the concrete root datum of GL₃. Positive roots/coroots are taken with respect to the upper triangular Borel (p. 9). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4, (1.1) — Weyl group W, affine Weyl group W_a = Λ_R ⋊ W and extended affine Weyl group W̃ = X^*(T) ⋊ W of GL₃
items.statement: W (resp. W_a, resp. W̃) is the Weyl group (resp. affine Weyl group, resp. extended affine Weyl group) of G = GL₃/F, and W_a = Λ_R ⋊ W(G), W̃ = X^*(T) ⋊ W(G).   (1.1)
items.note: The checkpoint's statement concerned Mathlib's Weyl group of a root pairing. W ≅ S₃; W_a is a Coxeter group with simple reflections α, β, γ⁺ (p. 10, Remark 2.3.10); W̃ = W_a ⋊ Ω with Ω the stabiliser of the base alcove. items.name: §1.4 — ε'₁, ε'₂; G^der = SL₃, Λ_W = X^*(T^der), X⁰(T), ε₁, ε₂; derived Weyl groups
items.statement: Let ε'₁ := (1,0,0) and ε'₂ := (0,0,−1) in X^*(T) = Z³. Let G^der := SL_{3/F} with torus T^der, and Λ_W := X^*(T^der) the weight lattice of G^der. Let X⁰(T) be the kernel of the restriction map X^*(T) ↠ Λ_W, and ε₁, ε₂ the images of ε'₁, ε'₂ in Λ_W. The Weyl groups W^der, W_a^der, W̃^der of G^der are defined similarly, and there are canonical isomorphisms W ≅ W^der and W_a ≅ W_a^der.
items.note: X⁰(T) = Z·(1,1,1). Λ_W = Z³/Z(1,1,1) with basis ε₁, ε₂ (the fundamental weights ω₁ = [1,0,0], ω₂ = [1,1,0] = [0,0,−1]); ε₁+ε₂ = image of (1,0,−1) = image of η; Λ_W/Λ_R ≅ Z/3. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — the finite set S, the fields F_ṽ, and the embedding set J
items.statement: Let S be a finite set; for each ṽ ∈ S let F_ṽ be an unramified extension of Q_p of degree f_ṽ with residue field k_ṽ. J is the set of ring homomorphisms ∏_{ṽ∈S} k_ṽ → F. Fixing embeddings σ_{ṽ,0} : k_ṽ ↪ F and setting σ_{ṽ,i} := σ_{ṽ,0} ∘ φ^{−i}, J is identified with the set of pairs (ṽ, i_ṽ) with ṽ ∈ S and i_ṽ ∈ Z/f_ṽ. When #S = 1 the subscripts may be dropped and the single field F_ṽ is denoted K.
items.note: In applications S is a set of places of F dividing p. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — G̲₀ = ∏ Res_{k_ṽ/F_p} GL₃, G̲, T̲, Z̲; X^*(T̲) = (Z³)^J; ε'_{1,i}, ε'_{2,i}; positive roots
items.statement: G̲₀ := ∏_{ṽ∈S} Res_{k_ṽ/F_p} GL₃ with diagonal torus T̲₀ and centre Z̲₀; G̲ := G̲₀ ×_{F_p} F, and T̲, Z̲ are defined similarly. There are natural isomorphisms G̲ ≅ ∏_{i∈J} GL_{3/F} and similarly for T̲, Z̲, X^*(T̲), R̲, R̲^∨ (R̲, R̲^∨ the roots and coroots of G̲). For μ ∈ X^*(T̲) write μ = Σ_{i∈J} μ_i = Σ_{ṽ∈S} μ_ṽ. X^*(T̲) is identified with (Z³)^J; ε'_{1,i}, ε'_{2,i} are (1,0,0), (0,0,−1) in the i-th coordinate and 0 otherwise. R̲⁺ ⊆ R̲ (resp. R̲^{∨,+} ⊆ R̲^∨) are the positive roots (resp. coroots) with respect to the upper triangular Borel in each embedding; dominant (co)characters are defined with respect to these choices.
items.note: Convention. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — dominant weights X^*_+(T̲) and p-restricted weights X₁(T̲)
items.statement: X^*_+(T̲) is the set of dominant weights. X₁(T̲) ⊂ X^*_+(T̲) is the subset of λ ∈ X^*_+(T̲) with 0 ≤ ⟨λ, α^∨⟩ ≤ p − 1 for all simple roots α ∈ R̲⁺; X₁(T̲) is the set of p-restricted weights.
items.note: Standard (cf. Jantzen). X₁(T̲) is stable under X⁰(T̲)-translation. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — the weights η'_i, η', η_i and η
items.statement: η'_i ∈ X^*(T̲) is (1,0,−1) in the i-th coordinate and 0 otherwise, η' := Σ_{i∈J} η'_i; η_i ∈ X^*(T̲) is (2,1,0) in the i-th coordinate and 0 otherwise, η := Σ_{i∈J} η_i. Then η is a lift of the half-sum of the positive roots of G̲.
items.note: Η = η' + (1,1,1)_J, so η and η' have the same image ε₁+ε₂ in Λ_W; η ∉ Λ̲_R (sum of coordinates 3 ≠ 0) whereas η' ∈ Λ̲_R — relevant for the cosets W̲_a t_η. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — W̲ (with w₀), W̲_a, W̲̃, Λ̲_R and product identifications
items.statement: W̲ is the Weyl group of G̲ with longest element w₀; W̲_a and W̲̃ are the affine and extended affine Weyl groups of G̲; Λ̲_R ⊂ X^*(T̲) is the root lattice of G̲. There are identifications W̲ ≅ W^J, W̲_a ≅ W_a^J, W̲̃ ≅ W̃^J and isomorphisms analogous to (1.1) (W̲_a = Λ̲_R ⋊ W̲, W̲̃ = X^*(T̲) ⋊ W̲). The groups W̲, W̲̃, W̲_a act naturally on X^*(T̲).
items.note: Convention. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — translations t_λ and the p-dot action
items.statement: For λ ∈ X^*(T̲), t_λ denotes its image under X^*(T̲) ↪ W̲̃. The dot action is always the p-dot action: t_λ w · μ = t_{pλ} w(μ + η) − η, i.e. t_λw · μ = w(μ + η) + pλ − η, for w ∈ W̲, λ, μ ∈ X^*(T̲) (and μ ∈ X^*(T̲) ⊗ R).
items.note: Contrast with the 'usual' action t_λw(μ) = w(μ) + λ used in §2.3 for the action of W̲̃ on Λ̲_W × A (Definition 2.3.6 ff.). Note w̃·(μ + z) = w̃·μ + z for z ∈ X⁰(T̲), and w̃·(μ + ν) = w̃·μ + w(ν). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — root hyperplanes H_{α,n}, p-alcoves, p-restricted alcoves, dominant base alcove C̲₀
items.statement: For (α, n) ∈ R̲⁺ × Z, the root hyperplane is H_{α,n} := {λ : ⟨λ + η, α^∨⟩ = np}. An alcove (or p-alcove) is a connected component of X^*(T̲) ⊗_Z R ∖ ⋃_{(α,n)} H_{α,n}. An alcove C̲ is p-restricted if 0 < ⟨λ + η, α^∨⟩ < p for all simple roots α ∈ R̲⁺ and all λ ∈ C̲. C̲₀ ⊂ X^*(T̲) ⊗ R is the dominant base alcove, i.e. C̲₀ = {λ : 0 < ⟨λ+η, α^∨⟩ < p for all α ∈ R̲⁺}.
items.note: Alcoves are for the dot action, so the base alcove has a vertex at −η (§2.1). For GL₃ in one embedding there are two p-restricted alcoves: C₀ (lower) and C₁ (upper, p < ⟨λ+η, α₀^∨⟩ < 2p for the highest root α₀). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — W̲̃⁺ and W̲̃₁⁺ (elements taking C̲₀ to a dominant, resp. p-restricted, alcove); C₀, W̃⁺, W̃₁⁺ for G
items.statement: W̲̃⁺ := {w̃ ∈ W̲̃ : w̃ · C̲₀ is dominant} and W̲̃₁⁺ := {w̃ ∈ W̲̃⁺ : w̃ · C̲₀ is p-restricted}. The same definitions for G = GL₃ give the dominant base alcove C₀, W̃⁺ and W̃₁⁺.
items.note: Dot action. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — the element w̃_h = w₀ t_{−η} ∈ W̲̃₁⁺
items.note: Check (done for this reading): w₀t_{−η}·μ = w₀(μ + η − pη) − η; for μ ∈ C₀ this has ⟨·+η, α^∨⟩ ∈ (0,p) for simple α and ∈ (p, 2p) for the highest root, so w̃_h·C₀ = C₁ in each embedding and w̃_h ∈ W̲̃₁⁺. In W̃^der, w̃_h = (13)t_{−(ε₁+ε₂)} (one of the six elements of W̃₁^{der,+}); w̃_h² = t_{−(2,2,2)} ∈ X⁰-translations. Used to define the map ℛ (p. 17). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — the Frobenius action π on X^*(T̲) and on the Weyl groups
items.statement: There is a Frobenius action π on X^*(T̲) and an induced action on W̲ defined by π(w)(π(λ)) = π(w(λ)). Under the standard identification, π(λ)_{ṽ,i_ṽ} = λ_{ṽ,i_ṽ−1} for λ ∈ X^*(T̲), and similarly π(s)_{ṽ,i_ṽ} = s_{ṽ,i_ṽ−1} for s in any of the Weyl groups above.
items.note: Used in the congruences modulo (p − π)X⁰(T̲) defining Serre weights (F(λ) ≅ F(λ') iff λ − λ' ∈ (p−π)X⁰(T̲)) and in (2.4), Proposition 2.3.1. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — G̲^der, T̲^der, Λ̲_W, X⁰(T̲), ε_{1,i}, ε_{2,i}, and derived Weyl groups
items.statement: G̲₀^der := ∏_{ṽ∈S} Res_{k_ṽ/F_p} SL₃ with torus T̲₀^der; G̲^der := G̲₀^der ×_{F_p} F and T̲^der similarly. Λ̲_W := X^*(T̲^der) is the weight lattice of G̲^der, X⁰(T̲) the kernel of the restriction X^*(T̲) ↠ Λ̲_W, and ε_{1,i}, ε_{2,i} the images of ε'_{1,i}, ε'_{2,i}. The Weyl groups W̲^der, W̲_a^der, W̲̃^der, W̲̃^{der,+}, W̲̃₁^{der,+} for G̲^der (and W̃^{der,+}, W̃₁^{der,+} for G) are defined similarly, with analogous product decompositions.
items.note: Convention. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — the simple affine reflections α, β, γ⁺ of W_a (GL₃)
items.statement: α, β, γ⁺ denote the generators of the affine Weyl group W_a of GL₃ given by reflection over the walls of C₀, with α, β ∈ W and γ⁺ the affine reflection. They satisfy α(ε'₂) = ε'₂ and β(ε'₁) = ε'₁.
items.note: Hence α = (12) = s_{α₁}, β = (23) = s_{α₂}, and γ⁺ = t_{(1,0,−1)}(13) (reflection in the upper wall ⟨λ+η, α₀^∨⟩ = p of C₀ for the dot action; in the usual action, reflection in ⟨x, α₀^∨⟩ = 1). Checked: γ⁺αβα = t_{(1,0,−1)}. The symbol α is also used for roots elsewhere. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — S₃ ↪ GL₃(Z) by permutation matrices
items.statement: S₃ is the symmetric group on {1,2,3}; the injection S₃ ↪ GL₃(Z) sends s to the permutation matrix whose (k,m)-entry is δ_{k,s(m)} (Kronecker δ). The same letter s denotes the permutation matrix.
items.note: Thus s·e_m = e_{s(m)}, i.e. (s·x)_k = x_{s^{−1}(k)}. With this convention the list of W̃₁^{der,+} (p. 11), the relation (2.4) and Table 2 were checked for this reading. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — embedding X^*(T) ↪ GL₃(F((v))), λ ↦ v^λ, and W̃ ↪ GL₃(F((v))); ordered products
items.statement: X^*(T) ↪ GL₃(F((v))) by λ ↦ v^λ, where v^{(a,b,c)} is the diagonal matrix with entries v^a, v^b, v^c; together with the permutation matrices this gives an embedding W̃ ↪ GL₃(F((v))). For m ≥ 0 and square matrices (B_j)_{j=0,…,m} of the same size, ∏_{j=0}^m B_j := B₀·B₁·…·B_m.
items.note: Convention used for shapes of Kisin modules in §3. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: §1.4 — JH(V̄): Jordan–Hölder factors of the reduction of a lattice
items.statement: For a representation V of a finite group Γ over an E-vector space, JH(V̄) is the set of Jordan–Hölder factors of the mod ϖ reduction of an O-lattice in V. This set is independent of the choice of lattice.
items.note: Independence of the lattice is the Brauer–Nesbitt principle (cited as a known fact, not proved). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §1.4 — Irr(Spec R) = minimal primes
items.statement: For a ring R, Irr(Spec(R)) denotes the set of minimal primes of R.
items.note: Convention. Library: minimalPrimes at the pinned commits.

items.name: §2 — the finite group G := G̲₀(F_p)
items.statement: G := G̲₀(F_p) = ∏_{ṽ∈S} GL₃(k_ṽ).
items.note: Serre weights, Deligne–Lusztig representations R_s(μ), and Ext¹_G are all for this group. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.1 — the restricted alcoves C₀, C₁ and A = {C₀, C₁}^J ≅ {0,1}^J
items.statement: The surjection X^*(T) → Λ_W identifies the p-restricted alcoves of GL₃ and SL₃. C₀ and C₁ denote the p-restricted lower and upper alcoves of the weight space of GL₃, and A := {C₀, C₁}^J, naturally identified with the set of p-restricted alcoves for G̲ (or G̲^der). Alcoves are fundamental domains for the dot action, so the base alcove has a vertex at −η. One also writes 0 and 1 for C₀ and C₁, identifying A with {0,1}^J. C̲₀ ⊆ X(T̲) ⊗ R is the lowest alcove (C₀)_{i∈J}.
items.note: Convention. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.1 — W̲̃^der = Λ̲_W ⋊ W̲ acting by the p-dot action; W̲̃₁^{der,+}
items.statement: W̲̃^der = Λ̲_W ⋊ W̲ acts via the p-dot action on Λ̲_W ⊗ R. W̲̃₁^{der,+} ⊂ W̲̃^der is the set of elements taking C̲₀ to an element of A.
items.note: Per embedding, W̃₁^{der,+} has 6 elements (next item); W̲̃₁^{der,+} ≅ (W̃₁^{der,+})^J has 6^{#J}. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.1 — the six elements of W̃₁^{der,+} for SL₃
items.statement: W̃₁^{der,+} has exactly six elements: id, (12)t_{−(ε₁−ε₂)}, (23)t_{−(ε₂−ε₁)}, (123)t_{−ε₂}, (132)t_{−ε₁} and (13)t_{−(ε₁+ε₂)}.
items.note: Asserted without proof. Verified for this reading with the permutation convention (s·x)_k = x_{s^{−1}(k)}: id, (123)t_{−ε₂}, (132)t_{−ε₁} fix C₀ (they form the stabiliser Ω ≅ Z/3), and (12)t_{−(ε₁−ε₂)}, (23)t_{−(ε₂−ε₁)}, (13)t_{−(ε₁+ε₂)} = w̃_h send C₀ to C₁. Each coset of W_a^der in W̃^der (≅ Λ_W/Λ_R ≅ Z/3) contains exactly one element of each type. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.1 — the isomorphisms ι^der : Λ̲_W/Λ̲_R ≅ W̲̃^der/W̲_a^der and ι : X^*(T̲)/Λ̲_R ≅ W̲̃/W̲_a
items.statement: The inclusion Λ̲_W ↪ W̲̃^der (resp. X^*(T̲) ↪ W̲̃) induces an isomorphism ι^der : Λ̲_W/Λ̲_R ⥲ W̲̃^der/W̲_a^der (resp. ι : X^*(T̲)/Λ̲_R (≅ X^*(Z̲)) ⥲ W̲̃/W̲_a).
items.note: Standard from W̃ = X^*(T) ⋊ W, W_a = Λ_R ⋊ W. X^*(T̲)/Λ̲_R ≅ X^*(Z̲) via restriction to the centre. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.1 — the sets P^der ⊂ Λ̲_W × W̲̃₁^{der,+} and P ⊂ X^*(T̲) × W̲̃₁⁺
items.statement: P^der ⊂ Λ̲_W × W̲̃₁^{der,+} is the subset of pairs (ω, w̃) with ι^der(−π^{−1}(ω) + Λ̲_R) = w̃ W̲_a^der. P ⊂ X^*(T̲) × W̲̃₁⁺ is defined similarly (pairs (ω', w̃') with ι(−π^{−1}(ω') + Λ̲_R) = w̃' W̲_a). Restriction gives a natural surjection P ↠ P^der.
items.note: Key bookkeeping device for Tr_μ; π is the Frobenius of §1.4. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.1 — β : P^der → Λ̲_W × A is a bijection
items.statement: The map β : P^der → Λ̲_W × A, (ω, w̃) ↦ (ω, π(w̃)·C̲₀), is a bijection.
items.note: Proof: ι^der is a bijection and W̲_a^der acts simply transitively on the alcoves of G̲^der (so each coset w̃W̲_a^der contains exactly one element sending C̲₀ to each restricted alcove). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.1, (2.1) — the map P^der → X^*(T̲)/(p−π)X⁰(T̲) and 𝔗𝔯'_μ : Λ̲_W × A → X^*(T̲)/(p−π)X⁰(T̲)
items.statement: Let μ be an element of C̲₀/(p − π)X⁰(T̲) (the construction does not depend on the lift of μ to X^*(T̲)). Define P^der → X^*(T̲)/(p − π)X⁰(T̲), (ω, w̃) ↦ w̃'·(μ − η + ω'),   (2.1) where (ω', w̃') ∈ P is a lift of (ω, w̃); this does not depend on the choice of lift. 𝔗𝔯'_μ : Λ̲_W × A → X^*(T̲)/(p − π)X⁰(T̲) is the composite of β^{−1} with (2.1).
items.note: Independence of the lift asserted without proof; check: replacing ω' by ω' + z (z ∈ X⁰(T̲)) forces w̃' ↦ t_{−π^{−1}z}w̃', changing the value by z − pπ^{−1}z = −(p−π)π^{−1}z ∈ (p−π)X⁰(T̲). The formula makes sense for any μ ∈ X^*(T̲); later statements (Proposition 2.1.4) take μ ∈ X^*(T̲) arbitrary, and §2.3 uses μ with μ − η ∈ C̲₀. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Definition 2.1.2 — p-regular weights
items.statement: A weight λ ∈ X^*(T̲) is p-regular if ⟨λ + η, α^∨⟩ ∉ pZ for all positive coroots α^∨ ∈ R̲^{∨,+}. A p-regular element belongs to a unique alcove.
items.note: P-regular = not on any root hyperplane H_{α,n}; equivalently '0-deep in its alcove' (Definition 2.1.9 with n = 0; Remark 2.2.8). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.1 — Λ̲_W^μ and the translation map 𝔗𝔯_μ
items.statement: Λ̲_W^μ := {ω ∈ Λ̲_W : ω + μ − η ∈ C̲₀} (taking the image of μ − η in Λ̲_W). 𝔗𝔯_μ is the restriction of 𝔗𝔯'_μ to Λ̲_W^μ × A. Explicitly, for (ω, a) ∈ Λ̲_W^μ × A, 𝔗𝔯_μ(ω, a) = w̃'·(μ − η + ω') mod (p−π)X⁰(T̲), where (ω', w̃') ∈ P lifts β^{−1}(ω, a).
items.note: Λ̲_W^μ is the set of lattice points of a translate of a p-alcove (Remark 2.1.7); it is a product over J of per-embedding sets. The chart 𝔗𝔯_μ is the basic coordinate system on p-regular Serre weights of fixed central character. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 2.1.3(1) — 𝔗𝔯_μ(ω, a) is p-regular and lies in alcove π^{−1}(a)
items.statement: For (ω, a) ∈ Λ̲_W^μ × A, (any lift of) 𝔗𝔯_μ(ω, a) in X^*(T̲) is p-regular and lies in the alcove π^{−1}(a).
items.note: Proof: with (ω', w̃') ∈ P lifting β^{−1}(ω, a), μ − η + ω' is p-regular in C̲₀ by definition of Λ̲_W^μ, so w̃'·(μ − η + ω') is p-regular in w̃·C̲₀ = π^{−1}(a) (as β(ω, w̃) = (ω, π(w̃)·C̲₀)). Changes by (p−π)X⁰(T̲) do not affect pairings with coroots. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 2.1.3(2) — 𝔗𝔯_μ is injective
items.statement: The map 𝔗𝔯_μ : Λ̲_W^μ × A → X^*(T̲)/(p − π)X⁰(T̲) is injective.
items.note: Proof: if 𝔗𝔯_μ(ω, a) = 𝔗𝔯_μ(ν, b) with lifts (ω', w̃'), (ν', x̃') ∈ P, restricting to Z̲ and using the coset condition defining P gives (1 − pπ^{−1})(ω' − ν')|_Z̲ ∈ (1 − pπ^{−1})·3X^*(Z̲) (since X⁰(T̲)|_Z̲ = 3X^*(Z̲)), hence ω'|_Z̲ ≡ ν'|_Z̲ mod 3X^*(Z̲); with a = b (part (1)) and ι this gives w̃' ≡ x̃' mod X⁰(T̲), whence ω = ν. Steps checked for this reading. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 2.1.4 — image of 𝔗𝔯_μ: all p-regular restricted weights with the central character of μ − η
items.statement: Let μ ∈ X^*(T̲). Then 𝔗𝔯_μ(Λ̲_W^μ × A) = {λ ∈ X₁(T̲)/(p − π)X⁰(T̲) : λ is p-regular and (λ − μ + η)|_Z̲ ∈ (p − π)X^*(Z̲)}.   (2.2)
items.note: ⊆ from Proposition 2.1.3(1) and (λ − μ + η)|_Z̲ = (1 − pπ^{−1})ω'|_Z̲ = (p−π)(−π^{−1}ω')|_Z̲. ⊇: for λ in the right side take a ∋ π(λ), ω' with (λ − μ + η)|_Z̲ = (1 − pπ^{−1})ω'|_Z̲, ω its image, (ω', w̃') ∈ P over β^{−1}(ω, a), ν := λ − w̃'·(μ − η + ω') ∈ Λ̲_R; then (w'^{−1}(ν) + ω', w̃') ∈ P lifts β^{−1}(w'^{−1}(ν) + ω, a) and 𝔗𝔯_μ(w'^{−1}(ν) + ω, a) = λ. The proof leaves implicit that w'^{−1}(ν) + ω ∈ Λ̲_W^μ; this holds because λ ∈ π^{−1}(a) = w̃'·C̲₀ forces μ − η + ω' + w'^{−1}(ν) = w̃'^{−1}·λ ∈ C̲₀. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 2.1.5 — change of centre for the charts 𝔗𝔯 (chart overlap)
items.statement: Let λ − η be a lift of 𝔗𝔯_μ(ε, C̲₀) (with ε ∈ Λ̲_W^μ), and let β^{−1}(ε, C̲₀) = (ε, w̃). Then 𝔗𝔯_λ(ν, a) = 𝔗𝔯_μ(w^{−1}(ν) + ε, a) for all (ν, a) ∈ Λ̲_W^λ × A, where w ∈ W̲ is the image of w̃.
items.note: Proof: with lifts (ν', x̃') of β^{−1}(ν, a) and (ε', w̃') of (ε, w̃), 𝔗𝔯_λ(ν, a) = x̃'·(λ − η + ν') = x̃'·(w̃'·(μ − η + ε') + ν') = x̃'w̃'·(μ − η + ε' + w^{−1}(ν')) = 𝔗𝔯_μ(w^{−1}(ν) + ε, a). The last step uses (unstated) that w̃ stabilises C̲₀ (so x̃'w̃'·C̲₀ = x̃'·C̲₀ = π^{−1}(a)) and that x̃'w̃'W̲_a = t_{−π^{−1}(ν'+ε')}W̲_a with w^{−1}ν' ≡ ν' mod Λ̲_R; both checked. The proof works for any μ ∈ X^*(T̲) and any ε ∈ Λ̲_W^μ; λ − η then lies in C̲₀. The chart change (ν, a) ↦ (w^{−1}(ν) + ε, a) is affine with linear part in W̲. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.1 — Serre weights of G and the notation F(λ)
items.statement: A Serre weight is an irreducible F̄_p-representation of G. For λ ∈ X₁(T̲), F(λ) denotes the Serre weight obtained by restricting to G the irreducible algebraic representation of G̲ of highest weight λ.
items.note: Via the next item, F(λ) depends only on λ mod (p − π)X⁰(T̲); the paper writes F(𝔗𝔯_μ(ω, a)) for F of any lift. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: [Her09, Theorem 3.10] — classification of Serre weights of G by X₁(T̲)/(p − π)X⁰(T̲) (cited)
items.statement: Every Serre weight of G is obtained by restriction to G from an irreducible algebraic representation of G̲ of highest weight λ ∈ X₁(T̲), and λ ↦ F(λ) induces a bijection from X₁(T̲)/(p − π)X⁰(T̲) to the set of (isomorphism classes of) Serre weights of G.
items.locator: §2.1, published p. 13 (citing [Her09, Theorem 3.10]; cf. beginning of §4.2)
items.note: Cited, not proved. Printed 'a bijection between from X₁(T̲)/(p − π)X⁰(T̲) to the set of Serre weights' (new misprint). Underlying facts: Steinberg's restriction theorem and the description of characters of the centre Z̲₀(F_p) as X^*(Z̲)/(p − π)X^*(Z̲). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.1 — p-regular Serre weights
items.statement: A Serre weight F is p-regular if F ≅ F(λ) with λ ∈ X₁(T̲) p-regular (Definition 2.1.2).
items.note: Equivalently 0-deep (Definition 2.1.9). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.1 — F(𝔗𝔯_μ(−)) is a bijection from Λ̲_W^μ × A onto the p-regular Serre weights with central character of F(μ − η)
items.statement: Given μ ∈ C̲₀ and (ω, a) ∈ Λ̲_W^μ × A, F(𝔗𝔯_μ(ω, a)) is a p-regular Serre weight, and F(𝔗𝔯_μ(−)) induces a bijection between Λ̲_W^μ × A and the set of p-regular Serre weights of G with the same central character as F(μ − η).
items.note: Consequence of Propositions 2.1.3(2) and 2.1.4 together with [Her09, Theorem 3.10]: the central character of F(λ) is λ|_Z̲ mod (p−π)X^*(Z̲). The argument works for every μ ∈ X^*(T̲) ('central character of F(μ − η)' meaning (μ − η)|_Z̲ mod (p−π)X^*(Z̲)); the paper's standing lowest-alcove convention elsewhere is μ − η ∈ C̲₀ (see the issue on 'μ ∈ C̲₀' in §2.1). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Definition 2.1.6 (first part) — adjacency in Λ̲_W^μ × A
items.statement: (ω, a) and (ν, b) in Λ̲_W^μ × A are adjacent if there exists j ∈ J such that a_i = b_i and ω_i = ν_i for all i ∈ J with i ≠ j, a_j ≠ b_j, and ω_j − ν_j ∈ {0, ±(ε_{1,j} − ε_{2,j}), ±ε_{1,j}, ±ε_{2,j}}.   (2.3)
items.note: The checkpoint's statement paraphrased Definition 2.1.6 together with Remark 2.1.7 and used 'Lambda_W × {0,1}^J' coordinates — now split. The nonzero elements of the set in (2.3) are the six W-conjugates of the fundamental weights ε₁ = [1,0,0], ε₂ = [1,1,0] (W-invariant set). The resulting graph on Λ̲_W^μ × A is the Cartesian product over j ∈ J of the per-embedding graphs. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: Translation-map construction and overlap proofs are explicit remaining gaps G01; the graph must not be defined by Ext, whose comparison is a theorem.

api.name: adj_chart_independent
api.statement: The relation is invariant under Lemma 2.1.5 chart changes.

api.name: adj_one_embedding
api.statement: Adjacent vertices differ in exactly one component.

unitTests: The labels (0,0) and (0,1) are adjacent.
The displacement epsilon1+epsilon2 is not an edge.
Changing labels at two embeddings is not one edge.

items.name: Definition 2.1.6 (second part) — adjacent p-regular Serre weights
items.statement: p-regular Serre weights F and F' are adjacent if one can write F = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(ω, a)) and F' = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(ν, b)) for some p-regular μ ∈ C̲₀/(p − π)X⁰(T̲) and some (ω, a), (ν, b) ∈ Λ̲_W^μ × A which are adjacent in Λ̲_W^μ × A.
items.note: Adjacent weights necessarily have the same central character. 'p-regular μ ∈ C̲₀' is redundant as printed (C̲₀ is open); see the issue on the μ ∈ C̲₀ vs μ − η ∈ C̲₀ convention. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.1 — adjacency of Serre weights does not depend on the chart centre μ
items.statement: Adjacency of p-regular Serre weights (Definition 2.1.6) does not depend on the choice of the lowest alcove weight μ. Precisely: if F = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(ω, a)), F' = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(ν, b)) are adjacent p-regular Serre weights and λ is such that F(λ − η) and F(μ − η) have the same central character, then F(𝔗𝔯_λ(w(ω − ε), a)) = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(ω, a)) and F(𝔗𝔯_λ(w(ν − ε), b)) = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(ν, b)) for some w ∈ W̲ and ε ∈ Λ̲_W, and (w(ω − ε), a), (w(ν − ε), b) are again adjacent since the set in (2.3) is W̲-invariant.
items.note: Proof by Proposition 2.1.5. The paper takes 'λ ∈ C̲₀'; Proposition 2.1.5 needs λ − η to be a lift of some 𝔗𝔯_μ(ε, C̲₀), i.e. λ − η ∈ C̲₀ (recorded as a misprint). For arbitrary λ the claim still follows by composing two chart changes of Proposition 2.1.5 through an intermediate centre. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Remark 2.1.7 — geometric description of adjacency
items.statement: Geometrically, Λ̲_W^μ is the intersection of Λ̲_W with a translate of a p-alcove, and two pairs (ω, a) and (ν, b) are adjacent if and only if ω and ν are either equal or neighbours (that is, differ by a W̲-conjugate of a fundamental weight) and either ω ≠ ν and a and b have different labels in the unique component where ω and ν differ, or ω = ν and a and b differ in exactly one component.
items.note: Restatement of Definition 2.1.6, read with the implicit conventions that 'neighbours' means ω_j − ν_j is a W-conjugate of a fundamental weight in a single component j, and that in the first case a and b agree outside j. The remark's final sentence ('there are 7^{#J} adjacent vertices') is wrong; the correct count 7·#J is item T64 (issue E15). In each component the lattice points of the translated alcove form a triangular region whose sides are parallel to ε₂, ε₁, ε₁ − ε₂ (walls for α₁, α₂, α₀). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Remark 2.1.7 (corrected) — interior degree of the extension graph is 7·#J
items.statement: Let (ω, a) ∈ Λ̲_W^μ × A be such that all its neighbours ω + δ (δ ∈ {±ε_{1,j}, ±ε_{2,j}, ±(ε_{1,j} − ε_{2,j})}, j ∈ J) lie in Λ̲_W^μ. Then the vertices adjacent to (ω, a) are in bijection with J × {0, ±ε₁, ±ε₂, ±(ε₁ − ε₂)}, via (j, δ) ↦ (ω + δ_j, a with a_j flipped); hence (ω, a) has exactly 7·#J adjacent vertices.
items.locator: §2.1, Remark 2.1.7, published p. 14; arXiv v4 p. 12 (corrected statement; see E15)
items.note: Existing id kept (statement made exact). Immediate from Definition 2.1.6: an adjacent vertex changes exactly one component j, flips a_j (A_j = {0,1}), and moves ω_j by one of 7 displacements. The paper prints 7^{#J}. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: A neighbor has a unique changed alcove label, determining j. Its coordinate displacement determines one of seven distinct values. Conversely each such pair changes that coordinate and flips its label, giving a neighbor. These maps are inverse. The zero displacement still flips one label; simultaneous flips in several embeddings are not edges.

items.name: §2.1 — the graph on Λ̲_W^μ × A is connected; induced metric on p-regular Serre weights of fixed central character, independent of μ
items.statement: Definition 2.1.6 endows Λ̲_W^μ × A with a graph structure (edges = adjacency). This graph is connected and hence carries a path metric. By Proposition 2.1.4, any μ ∈ C̲₀ thus endows the set of p-regular Serre weights with the same central character as F(μ − η) with a metric, and by Proposition 2.1.5 this metric is independent of the choice of μ.
items.note: Connectedness is asserted 'by the above description': each per-embedding factor is the set of lattice points in an alcove translate (a connected triangular grid under the six steps of (2.3)), each step flips the label, and the label can be flipped without moving ω; the graph is the Cartesian product over J. Consequently (not stated) d_gph is the sum of the per-embedding distances. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Definition 2.1.8 — graph distance d_gph
items.statement: Given p-regular Serre weights F, F' with the same central character, d_gph(F, F') denotes their distance (for the metric induced by the adjacency graph). In particular, F and F' are adjacent if and only if d_gph(F, F') = 1.
items.note: The checkpoint's statement added that 'on a product of embedding graphs this distance is the sum of component distances' — true (the graph is the Cartesian product over J of per-embedding graphs) but not stated in the paper; it is implicit in later formulas such as ℓℓ(R̄^σ) = 2Def_R(σ) + 3(f − Def_R(σ)) + 1 (Theorem 4.1.9). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: Prove connectivity before exporting an N-valued metric; an arbitrary graph distance can be infinite.

api.name: distance_edge
api.statement: Distance one is adjacency.

api.name: distance_product
api.statement: Cartesian-product distance is the sum.

unitTests: A vertex has distance zero from itself.
Distinct central-character components are not assigned finite distance.
Two independent single-coordinate edges have product distance two.

items.name: Definition 2.1.9 — λ lies n-deep in its alcove
items.statement: Let λ ∈ X^*(T) be a weight. λ lies n-deep in its alcove if for all α^∨ ∈ R^{∨,+} there exist integers m_α ∈ Z such that p m_α + n < ⟨λ + η, α^∨⟩ < p(m_α + 1) − n. The analogous definition applies to weights in X^*(T̲) (all α^∨ ∈ R̲^{∨,+}).
items.note: The checkpoint's statement added 'Fix p>3, X*(T)=(Z^3)^J, η=(2,1,0)^J' and paraphrased. 0-deep = p-regular. The p-dot action of W̲̃ preserves 'n-deep in its alcove' (it permutes alcoves and walls isometrically), which is used e.g. in Corollary 2.3.13. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: Keep all positive coroots, strict inequalities, and embedding coordinates; affine p-dot translations are by p times a weight.

api.name: depth_affine_invariant
api.statement: An affine p-dot action preserves n-depth.

api.name: depth_mono
api.statement: n-depth implies m-depth for 0≤m≤n.

unitTests: A weight on a strip endpoint is not 0-deep.
For p=101 the triple (40,20,0) is 13-deep in C0 after adding eta.
Translation by p times a root preserves depth while crossing into another alcove.

items.name: §2.1 — n-deep in the base alcove C̲₀
items.statement: A dominant weight λ ∈ X^*(T̲) lies n-deep in alcove C̲₀ if n < ⟨λ + η, α^∨⟩ < p − n for all positive coroots α^∨ ∈ R̲^{∨,+}.
items.note: Printed with a dangling 'for all i = 0, …, f − 1' (no i appears; leftover from arXiv v1 where the condition read ⟨λ_i + η_i, α_i⟩) — recorded as a misprint. Here 'if' is used in the sense of 'iff'. For GL₃ in one embedding with λ + η = (a,b,c): n < a − b, b − c and a − c < p − n. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.1 — n-deep Serre weights
items.statement: A Serre weight F is n-deep if F ≅ F(μ) for some μ ∈ X₁(T̲) which is n-deep (in its alcove).
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.1 — the extension graph
items.statement: The extension graph is the graph on the set of p-regular Serre weights (of G) whose edges join adjacent weights (Definition 2.1.6); it is a disjoint union over central characters, each component carrying the metric d_gph.
items.note: Justified by Theorem 2.1.10. Each connected component (fixed central character) is identified with Λ̲_W^μ × A via F(𝔗𝔯_μ(−)). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Theorem 2.1.10 — Ext¹ between generic Serre weights is nonzero exactly for adjacent weights
items.statement: Let F, F' be Serre weights which are both 6-deep. Then Ext¹_G(F, F') ≠ 0 if and only if F and F' are adjacent.
items.note: Proof: this is Lemma 4.2.6 (§4.2), whose proof uses only modular representation theory and no results from other sections. G = G̲₀(F_p). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Remark 2.1.11 — the extension graph is bipartite
items.statement: Partition the vertices (ω, a) of Λ̲_W^μ × A into two sets according to the class of Σ_i a_i mod 2 (interpreting a_i ∈ {0,1}). This makes the extension graph bipartite.
items.note: The checkpoint's statement added the consequence 'an edge changes distance from a fixed vertex by ±1' and cited Proposition 4.3.16 — that consequence is standard (triangle inequality gives |d(x,y) − d(x,y')| ≤ 1 for adjacent y, y', bipartiteness excludes 0) but is not part of the remark. Proof: adjacent vertices differ in exactly one label a_j, so Σ a_i changes parity. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: Each edge flips precisely one label. Triangle inequalities bound the change by one.

items.name: §2.2 — (tame) inertial types for K = F_ṽ and their reductions τ̄
items.statement: Suppose S = {ṽ} and K = F_ṽ. An inertial type is a representation τ : I_K → GL₃(E) with open kernel which extends to the Weil group of K. It is tame if it factors through the tame inertial quotient. All tame inertial types are defined over O, and τ̄ : I_K → GL₃(F) denotes the reduction to the residue field.
items.note: Planned: LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 plans fixed labeled Hodge-type and inertial-type potentially semistable deformation rings in every rank, with bounded-height lattice moduli and minimally ramified conditions; LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3 plans Kisin's potentially semistable deformation rings with fixed Hodge and inertial type and their dimension.

items.name: §2.2, (2.4) — the action of X^*(T̲) ⋊ W̲ on pairs (w, μ) and the equivalence ∼
items.statement: For (w, μ) ∈ W̲ × X^*(T̲) and (ν, σ) ∈ X^*(T̲) ⋊ W̲ define ^{(ν,σ)}(w, μ) := (σ w π(σ)^{−1}, σ(μ) + pν − σ w π(σ)^{−1} π(ν)),   (2.4) and write (w, μ) ∼ (w', μ') if there is (ν, σ) with ^{(ν,σ)}(w, μ) = (w', μ').
items.locator: §2.2, (2.4), published p. 15 (following [Her09, (4.1)] and the paragraph preceding [GHS18, Definition 10.1.12])
items.note: Π is the Frobenius of §1.4. Checked for this reading: with σ = 1, replacing μ by μ + pν − wπ(ν) leaves the exponents in (2.5) unchanged mod p^{f'} − 1 (using (s·x)_k = x_{s^{−1}(k)}). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Definition 2.2.1 — the tame inertial type τ(w, μ)
items.statement: Define τ(w, μ) : I_K → GL₃(O) as follows. If w = (s₀, …, s_{f−1}), set s_τ := s₀ s_{f−1} s_{f−2} ⋯ s₁ ∈ W and let 𝛂 ∈ X^*(T̲) be given by 𝛂₀ = μ₀ and 𝛂_j = s₁^{−1} s₂^{−1} ⋯ s_j^{−1}(μ_j) for 1 ≤ j ≤ f − 1. Let r be the order of s_τ and f' := f r. Then τ(w, μ) := ⊕_{1≤i≤3} ω_{f'}^{Σ_{0≤k≤r−1} 𝐚^{(0)}_{s_τ^k(i)} p^{fk}},   (2.5) where 𝐚^{(0)} := Σ_{j=0}^{f−1} 𝛂_j p^j ∈ Z³.
items.note: Ω_{f'} is the (Teichmüller) fundamental character of niveau f' (§1.4), a character of I_K. Cf. [Her09, (6.15)], [GHS18, Definition 8.2.2]. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: §2.2 — normal form (w, μ) ∼ ((s_τ, 1, …, 1), 𝛂)
items.statement: In Definition 2.2.1, (w, μ) ∼ ((s_τ, 1, …, 1), 𝛂) and τ(w, μ) ≅ τ((s_τ, 1, …, 1), 𝛂) by construction.
items.note: Checked for this reading: take ν = 0 and σ_j = s₁^{−1}⋯s_j^{−1} (σ₀ = 1) in (2.4); then σ_j s_j σ_{j−1}^{−1} = 1 for j ≥ 1, the 0-th component is s₀ σ_{f−1}^{−1} = s_τ, and σ(μ) = 𝛂. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: §2.2 — every tame inertial type for K is some τ(w, μ) (cited)
items.statement: Every tame inertial type τ : I_K → GL₃(E) is isomorphic to τ(w, μ) for some (w, μ) ∈ W̲ × X^*(T̲) (Definition 2.2.1 'describes all isomorphism classes of tame inertial types for K').
items.note: Cited, not proved. The paper does not state explicitly that τ(w, μ) ≅ τ(w', μ') iff (w, μ) ∼ (w', μ'); only the 'if' direction is recorded ('by construction'). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Definition 2.2.2(1) — regular tame inertial types
items.statement: A tame inertial type τ is regular if the characters appearing on the right-hand side of (2.5) are pairwise distinct.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Definition 2.2.2(2) — n-generic tame inertial types
items.statement: A tame inertial type τ is n-generic if τ ≅ τ(s, λ + η) for some s ∈ W̲ and some λ ∈ X^*_+(T̲) which is n-deep in alcove C̲₀.
items.note: Differs slightly from [LLHLM18, Definition 2.1] and by a shift by η from [GHS18, Definition 10.1.12] (Remark 2.2.3). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Definition 2.2.2(3) — n-generic ρ̄
items.statement: ρ̄ : G_K → GL₃(F) is n-generic if ρ̄^{ss}|_{I_K} ≅ τ̄ for a tame inertial type τ which is n-generic.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Definition 2.2.2(4) — lowest alcove presentation of a tame inertial type
items.statement: A lowest alcove presentation of τ is a pair (s, μ) ∈ W̲ × X^*(T̲) with μ ∈ C̲₀ such that τ ≅ τ(s, μ + η). Such a presentation exists exactly when τ is 0-generic (by definition).
items.note: Note the shift: a lowest alcove presentation has μ ∈ C̲₀ and type τ(s, μ + η), whereas for Deligne–Lusztig representations R_s(μ) the lowest-alcove condition is μ − η ∈ C̲₀ (Definition 2.2.5). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark 2.2.3 — comparison of genericity notions
items.statement: The notion of genericity in [LLHLM18, Definition 2.1] is slightly different from Definition 2.2.2(2); in particular, an inertial type which is n-generic in the sense of Definition 2.2.2(2) is a fortiori n-generic in the sense of [LLHLM18]. The notion of genericity differs from that of [GHS18, Definition 10.1.12] by a shift by η.
items.note: Needed to import results of [LLHLM18] under the present hypotheses; stated without proof. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark 2.2.4 — 1-generic types are regular
items.statement: If τ is 1-generic, then τ is regular.
items.note: Stated without proof. Sketch (checked in the case s_τ = 1): the exponents differ by Σ_j d_j p^j with 2 ≤ |d_j| ≤ p − 2 not all zero, which cannot vanish modulo p^f − 1. 0-generic does not suffice (e.g. f = 1, s = 1, a − c = p − 1). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: §2.2 — collections τ_S(s, μ); regular and n-generic collections; n-generic ρ̄_S
items.statement: For arbitrary finite S, s ∈ W̲ and μ ∈ X^*(T̲), define s_ṽ and μ_ṽ in the evident way and set τ_S(s, μ) := (τ_ṽ(s_ṽ, μ_ṽ))_{ṽ∈S}. The notions regular and n-generic extend in the evident way to collections of tame inertial types, and there is an evident notion of n-generic for a collection ρ̄_S of Galois representations ρ̄_ṽ : G_{F_ṽ} → GL₃(F), ṽ ∈ S.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: §2.2 — good pairs (s, μ) and the Deligne–Lusztig representation R_s(μ) of G
items.statement: Let (s, μ) ∈ W̲ × X^*(T̲) be a good pair in the sense of [LLHL19, Section 2.2]. Following [GHS18, Propositions 9.2.1 and 9.2.2], one attaches to (s, μ) a genuine Deligne–Lusztig representation R_s(μ) of G = G̲₀(F_p) defined over E (E sufficiently large). R_s(μ) is denoted R(s, μ) in [GHS18]. By inflation R_s(μ) is also regarded as a smooth ∏_{ṽ∈S} GL₃(O_{F_ṽ})-representation.
items.note: Cited construction (the context is slightly more general than [LLHL19, §2.2] since #S may exceed one). 'Genuine' = an actual representation (±R_T^G(θ) with the right sign). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Definition 2.2.5 — n-generic Deligne–Lusztig representations
items.statement: Let (s, μ) ∈ W̲ × X^*(T̲) be a good pair and n ≥ 0. R_s(μ) is n-generic if there is an isomorphism R_s(μ) ≅ R_{s'}(μ') with μ' − η n-deep in alcove C̲₀ (then (s', μ') is good, by the evident generalisation of [LLHL19, Lemma 2.2.3]).
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.2 — τ_S(s, μ) is n-generic iff R_s(μ) is n-generic (cited)
items.statement: For a good pair (s, μ) and n ≥ 0, τ_S(s, μ) is n-generic (Definition 2.2.2(2)) if and only if R_s(μ) is n-generic (Definition 2.2.5).
items.note: Cited from [GHS18, Proposition 9.2.1] and the evident generalisation of [LLHL19, Proposition 2.2.4]; not proved here. (Also cited: the evident generalisation of [LLHL19, Lemma 2.2.3], that (s', μ') in Definition 2.2.5 is good.) Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.2 — the K-types σ(τ_ṽ) (inertial local Langlands) and σ(τ_S)
items.statement: σ(τ_ṽ) is a smooth GL₃(O_{F_ṽ})-representation associated with τ_ṽ as in [CEG+16, Theorem 3.7], and σ(τ_S) := ⊗_{ṽ∈S} σ(τ_ṽ), a ∏_{ṽ∈S} GL₃(O_{F_ṽ})-representation.
items.note: Cited construction (inertial local Langlands / K-types). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Proposition 2.2.6(1) — generic R_s(μ) is irreducible (cited from [DL76, Theorem 6.8])
items.statement: Let (s, μ) be a good pair with μ − η ∈ X^*(T̲) 1-deep in alcove C̲₀. Then R_s(μ) is irreducible.
items.note: Cited from [DL76, Theorem 6.8] (R_T^G(θ) is irreducible up to sign for θ in general position); 1-deep ensures general position. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 2.2.6(2) — σ(τ_S) can be taken to be R_s(μ) (cited from [LLHL19, Corollary 2.3.5])
items.statement: Let (s, μ) be a good pair with μ − η ∈ X^*(T̲) 1-deep in alcove C̲₀, and let τ_S = τ_S(s, μ). Then σ(τ_S) can be taken to be R_s(μ) (inflated to ∏_{ṽ∈S} GL₃(O_{F_ṽ})).
items.note: Cited from [LLHL19, Corollary 2.3.5]. The printed statement does not name τ_S; that τ_S = τ_S(s, μ) is implicit from context. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.2 — the representations V(τ̄_ṽ) and V(τ̄_S) of [GHS18]
items.statement: Let τ̄_S be a collection of tame representations τ̄_ṽ : I_{F_ṽ} → GL₃(F) which extend to G_{F_ṽ}. By [GHS18, Proposition 9.2.1] one attaches to τ̄_ṽ an E-valued representation V(τ̄_ṽ) of GL₃(k_ṽ), and V(τ̄_S) := ⊗_{ṽ∈S} V(τ̄_ṽ) is a G-representation. ρ̄_S|_{I_{F_S}} denotes the collection of restrictions to inertia of ρ̄_S.
items.note: Cited construction. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: [GHS18, Proposition 9.2.3] — V(τ̄_S(s, μ)) ≅ R_s(μ) (cited)
items.statement: If τ̄_S = τ̄_S(s, μ) for a good pair (s, μ), then V(τ̄_S) ≅ R_s(μ).
items.note: Cited, not proved. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.2 — the self-bijection ℛ of p-regular Serre weights
items.statement: With w̃_h := w₀ t_{−η} ∈ W̲̃, ℛ is the self-bijection of the set of p-regular Serre weights defined in [GHS18, Section 9.2] by ℛ(F(λ)) := F(w̃_h · λ).
items.note: For λ ∈ X₁(T̲) p-regular, w̃_h·λ ∈ X₁(T̲) is p-regular (w̃_h swaps C₀ and C₁ in each embedding), and w̃_h·(λ + z) = w̃_h·λ + z for z ∈ X⁰(T̲), so ℛ is well defined. ℛ is not an involution: ℛ² is twisting by det^{−2} (w̃_h² = t_{−(2,2,2)}); t_{1̲}∘ℛ is an involution (used in Proposition 2.3.5). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Definition 2.2.7 — the set W^?(ρ̄_S) of predicted Serre weights ([GHS18, Definition 9.2.5])
items.statement: Let ρ̄_S be a collection of 2-generic semisimple Galois representations ρ̄_ṽ : G_{F_ṽ} → GL₃(F). The set of predicted weights for ρ̄_S is W^?(ρ̄_S) := {ℛ(F) : F ∈ JH(V̄(ρ̄_S|_{I_{F_S}}))}.
items.note: Herzig's set; cited definition. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Definition 2.2.7 (continued) — W^?(ρ̄_S, τ_S)
items.statement: If τ_S is a collection of tame inertial types τ_ṽ : I_{F_ṽ} → GL₃(O), W^?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) := W^?(ρ̄_S) ∩ JH(σ̄(τ_S)).
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark 2.2.8 — why 2-genericity: JH(V̄(ρ̄_S|_I)) consists of 0-deep weights
items.statement: The condition that ρ̄_S|_{I_{F_S}} is 2-generic ensures that the elements of JH(V̄(ρ̄_S|_{I_{F_S}})) are all 0-deep, so that ℛ is defined on them (cf. Lemma 4.2.13).
items.note: Proof deferred to Lemma 4.2.13. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: §2.2 — obvious Serre weights W_obv(ρ̄) ([GHS18, Definition 7.1.3])
items.statement: There is a subset W_obv(ρ̄) ⊆ W^?(ρ̄) of obvious Serre weights of ρ̄ ([GHS18, Definition 7.1.3]); W_obv(ρ̄_S) is defined in the evident way (componentwise).
items.note: Cited definition; described explicitly in extension-graph coordinates by Proposition 2.3.1 (6^{#J} weights, the vertices r(Σ₀^obv)^J). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: §2.3 — standing assumption: ρ̄_ṽ 2-generic and semisimple
items.statement: Throughout §2.3, ρ̄_ṽ is assumed 2-generic and semisimple for all ṽ ∈ S.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 2.3.1 — obvious weights in extension-graph coordinates
items.statement: Let ρ̄_S be a collection of semisimple Galois representations with ρ̄_S|_{I_{F_S}} ≅ τ̄_S(s, λ), where λ − η is 3-deep in C̲₀. Then W_obv(ρ̄_S) = {F(𝔗𝔯_λ(s(ω), π(w̃)·C̲₀)) : w̃ = w t_{−π^{−1}ω} ∈ W̲̃₁^{+,der}}.
items.note: Proof: 'follows from [LLHL19, Corollary 2.2.13 and (2.6)]' — (2.6) there refers to [LLHL19], not to this paper's (2.6) (p. 20). In each embedding the six elements of W̃₁^{der,+} give (ω_j, alcove) ∈ {(0,C₀), (ε₁,C₀), (ε₂,C₀), (ε₁−ε₂,C₁), (ε₂−ε₁,C₁), (ε₁+ε₂,C₁)} = r(Σ₀^obv) (checked), consistent with Proposition 2.3.4 and Definition 2.3.8. W̲̃₁^{+,der} is the set written W̲̃₁^{der,+} in §2.1. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Definition 2.3.2 — the nine-point set Σ₀ ⊂ Λ_W × A and Σ = Σ₀^J
items.note: Existing id kept (was located at Definition 2.3.3 and bundled Σ₀^obv/Σ₀^inn and r; those are now separate items). Figure 1 draws Σ₀ as the triangle with vertices (ε₁+ε₂, C₀) (top), (ε₁−ε₂, C₀), (ε₂−ε₁, C₀) and edge midpoints ε₁, ε₂, 0 each carrying both labels C₀, C₁ (checked: ε₁, ε₂, 0 are the midpoints). W^?(ρ̄_S) and JH(R̄_s(μ)) are described in terms of Σ. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: Use the actual finite coordinate set; compare it with constituents by Proposition 2.3.5, not by definition.

api.name: sigma_card
api.statement: One factor has nine vertices; the J-product has 9^|J|.

api.name: sigma_partition
api.statement: Inner and obvious vertices are disjoint and exhaust Sigma.

unitTests: One factor has six obvious and three inner points.
The induced graph has 15 edges.
For two factors there are 81 vertices.

items.name: Figure 1 — the triangle Σ₀ inside Λ_W × {C₀, C₁}
items.statement: Figure 1 depicts Σ₀ as a triangle in Λ_W with vertices labelled (ε₁+ε₂, C₀), (ε₁−ε₂, C₀), (ε₂−ε₁, C₀) and edge midpoints labelled {(ε₁, C₀), (ε₁, C₁)} (between ε₁+ε₂ and ε₁−ε₂), {(ε₂, C₀), (ε₂, C₁)} (between ε₁+ε₂ and ε₂−ε₁) and {(0, C₀), (0, C₁)} (between ε₁−ε₂ and ε₂−ε₁).
items.note: Used 'to directly compute' the sets Σ_w̃ (p. 22). Consistent with Definition 2.3.2 (checked). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Definition 2.3.3 — obvious and inner parts Σ₀^obv, Σ₀^inn; obvious/inner in component i
items.statement: Σ₀^obv := {(ε₁+ε₂, 0), (ε₁−ε₂, 0), (ε₂−ε₁, 0), (0, 1), (ε₁, 1), (ε₂, 1)} and Σ₀^inn := Σ₀ ∖ Σ₀^obv = {(0, 0), (ε₁, 0), (ε₂, 0)}. (ω, a) ∈ Σ is obvious (resp. inner) in component i if (ω_i, a_i) ∈ Σ₀^obv (resp. (ω_i, a_i) ∈ Σ₀^inn).
items.note: In Figure 1: Σ₀^inn = the three edge midpoints with the lower label C₀; Σ₀^obv = the three vertices (label C₀) and the three midpoints with the upper label C₁. Σ₀^inn and Σ₀^obv are stable under the rotation symmetry (conjugation by Ω ≅ Z/3) of Σ₀. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.3 — the involution r (flip all alcove labels)
items.statement: r is the involution of Λ̲_W^μ × A defined by r(ω, a) := (ω, a') with a'_i ≠ a_i for all i ∈ J.
items.note: R preserves adjacency (Definition 2.1.6) and commutes with the usual action of W̲̃ on the first factor. Relation with ℛ: t_{1̲}∘ℛ∘𝔗𝔯_μ = 𝔗𝔯_μ∘r (next items). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 2.3.4 — W^?(ρ̄_S) = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(t_ν s r(Σ)))
items.statement: Let μ ∈ X^*(T̲). Suppose that V(ρ̄_S|_{I_{F_S}}) = R_s(μ + ν) where ν ∈ Λ̲_R and μ + ν − η is 3-deep in alcove C̲₀. Then W^?(ρ̄_S) = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(t_ν s r(Σ))), where t_ν s acts on Λ̲_W × A through the first factor by the usual action: t_ν s(ω, a) = (s(ω) + ν, a).
items.note: Proof: Proposition 2.3.1 gives W_obv(ρ̄_S) = {F(𝔗𝔯_{μ+ν}(s(ω), π(w̃)·C̲₀))}, and 𝔗𝔯_{μ+ν}(s(ω), ·) = 𝔗𝔯_μ(s(ω) + ν, ·) since ν ∈ Λ̲_R (checked: the same w̃' serves both). By the generalised Jantzen formula [Her09, Appendix, Theorem 3.4] and 3-deepness, W^?(ρ̄_S) is given by [GHS18, Proposition 10.1.8]: F({𝔗𝔯_μ(t_ν s(ω), a) | w̃ = w t_{−π^{−1}ω} ∈ W̲̃₁^{+,der}, π(w̃)·C̲₀ ↑ a}), which equals F(𝔗𝔯_μ(t_ν s r(Σ))) (checked: per embedding, the 6 obvious pairs together with the upward alcove relation C₀ ↑ C₁ give exactly r(Σ₀)). ↑ is Jantzen's linkage order on alcoves (not defined in the paper). The step from V(ρ̄_S|_I) = R_s(μ+ν) to ρ̄_S|_I ≅ τ̄_S(s, μ+ν) (needed for Proposition 2.3.1) is tacit ([GHS18, Proposition 9.2.3]). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: [Her09, Appendix, Theorem 3.4] — generalised Jantzen formula for reductions of Deligne–Lusztig representations (cited)
items.statement: The mod p reduction (semisimplification) of the Deligne–Lusztig representation R_s(μ + ν) of G is given explicitly in terms of reductions of Weyl modules (restricted to G).
items.note: Cited black box (Jantzen's formula generalised in the appendix of [Her09]); combined with 3-deepness it yields the 'generic pattern' decomposition used in Propositions 2.3.4–2.3.5. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: [GHS18, Proposition 10.1.8] — W^? as the set of weights obtained from obvious weights by moving up in alcoves (cited)
items.statement: For ρ̄_S as in Proposition 2.3.4 (generic), W^?(ρ̄_S) = F({𝔗𝔯_μ(t_ν s(ω), a) | w̃ = w t_{−π^{−1}ω} ∈ W̲̃₁^{+,der}, π(w̃)·C̲₀ ↑ a}).
items.note: Cited black box, stated here in the paper's coordinates. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.3 — compatibility t_{1̲}∘ℛ∘𝔗𝔯_μ = 𝔗𝔯_μ∘r
items.statement: t_{1̲} ∘ ℛ ∘ 𝔗𝔯_μ = 𝔗𝔯_μ ∘ r on Λ̲_W^μ × A, where 1̲ = (1,1,1)_{i∈J} ∈ X⁰(T̲) and t_{1̲} acts by the dot action (translation by p·1̲ ≡ 1̲ modulo (p − π)X⁰(T̲), i.e. twist by det).
items.note: Asserted without proof ('Since …'). Checked for this reading: v := w₀t_{−η+1̲} ∈ W̲_a is an involution sending C₀ ↔ C₁ in each embedding; if (ω', w̃') lifts β^{−1}(ω, a) then (ω', v w̃') lifts β^{−1}(r(ω, a)), and v·x = w̃_h·x + p·1̲. Consequently t_{1̲}∘ℛ is an involution although ℛ² = t_{−2·1̲}. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 2.3.5 — Jordan–Hölder factors of generic R̄_s(μ + ν): JH(R̄_s(μ + ν)) = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(t_ν s(Σ)))
items.statement: If ν ∈ X^*(T̲) is such that ν + η ∈ Λ̲_R and μ + ν − η is 3-deep in alcove C̲₀, then JH(R̄_s(μ + ν)) = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(t_ν s(Σ))).
items.note: Proof: by t_{1̲}∘ℛ∘𝔗𝔯_μ = 𝔗𝔯_μ∘r, F(𝔗𝔯_μ(ω, a)) ∈ JH(R̄_s(λ − 1̲)) iff F(𝔗𝔯_μ(r(ω, a))) ∈ ℛ(JH(R̄_s(λ))) = W^?(ρ̄_S) where V(ρ̄|_{I_{F_S}}) = R_s(λ); then apply Proposition 2.3.4. The proof leaves implicit the choice λ := μ + ν + 1̲ (so λ − 1̲ = μ + ν) and the check ν + 1̲ = (ν + η) − (η − 1̲) ∈ Λ̲_R, together with R_s(λ − 1̲) ⊗ det ≅ R_s(λ) and that t_{ν+1̲} and t_ν act identically on Λ̲_W. Consequence: #JH(R̄_s(μ+ν)) = 9^{#J} and R̄ is multiplicity free (used in §4). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Definition 2.3.6 — R_w̃(μ) for w̃ ∈ W̲̃
items.statement: For w̃ ∈ W̲̃, R_w̃(μ) := R_w(μ + w̃(0)), where w ∈ W̲ is the projection of w̃ and w̃(0) is computed with the usual (non-dot) action.
items.note: So R_{t_κ w}(μ) = R_w(μ + κ). Used e.g. in Proposition 3.4.1 (V(T*_dd(M)|_{I_K}) = R_{s w̃*}(μ + η)). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.3 — the usual action of W̲̃ on Λ̲_W × A
items.statement: W̲̃ acts on Λ̲_W × A through W̲̃^der on the first factor only, via the usual action (not the dot action): t_κ w (ω, a) = (w(ω) + κ̄, a), κ̄ the image of κ in Λ̲_W.
items.note: In particular X⁰(T̲)-translations (e.g. t_{1̲}) act trivially, and t_η acts as translation by ε₁+ε₂ ∈ Λ̲_R-image, so W̲_a t_η acts on Λ̲_W as W̲_a does. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 2.3.7 (first part) — JH(R̄_{w̃^{−1}}(μ)) = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(w̃^{−1}(Σ))) for w̃ ∈ W̲_a t_η
items.statement: Let w̃ ∈ W̲_a t_η and assume that μ + w̃^{−1}(0) − η is 3-deep in C̲₀. Then JH(R̄_{w̃^{−1}}(μ)) = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(w̃^{−1}(Σ))).
items.note: From Proposition 2.3.5: write w̃^{−1} = t_κ s; then κ = w̃^{−1}(0) satisfies κ + η ∈ Λ̲_R and R_{w̃^{−1}}(μ) = R_s(μ + κ) (checked). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 2.3.7 (second part) — W^?(ρ̄_S) = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(w̃(r(Σ)))) for w̃ ∈ W̲_a
items.statement: If w̃ ∈ W̲_a and V(ρ̄_S|_{I_{F_S}}) = R_w̃(μ), then W^?(ρ̄_S) = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(w̃(r(Σ)))) [the depth hypothesis needed is that μ + w̃(0) − η be 3-deep in C̲₀].
items.note: From Proposition 2.3.4 with w̃ = t_ν s, ν = w̃(0) ∈ Λ̲_R. As printed, the sentence is attached to 'Let w̃ ∈ W̲_a t_η and assume that μ + w̃^{−1}(0) − η is 3-deep', which is inconsistent (W̲_a ∩ W̲_a t_η = ∅) and gives the wrong depth condition; the bracketed hypothesis is what the proof uses (see sourceIssues; arXiv v2 Proposition 2.2.10 had the consistent version). In the only use in §2 ((2.7), w̃ = s ∈ W̲) both conditions coincide. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.3 — fixed (s, μ) and the notation σ^{(s,μ)}_{(ω,a)}
items.statement: For the rest of §2.3 fix a character μ with μ − η 3-deep in C̲₀ and s ∈ W̲. For (sω, a) ∈ Λ̲_W^μ × A, σ^{(s,μ)}_{(ω,a)} := F(𝔗𝔯_μ(sω, a)), abbreviated σ_{(ω,a)} when (s, μ) is clear.
items.note: Heavily used in §§3–5 (e.g. Propositions 3.4.2, 3.5.x, 3.6.x) to label W^?(ρ̄, τ) and JH factors. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.3, (2.6) — parametrisation of JH(R̄_{s w̃^{−1}}(μ)) by w̃^{−1}(Σ)
items.statement: Let w̃ ∈ W̲_a t_η with s w̃^{−1}(Σ) ⊂ Λ̲_W^μ × A and μ + s w̃^{−1}(0) − η 3-deep. Then w̃^{−1}(Σ) → JH(R̄_{s w̃^{−1}}(μ)), w̃^{−1}(ω, a) ↦ σ^{(s,μ)}_{(w̃^{−1}(ω), a)}, is a bijection.   (2.6)
items.note: By Proposition 2.3.7 (first part) applied to w̃ s^{−1} ∈ W̲_a t_η (note W̲_a t_η s^{−1} = W̲_a t_η) and injectivity of 𝔗𝔯_μ. Printed with '→' for '↦'. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.3, (2.7) — parametrisation of W^?(ρ̄_S) by r(Σ)
items.statement: If V(ρ̄_S|_{I_{F_S}}) = R_s(μ), then r(Σ) → W^?(ρ̄_S), r(ω, a) ↦ σ^{(s,μ)}_{r(ω,a)}, is a bijection.   (2.7)
items.note: By Proposition 2.3.7 (second part) with w̃ = s, or directly Proposition 2.3.4 with ν = 0; #W^?(ρ̄_S) = 9^{#J}. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Definition 2.3.8 (first part) — outer/inner Jordan–Hölder factors and the defect Def_R(σ)
items.statement: σ ∈ JH(R̄_{s w̃^{−1}}(μ)) is an outer (resp. inner) weight for R := R_{s w̃^{−1}}(μ) in component i ∈ J if σ = σ_{(w̃^{−1}(ω), a)} with (ω_i, a_i) ∈ Σ₀^obv (resp. (ω_i, a_i) ∈ Σ₀^inn). The defect of σ with respect to R is Def_R(σ) := #{i ∈ J : σ is an inner weight of R in component i}.   (2.8)
items.note: Existing id kept (the checkpoint's statement was a paraphrase). Here (ω, a) ∈ Σ, w̃ ∈ W̲_a t_η as in (2.6). Well-definedness (independence of the presentation of R with μ fixed) is not discussed; it holds because two presentations differ by an element of W̲̃^der stabilising Σ, and the per-embedding stabiliser of Σ₀ (rotations, conjugation by Ω ≅ Z/3) preserves Σ₀^inn (checked). Used in Theorem 4.1.9: ℓℓ(R̄^σ) = 2Def_R(σ) + 3(f − Def_R(σ)) + 1. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: The chart comparison and the constituent bijection must be supplied by G01; do not count all lower-alcove coordinates as inner.

api.name: defect_bounds
api.statement: 0≤Def≤|J|.

api.name: defect_product
api.statement: Defects add under products.

unitTests: (epsilon1+epsilon2,0) has defect zero.
(0,0) has defect one.
((0,0),(0,1)) has defect one.

items.name: Definition 2.3.8 (second part) — obvious/shadow weights of ρ̄_S and the defect Def_{ρ̄_S}(σ)
items.statement: If V(ρ̄_S|_{I_{F_S}}) = R_s(μ), σ ∈ W^?(ρ̄_S) is an obvious (resp. shadow) weight for ρ̄_S in component i ∈ J if σ = σ_{r(ω,a)} with (ω_i, a_i) ∈ Σ₀^obv (resp. (ω_i, a_i) ∈ Σ₀^inn). The defect of σ with respect to ρ̄_S is Def_{ρ̄_S}(σ) := #{i ∈ J : σ is a shadow weight of ρ̄_S in component i}.   (2.9)
items.note: Σ is obvious in every component iff σ ∈ W_obv(ρ̄_S) (Proposition 2.3.1). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Table 1 — the graph structure on Σ₀
items.note: Vertices written σ_{(ω,a)} in the table. Checked for this reading: this is exactly the restriction of the adjacency of Definition 2.1.6 to Σ₀ (edges join label-0 and label-1 vertices whose ω differ by an element of {0, ±ε₁, ±ε₂, ±(ε₁−ε₂)}). Eccentricities: 2 for Σ₀^inn, 3 for Σ₀^obv (consistent with Theorem 4.1.9(1)). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.3 — product graph Σ₀^J; the bijections (2.6), (2.7) respect adjacency
items.statement: Σ₀^J denotes the product graph of Table 1 (vertices adjacent iff they differ in exactly one component, where they are adjacent in Σ₀). The bijections (2.6) and (2.7) respect adjacency for JH(R̄_{s w̃^{−1}}(μ)), W^?(ρ̄_S) and Σ₀^J.
items.note: Asserted without proof; holds because the maps are compositions of r and affine maps of Λ̲_W with linear part in W̲ (which preserve the W̲-invariant set (2.3)) with the chart 𝔗𝔯_μ, and adjacency of Serre weights is defined through the chart (Definition 2.1.6). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §2.3 — Bruhat order on W̃ (and W̲̃) from the dominant base alcove
items.statement: The choice of the dominant base alcove endows the extended affine Weyl group W̃ of G = GL_{3/F} with a Bruhat order ≤; similarly there is the natural generalisation of the Bruhat order ≤ on W̲̃ (componentwise).
items.note: Standard: W̃ = W_a ⋊ Ω with Ω the stabiliser of the base alcove; w̃ ≤ w̃' iff they have the same Ω-component and their W_a-parts are ≤ in the Coxeter group (W_a, {α, β, γ⁺}). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Definition 2.3.9 — the admissible set Adm(λ)
items.statement: For λ ∈ X^*(T), Adm(λ) := {w̃ ∈ W̃ | w̃ ≤ t_{s(λ)} for some s ∈ W}. For μ = (μ_j)_j ∈ X^*(T̲), Adm(μ) := ∏_j Adm(μ_j) ⊂ W̲̃.
items.note: Dominant-base-alcove convention; in [LLHLM18] the corresponding set for the antidominant alcove is called Adm(η), denoted Adm^∨(η) here (Remark 2.3.10). #Adm(η) = 25 (Figure 2; checked). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Remark 2.3.10 — dominant vs antidominant base alcove; γ⁺ = t_{(1,0,−1)}(13), γ = (13)t_{(1,0,−1)}; Adm^∨(η)
items.statement: For the combinatorics of weights (§2) one uses the dominant base alcove and the affine reflection γ⁺ = t_{(1,0,−1)}(13) as a generator of W_a^der. On the Galois side (§3) the antidominant base alcove appears naturally, and the analogous set Adm^∨(η) for the antidominant base alcove plays an important role (Definition 3.1.1); its affine generator is γ = (13)t_{(1,0,−1)}. What [LLHLM18] calls Adm(η) is denoted Adm^∨(η) here.

items.name: Corollary 2.3.11 (first part) — ℛ(JH(R̄_s(μ))) ∩ JH(R̄_{s w̃^{−1}}(μ)) is indexed by Σ_{w̃^{−1}}
items.statement: Let w̃ ∈ W̲_a t_η and assume that μ − η and μ + s w̃^{−1}(0̲) − η are 3-deep in C̲₀. Then ℛ(JH(R̄_s(μ))) ∩ JH(R̄_{s w̃^{−1}}(μ)) = {σ^{(s,μ)}_{r(ω,a)} : (ω, a) ∈ Σ_{w̃^{−1}}}.
items.note: Proof: reduce to s = id by Proposition 2.3.7; then (2.6), (2.7) identify the intersection with 𝔗𝔯_μ(w̃^{−1}(Σ) ∩ r(Σ)), and w̃^{−1}(Σ) ∩ r(Σ) = r(Σ_{w̃^{−1}}) (r commutes with the action, r² = 1).
