Then JH(R̄_s(μ − 1̲)) ∩ ℛ(JH(R̄_{s w̃}(μ − 1̲))) = {σ^{(s,μ)}_{(ω,a)} : (ω, a) ∈ Σ_w̃}.
items.note: 'Proved similarly': JH(R̄_s(μ − 1̲)) = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(sΣ)) by Proposition 2.3.5 (ν = −1̲, ν + η ∈ Λ̲_R), and R_{sw̃}(μ − 1̲) = R_{s w̃ t_{−1̲}}(μ) with s w̃ t_{−1̲} ∈ W̲_a, so Proposition 2.3.7 (second part)/2.3.4 gives ℛ(JH) = F(𝔗𝔯_μ(s w̃ r(Σ))) provided μ + s w̃(0) − 1̲ − η (equivalently μ + s w̃(0) − η) is 3-deep. items.name: Lemma 2.3.12 — weights outside r(Σ) lie in w̃^{−1}(Σ) for some non-admissible w̃
items.statement: If (ω, a) ∈ (Λ̲_W × A) ∖ r(Σ), there exists w̃ ∈ W̲_a t_η such that (ω, a) ∈ w̃^{−1}(Σ) and w̃ ∉ Adm(η).
items.note: Proof: reduce to #J = 1 (in a component with (ω_i, a_i) ∉ r(Σ₀) choose a non-admissible w̃_i; in the others any w̃_i ∈ W_a t_η moving (ω_i, a_i) into Σ₀, which exists since every W_a-orbit on Λ_W × {0,1} meets Σ₀), then check with Figure 2. Verified by computer for #J = 1 on all (ω, a) with ω = aε₁ + bε₂, |a|, |b| ≤ 8 (far points are trivial). Also verified: no non-admissible element moves a point of r(Σ₀) into Σ₀. items.name: Corollary 2.3.13 — separating a non-predicted weight from W^? by a 3-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation
items.statement: Let λ ∈ X₁(T̲) be 5-deep and let μ − η ∈ C̲₀ be 3-deep. If F(λ) ∉ ℛ(JH(R̄_s(μ))), then there exists a 3-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation R_{s'}(μ') such that F(λ) ∈ JH(R̄_{s'}(μ')) but ℛ(JH(R̄_s(μ))) ∩ JH(R̄_{s'}(μ')) = ∅.
items.note: Proof: if (λ − μ + η)|_Z̲ ∉ (p − π)X^*(Z̲) any Deligne–Lusztig representation containing F(λ) works (tacitly a 3-generic one, which exists as λ is 5-deep). Otherwise by Proposition 2.1.4 σ^{(s,μ)}_{(ω,a)} ≅ F(λ) for some (sω, a) ∈ Λ̲_W^μ × A; (ω, a) ∉ r(Σ) by (2.7); Lemma 2.3.12 gives w̃ ∈ W̲_a t_η ∖ Adm(η) with (ω, a) ∈ w̃^{−1}(Σ); take s' = s w^{−1}, μ' = μ + s w̃^{−1}(0), so R_{s'}(μ') = R_{s w̃^{−1}}(μ). As ω − w̃^{−1}(0) ∈ W̲(Σ̄) (Σ̄ the image of Σ in Λ̲_W, pairings with coroots bounded by 2) and λ is 5-deep, μ + s w̃^{−1}(0) − η is 3-deep; Proposition 2.3.7 gives F(λ) ∈ JH(R̄_{s'}(μ')), and Corollary 2.3.11 with Σ_{w̃^{−1}} = ∅ (emptiness criterion; w̃^{−1} ∉ Adm(η)X⁰(T̲) because Adm(η)X⁰ is stable under inversion) gives the empty intersection. Checked. Used for weight elimination/modularity arguments in §3.5 (cf. p. 36 'By Corollary 2.3.13, τ_S above can be taken so that …'). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Codimension-two extension for Cohen–Macaulay sheaves on X_∞(τ_S) (cited from [HK04, Proposition 3.5]; used in the proof of Theorem 5.2.3)
items.statement: Let X_∞(τ_S) = Spec R_∞(τ_S) (normal and Cohen–Macaulay), Z ⊂ X_∞(τ_S) the locus of points lying on two irreducible components of the special fibre (codimension two), and j : U := X_∞(τ_S) ∖ Z ↪ X_∞(τ_S). If M is a Cohen–Macaulay sheaf on X_∞(τ_S) [of full support, i.e. maximal Cohen–Macaulay, as are the M_∞(σ(τ_S)°)], then j_* j^* M = M.
items.locator: §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.2.3, published p. 120; arXiv v4 p. 90 — outside R1's page range; also cited in the proof of Theorem 5.2.3, published p. 120 ('cf. [HK04, Proposition 3.5]')
items.note: The checkpoint's statement was a general Stacks-project form (Noetherian local A, finite CM module of full support, Z of height ≥ 2 ⇒ M̃ ≅ j_*j^*M̃), with locator 'Stacks 0E9I Lemma 31.5.11'. The paper cites [HK04, Proposition 3.5] (reflexive/S₂ extension). The printed hypothesis 'Cohen–Macaulay' needs 'of full support' (maximal CM): a CM sheaf supported on Z violates the conclusion; in the application M = M_∞(σ(τ_S)°) is maximal CM by axiom (1) of Definition 3.5.1. Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 (route 6).
items.proofOutline: By T57 every removed stalk has depth at least two. On each affine neighborhood T65 and T56 give vanishing in degrees zero and one, and T55 identifies the restriction as an isomorphism. These maps are natural and glue. This uses absolute stalk depths; the relative fibrewise codimension condition in HK04 3.5 is not asserted for the special-fibre crossings.

𝒥 is identified with the set of embeddings K ↪ E and with Z/fZ via the fixed embedding σ_0 (σ_i = σ_0 ∘ φ^{-i}); 'component i' and 'embedding i' are used interchangeably.

items.name: W̃^∨ — extended affine Weyl group with antidominant Bruhat order
items.statement: W̃^∨_𝒥 (respectively W̃^∨ for one embedding) is the partially ordered group which equals W̃_𝒥 (respectively W̃ of GL3) as a group, but whose Bruhat order ≤ is defined using the antidominant base alcove. For μ ∈ X^*(T_𝒥), Adm^∨(μ) is defined as in Definition 2.3.9 (Adm(μ) = ∏_j {w̃ ∈ W̃ : w̃ ≤ t_{s(μ_j)} for some s ∈ W}) but with this antidominant Bruhat order. The affine generator for the antidominant base alcove is γ = (13)t_{(1,0,−1)} (the dominant one being γ^+ = t_{(1,0,−1)}(13)). What [LLHLM18] calls Adm(η) is Adm^∨(η) here. A length function ℓ : W̃^∨ → Z is attached to this Coxeter structure.
items.note: Galois-side objects (Kisin-module shapes) live in W̃^∨; weight-side combinatorics (Table 2, Adm(η)) live in W̃ with the dominant base alcove; Definition 3.1.1 passes between them. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Definition 3.1.1 — the involution w̃ ↦ w̃^*
items.statement: Define a bijection W̃^∨_𝒥 → W̃_𝒥, w̃ ↦ w̃^*, by: (1) for w = (w_j) ∈ W_𝒥, w^* = (w^*_j) with w^*_j = w_{f−1−j}^{−1}; (2) for ν = (ν_j) ∈ X^*(T_𝒥), ν^* = (ν^*_j) with ν^*_j = ν_{f−1−j}; (3) for w̃ = w t_ν ∈ W̃^∨_𝒥, w̃^* := t_{ν^*} w^* ∈ W̃_𝒥. For j ∈ 𝒥, w̃^*_j denotes the j-th component of w̃^*.
items.note: Indices j are read mod f. The map is an involution (applying * twice returns w̃). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: w̃ ↦ w̃^* is a group antihomomorphism
items.statement: The map w̃ ↦ w̃^* of Definition 3.1.1 is an antihomomorphism of groups: (w̃_1 w̃_2)^* = w̃_2^* w̃_1^* for all w̃_1, w̃_2 ∈ W̃_𝒥.
items.note: Stated without proof ('Note that'). Checked: (w_1t_{ν_1}w_2t_{ν_2})^* = t_{(w_2^{-1}ν_1+ν_2)^*}w_2^*w_1^* = (w_2t_{ν_2})^*(w_1t_{ν_1})^*, using (w^{-1}λ)^* = w^*λ^*. Also used: (w̃^*)^* = w̃. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: s_τ, α_{(s,μ)}, r, K′, f′ attached to a lowest alcove presentation
items.statement: Let τ be a tame inertial type, always assumed 1-generic, with a fixed lowest alcove presentation (s, μ) (Definition 2.2.1/2.2.2(4): μ ∈ C_0 and τ ≅ τ(s, μ+η)). For s = (s_0,…,s_{f−1}) ∈ W_𝒥 and μ = (μ_j)_{0≤j≤f−1} ∈ X^*(T_𝒥) put s_τ := s_0 s_{f−1} s_{f−2} ⋯ s_1 ∈ W and α_{(s,μ)} ∈ X^*(T_𝒥) with α_{(s,μ),0} = μ_0 + η_0 and α_{(s,μ),j} = s_1^{−1}s_2^{−1}⋯s_j^{−1}(μ_j + η_j) for 1 ≤ j ≤ f−1. Let r ∈ {1,2,3} be the order of s_τ, f′ := fr, and K′ the unramified extension of Q_p of degree f′.
items.note: This is Definition 2.2.1 applied to (s, μ+η); in particular τ ≅ τ((s_τ,1,…,1), α_{(s,μ)}). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Remark 3.1.2 — orientation s_or of α_{(s,μ)}
items.statement: [LLHLM18] writes types as τ((s_τ,1,…,1), α_{(s,μ)}), with α_{(s,μ),j} = (a_{1,j}, a_{2,j}, a_{3,j}). The element s_or := (s_1^{−1}s_2^{−1}⋯s_{f−1}^{−1}, s_1^{−1}s_2^{−1}⋯s_{f−2}^{−1}, …, s_1^{−1}, 1) ∈ W_𝒥 (so s_{or,i} = s_1^{−1}⋯s_{f−1−i}^{−1}) is called the orientation of α_{(s,μ)} [LLHLM18, Definition 2.6 and (2.2)]. It satisfies s_or^*(α_{(s,μ)}) = μ + η, and hence (0, s_or^*)·((s_τ,1,…,1), α_{(s,μ)}) = (s, μ+η) for the action (2.4).
items.note: Checked: s^*_{or,j} = (s_{or,f−1−j})^{−1} = s_j⋯s_1, so s^*_{or,j}(α_{(s,μ),j}) = μ_j+η_j. The notion of lowest alcove presentation does not appear in [LLHLM18]. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Principal series type; base change τ′
items.statement: If r = 1 (i.e. s_τ = 1) τ is called a principal series type. Otherwise τ′ denotes the base change of τ to K′/K, i.e. τ regarded as a principal series type for G_{K′}.
items.note: Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: α′_{(s,μ)} — data for the base-changed type
items.statement: Using an embedding σ′_0 : k′ ↪ F extending σ_0, identify X^*(T)^{Hom(k′,F)} ≅ X^*(T_𝒥)^r and define α′_{(s,μ)} by α′_{(s,μ), j+kf} := s_τ^{−k}(α_{(s,μ),j}) for 0 ≤ j ≤ f−1, 0 ≤ k ≤ r−1.
items.note: Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: τ′ ≅ τ_{K′}(1, α′_{(s,μ)})
items.statement: If τ_{K′}(w′, μ′) denotes the construction of Definition 2.2.1 of tame types over K′ for (w′, μ′) ∈ (W_𝒥 × X^*(T_𝒥))^r, then τ′ ≅ τ_{K′}(1, α′_{(s,μ)}).
items.note: 'By direct comparison using equation (2.5)'. Checked with the convention (sα)_i = α_{s^{-1}(i)}: the exponent of the i-th character is Σ_k p^{fk} a^{(0)}_{s_τ^k(i)}, as in (2.5). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Equation (3.1) — orientation of α′_{(s,μ)}
items.statement: The orientation s′_or ∈ W_𝒥^r of α′_{(s,μ)} in the sense of [LLHLM18, Definition 2.6] is given by s′_{or, j+kf} = s_τ^{k+1} s_{or,j} for 0 ≤ j ≤ f−1, 0 ≤ k ≤ r−1.
items.note: Printed with 'def=' but it is a computation of the orientation (compare [LLHLM18, Proposition 6.1]). Consistent with the verification of (3.3) in the proof of Proposition 3.2.1. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: L′, Δ′ ⊆ Δ
items.statement: Let π_r := (−p)^{1/(p^{rf}−1)}, L′ := K′(π_r), Δ′ := Gal(L′/K′) ⊆ Δ := Gal(L′/K). τ defines an O-valued representation of Δ′.
items.note: Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: 𝔖_{L′,R} with Δ-action and Frobenius
items.statement: For a complete local Noetherian O-algebra R with residue field F′ finite over F, let 𝔖_{L′,R} := (W(k′) ⊗_{Z_p} R)[[u′]]. Δ acts as follows: g ∈ Δ′ acts by g(u′) = (g(π_r)/π_r) u′ and trivially on coefficients; if σ ∈ Gal(L′/Q_p) is the lift of Frobenius on W(k′) fixing π_r, then σ^f generates Gal(K′/K) and acts naturally on W(k′), trivially on u′ and R. Set v := (u′)^{p^{rf}−1}. Then (𝔖_{L′,R})^{Δ=1} = (W(k) ⊗_{Z_p} R)[[v]]. The Frobenius φ : 𝔖_{L′,R} → 𝔖_{L′,R} acts as σ on W(k′), trivially on R, and sends u′ to (u′)^p.
items.note: The invariants identity is noted without proof (Δ′-invariants are power series in v; σ^f-invariants of W(k′) are W(k)). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) for principal series τ (imported from [CL18, §3])
items.statement: If τ is a principal series type, Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) is the category of Kisin modules over L′ with tame descent datum of type τ and height in [0, h], as defined in [CL18, Section 3].
items.note: Cited, not defined here. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Kisin module over 𝔖_{L′,R} [LLHLM18, Definition 2.3]
items.statement: A Kisin module (𝔐, φ_𝔐) over 𝔖_{L′,R} of height ≤ h in the sense of [LLHLM18, Definition 2.3]: a finite projective 𝔖_{L′,R}-module 𝔐 with a φ-semilinear map φ_𝔐 whose linearisation has cokernel killed by E(u′)^h, E the Eisenstein polynomial of π_r.
items.note: Cited, not proved or restated in the paper; the gloss of the definition is the standard one and is not printed in LLHLM20. Planned: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.4 plans Breuil–Kisin modules over the Kummer tower, including descent data.

items.name: Definition 3.1.3 — Y^{[0,h],τ}(R), Kisin modules with tame descent datum of type τ
items.statement: An element (𝔐, φ_𝔐, {ĝ}) ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) is a Kisin module (𝔐, φ_𝔐) over 𝔖_{L′,R} [LLHLM18, Definition 2.3] with height less than h together with a semilinear action {ĝ} of Δ which commutes with φ_𝔐 such that for each 0 ≤ j ≤ f′−1, 𝔐^{(j)} mod u′ ≅ τ^∨ ⊗_O R as Δ′-representations. In particular, the semilinear action induces an isomorphism ι_𝔐 : (σ^f)^*(𝔐) ≅ 𝔐 as elements of Y^{[0,h],τ′}(R).
items.note: 'height less than h' should be read as 'height in [0,h]' (cf. the notation Y^{[0,h],τ}; see sourceIssues). Remark 3.1.5: τ^∨ appears because the Galois functors are contravariant, following [LLHLM18] (which instead put a minus sign in the descent-data equation before its Definition 2.1); [CL18, EGH13] use covariant functors. 𝔐^{(j)} is the j-th embedding component. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Remark 3.1.4 — Δ-action ⇔ ι_𝔐 with cocycle condition
items.statement: The datum of an extension of the Δ′-action on 𝔐 to a Δ-action is equivalent to the choice of an isomorphism ι_𝔐 : (σ^f)^*(𝔐) ≅ 𝔐 satisfying an appropriate cocycle condition.
items.note: Cited from [LLHLM18, Section 6.1]; both points of view are used interchangeably. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Eigenbasis of a Kisin module with principal series descent datum [LLHLM18, Definition 2.8]
items.statement: For a Kisin module with descent datum of principal series type τ′, an eigenbasis β′ = (β′^{(j′)})_{j′} is a collection of bases β′^{(j′)} = (f′_1^{(j′)}, f′_2^{(j′)}, f′_3^{(j′)}) of the 𝔐^{(j′)} consisting of Δ′-eigenvectors, as in [LLHLM18, Definition 2.8].
items.note: Cited. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: [LLHLM18, Lemma 6.2] — the identification 𝔐^{(j′)} ≅ ((σ^f)^*𝔐)^{(j′+f)}
items.statement: There is a natural isomorphism 𝔐^{(j′)} ≅ ((σ^f)^*(𝔐))^{(j′+f)} (indices mod f′), used to compare eigenbases in embeddings j′ and j′+f via ι_𝔐.
items.note: Cited. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Definition 3.1.6 — eigenbasis of 𝔐 ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(R)
items.statement: An eigenbasis of 𝔐 ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) is an eigenbasis β′ = (β′^{(j′)})_{j′} of 𝔐 considered as a Kisin module with descent datum of type τ′ [LLHLM18, Definition 2.8] which is compatible with ι_𝔐: writing β′^{(j′)} = (f′_1^{(j′)}, f′_2^{(j′)}, f′_3^{(j′)}), the composite 𝔐^{(j′)} ≅ ((σ^f)^*(𝔐))^{(j′+f)} →^{ι_𝔐} 𝔐^{(j′+f)} (left isomorphism from [LLHLM18, Lemma 6.2]) maps {f′_1^{(j′)}, f′_2^{(j′)}, f′_3^{(j′)}} to {f′_1^{(j′+f)}, f′_2^{(j′+f)}, f′_3^{(j′+f)}}, for all 0 ≤ j′ ≤ f′−1. Shorthand: ι_𝔐(β′^{(j′)}) = β′^{(j′+f)}.
items.note: The compatibility is between unordered sets; as ordered bases the proof of Proposition 3.2.1 writes ι^{(j′)}_𝔐(β′^{(j′)}) = β′^{(j′+f)} s_τ^{−1}. See also [LLHL19, Definition 3.2.8]. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: O_{E,K′}, O_{E,L′} (and O_{E,K})
items.statement: O_{E,K′} (respectively O_{E,L′}) is the p-adic completion of (W(k′)[[v]])[1/v] (respectively of (W(k′)[[u′]])[1/u′]); O_{E,K} is defined analogously with W(k).
items.note: Planned: PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.0 plans étale φ-modules and Fontaine's equivalence.

items.name: Categories Φ-Mod^ét_{K′}(R), Φ-Mod^ét_{dd,L′}(R), Φ-Mod^ét_K(R) [LLHLM18, §2.3]
items.statement: For a complete local Noetherian O-algebra R: Φ-Mod^ét_{K′}(R) is the category of étale (φ, O_{E,K′} ⊗̂_{Z_p} R)-modules; Φ-Mod^ét_{dd,L′}(R) that of étale (φ, O_{E,L′} ⊗̂_{Z_p} R)-modules with descent data from L′ to K′; Φ-Mod^ét_K(R) and Φ-Mod^ét_{dd,L}(R) are defined analogously.
items.note: Recalled from [LLHLM18, Section 2.3]. (No field L is defined in the paper; 'Φ-Mod^ét_{dd,L}' is presumably descent data from L′ to K.) Planned: PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.0 plans étale φ-modules and Fontaine's equivalence.

items.name: The étale φ-module 𝓜 = (𝔐 ⊗ O_{E,L′})^{Δ=1}
items.statement: Given (𝔐, ι_𝔐) ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(R), 𝔐 ⊗ O_{E,L′} is naturally an object of Φ-Mod^ét_{dd,L′}(R); define 𝓜 := (𝔐 ⊗ O_{E,L′})^{Δ=1} ∈ Φ-Mod^ét_K(R) with the induced Frobenius. This defines a functor Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) → Φ-Mod^ét_K(R).
items.note: Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: The functor ε_0 : Φ-Mod^ét_K(R) → Φ^f-Mod^ét_{W(k)}(R) [LLHLM18, §2.3]
items.statement: ε_0 sends 𝓜 to its 0-th embedding component 𝓜^{(0)} with the φ^f-structure given by the f-fold composite of the partial Frobenii φ^{(f−1)}∘⋯∘φ^{(0)} acting on 𝓜^{(0)}.
items.note: Recalled from [LLHLM18, Section 2.3]. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: The functor V^*_K
items.statement: For R a local Artinian O-algebra with finite residue field F, V^*_K is 'the usual functor' from Φ-Mod^ét_K(R) to representations of G_{K∞} over R (contravariant Fontaine functor).
items.note: Not defined in the paper; K_∞ is the Kummer-type extension used in [LLHLM18] (K_∞ = K((−p)^{1/p^∞})). Planned: PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.0 plans étale φ-modules and Fontaine's equivalence.

items.name: The functor T^*_dd : Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) → Rep_R(G_{K∞})
items.statement: T^*_dd (written T^*_{dd′} in [LLHLM18, §6.1]) is the functor Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) → Rep_R(G_{K∞}), (𝔐, ι_𝔐) ↦ V^*_K(𝓜), where 𝓜 = (𝔐 ⊗ O_{E,L′})^{Δ=1}.
items.note: Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Proposition 3.2.1 — Frobenius of 𝓜 in terms of the Kisin module
items.statement: Let τ be a 1-generic type with lowest alcove presentation (s, μ). Let 𝔐 ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) and β an eigenbasis of 𝔐. Let s_or = (s_{or,j})_j be the orientation for τ and write A^{(j)} = Mat_β(φ^{(j)}_{𝔐, s_{or,j+1}(3)}) for j ∈ {0,…,f−1}. Let 𝓜 = (𝔐 ⊗ O_{E,L′})^{Δ=1} ∈ Φ-Mod^ét_K(R). Then there is a basis 𝔣 = (𝔣^{(j)})_j of 𝓜 such that Mat_𝔣(φ^{(j)}_𝓜) = A^{(j)} s^*_j v^{μ^*_j + η^*_j}.
items.note: A sharpening of [LLHLM18, Proposition 2.26]. Proof: direct computation using [LLHLM18, Propositions 2.13, 2.26, 6.1, 6.9], equations (3.2), (3.3). s^*_j = s_{f−1−j}^{−1}, μ^*_j = μ_{f−1−j}. Checked: with (3.1) and Remark 3.1.2, (s′_{or,j′+1})^{−1}s′_{or,j′} = s^*_j and (s′_{or,j′})^{−1}(α′_{(s,μ),f′−1−j′}) = μ^*_j+η^*_j. Misprint in the proof: '0 ≤ j′ < f′−1' twice (issue E01). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Twisted eigenbasis 𝔣′^{(j′)} of 𝓜′^{(j′)} (proof of Proposition 3.2.1)
items.note: Compare [LLHLM18, Section 2.1]. The identity for p a′^{(j′)} − a′^{(j′+1)} was checked by telescoping. The printed range '0 ≤ j′ < f′−1' should be '≤' (E01). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: [LLHLM18, Proposition 2.13] as used — matrix of φ^{(j′)}_{𝓜′} in the bases 𝔣′
items.statement: (As used in the proof of Proposition 3.2.1.) For 0 ≤ j′ ≤ f′−1 the matrix of φ^{(j′)}_{𝓜′} : 𝓜′^{(j′)} → 𝓜′^{(j′+1)} with respect to the bases 𝔣′ is s′_{or,j′+1} A^{(j′)} (s′_{or,j′+1})^{−1} (u′)^{p a′^{(j′)}_{(s,μ)} − a′^{(j′+1)}_{(s,μ)}} = s′_{or,j′+1} A^{(j′)} (s′_{or,j′+1})^{−1} v^{α′_{(s,μ), f′−1−j′}} (equation (3.2)), where A^{(j′)} = Mat_{β′}(φ^{(j′)}_{𝔐′, s′_{or,j′+1}(3)}).
items.note: Cited ('a direct computation using [LLHLM18, Proposition 2.13]'). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: [LLHLM18, Proposition 6.9] as used — A^{(j′)} depends only on j′ mod f
items.statement: For 𝔐 ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) with an eigenbasis compatible with ι_𝔐, the matrices A^{(j′)} = Mat_{β′}(φ^{(j′)}_{𝔐′, s′_{or,j′+1}(3)}) depend only on j′ mod f.
items.note: Cited ('cf.'). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Proposition 3.2.2 — matrix of ε_0(𝓜)
items.statement: Let 𝔐 ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(R) and let 𝓜 = (𝔐 ⊗ O_{E,L′})^{Δ=1} ∈ Φ-Mod^ét_K(R) be the associated étale φ-module over K. If 𝔣 is a basis of 𝓜 and B^{(j)} := Mat_𝔣(φ^{(j)}_𝓜) are the matrices of the partial Frobenii, then the étale φ^f-module ε_0(𝓜) is described by Mat_{𝔣^{(0)}}(φ^f_{𝓜^{(0)}}) = ∏_{j=0}^{f−1} φ^j(B^{(f−j−1)}).
items.note: No proof printed (immediate). Product convention (§1.4): ∏_{j=0}^m B_j = B_0·B_1⋯B_m. Checked: φ^f(e^{(0)}) = e^{(0)} B^{(f−1)} φ(B^{(f−2)}) ⋯ φ^{f−1}(B^{(0)}). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Lemma 3.2.3 — inertial type from a monomial φ^f-module
items.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F) be semisimple and 0-generic. Let 𝓜 ∈ Φ^f-Mod^ét_{W(k)}(F) with V^*_K(𝓜) ≅ ρ̄|_{G_{K∞}}. Assume there exist s_0 ∈ W, λ = (λ_j) ∈ X^*_1(T_𝒥) and a basis of 𝓜 such that the φ^f-action on 𝓜 is given by D s_0^{−1} v^{μ} where D ∈ T(F) and μ := Σ_{j=0}^{f−1} p^j λ_j ∈ X^*(T). Then, letting s = (s_0, 1, …, 1) ∈ W_𝒥, V(ρ̄|_{I_K}) = R_s(λ).
items.note: Proof: with k the order of s_0, φ^{fk}(e_i) = (∏_{m=0}^{k−1} D_{s_0^{m+1}(i)}) v^{Σ_{m=0}^{k−1} p^{fm} μ_{s_0^{m+1}(i)}} e_i, so ρ̄|_{I_K} ≅ ⊕_i ω_{kf}^{Σ_m p^{fm} μ_{s_0^{m+1}(i)}} = τ̄(s, λ) by (2.5); checked. V is the map of [GHS18, Prop. 9.2.1] and V(τ̄(s,λ)) = R_s(λ) [GHS18, Prop. 9.2.3]. The proof uses neither λ ∈ X_1 nor 0-genericity; its application in Proposition 3.3.8 needs the intermediate statement ρ̄|_{I_K} ≅ τ̄(s,λ) (see sourceIssues). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Iwahori subgroup I(F′) ⊂ GL3(F′[[v]])
items.statement: For F′/F finite, I(F′) ⊂ GL3(F′[[v]]) is the Iwahori subgroup of elements which are upper triangular modulo v.
items.note: Planned: ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3 plans parahoric (Iwahori) group schemes.

items.name: Definition 3.3.1 — shape of a Kisin module (principal series type)
items.statement: Let τ be a principal series type and w̃ = (w̃_0, w̃_1, …, w̃_{f−1}) ∈ W̃^∨_𝒥. A Kisin module 𝔐 ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(F′) has shape w̃ if for any eigenbasis β the matrices (A^{(j)})_j = (Mat_β(φ^{(j)}_{𝔐, s_{or,j+1}(3)}))_j satisfy A^{(j)} ∈ I(F′) w̃_j I(F′) for all j (w̃_j viewed in GL3(F′((v))) via t_λ ↦ v^λ and permutation matrices).
items.note: Independence of the eigenbasis is implicit ('for any eigenbasis'). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Shape for a nonprincipal series type (via base change)
items.statement: For a nonprincipal series type τ, the shape of 𝔐 ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(F′) is defined in terms of its base change BC(𝔐) ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ′}(F′), as in [LLHL19, Definition 3.2.11] or [LLHLM18, Definition 6.10].
items.note: Cited; details not reproduced in the paper. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Closed substack Y^{λ,τ} ⊂ Y^{[0,h],τ} [CL18, §5]
items.statement: For λ ∈ X^*(T_𝒥) effective (λ_j = (a_{i,j})_i with a_{i,j} ≥ 0 for all i, j) and h ≫ 0, Y^{λ,τ} ⊂ Y^{[0,h],τ} is the closed substack defined in [CL18, Section 5] (cf. [LLHLM18, Section 2.2]).
items.note: Cited. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: F′-points of Y^{λ,τ} are the Kisin modules with shape in Adm^∨(λ)
items.statement: For any finite extension F′/F, Y^{λ,τ}(F′) ⊂ Y^{[0,h],τ}(F′) is the subgroupoid consisting of Kisin modules with shape in Adm^∨(λ).
items.note: Cited from [CL18, Section 5] / [LLHLM18, Section 2.2]; stated without proof. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Uniqueness of the Kisin module of type (η, τ) [LLHLM18, Theorem 3.2, §6.2]
items.statement: Let τ be 3-generic and ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F). There exists at most one Kisin module 𝔐 ∈ Y^{[0,2],τ}(F) (height in [0,2]) with T^*_dd(𝔐) ≅ ρ̄|_{G_{K∞}}; the same holds after extension of scalars.
items.locator: §3.3, after Definition 3.3.2, p. 31; used again in the proof of Theorem 3.3.12, p. 35
items.note: Cited: [LLHLM18, Theorem 3.2] for principal series types; [LLHLM18, Section 6.2 and the discussion before Lemma 6.13] in general. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Definition 3.3.2 — the shape w̃(ρ̄, τ)
items.statement: Let τ be a 3-generic type with lowest alcove presentation (s, μ) and ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F). Assume there exists 𝔐_ρ̄ ∈ Y^{η,τ}(F) with T^*_dd(𝔐_ρ̄) ≅ ρ̄|_{G_{K∞}}. Define w̃(ρ̄, τ) ∈ Adm^∨(η) to be the shape of 𝔐_ρ̄.
items.note: Well defined by cite-LLHLM18-thm-3-2-uniqueness. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Remark 3.3.3 — several places
items.statement: If #S > 1, for w̃ = (w̃_ṽ)_{ṽ∈S} define w̃^* := (w̃^*_ṽ)_{ṽ∈S} with each w̃^*_ṽ as in Definition 3.1.1; for a collection τ_S of 3-generic tame inertial types and a collection ρ̄_S of Galois representations put w̃(ρ̄_S, τ_S) := (w̃(ρ̄_ṽ, τ_ṽ))_{ṽ∈S}.
items.note: Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Definition 3.3.4 — semisimple Kisin module of shape w̃
items.statement: Let 𝔐 ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(F′), F′/F finite. 𝔐 is semisimple of shape w̃ = (w̃_j) if there exists an eigenbasis β of 𝔐 such that A^{(j)} ∈ T(F′[[v]]) w̃_j for 0 ≤ j ≤ f′−1.
items.note: T(F′[[v]]) = diagonal matrices with entries in F′[[v]]^×. The range j ≤ f′−1 uses that A^{(j′)} depends only on j′ mod f (w̃_j read mod f). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Proposition 3.3.5 — semisimple Kisin modules give semisimple representations
items.statement: If 𝔐 (∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(F′)) is semisimple of shape w̃, then T^*_dd(𝔐) is semisimple.
items.note: Proof: by Propositions 3.2.1 and 3.2.2 the matrix of ε_0(𝔐[1/u′]^{Δ=1}) lies in T(F′((v)))s for some s ∈ W; if s has order d, T^*_dd(𝔐) restricted to the unramified extension of K_∞ of degree d is a sum of characters, and since p ∤ d (d ≤ 3) T^*_dd(𝔐) is semisimple. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Proposition 3.3.6 — normal form of a semisimple Kisin module
items.statement: If 𝔐 is semisimple of shape w̃ = (w̃_j), then there exists an eigenbasis β such that A^{(j)} = w̃_j for 0 ≤ j ≤ f−2 and A^{(f−1)} ∈ T(F′) w̃_{f−1}.
items.note: Cited: 'See [LLHL19, Proposition 3.2.16]'. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Definition 3.3.7 — the étale φ-module 𝓜(w̃)
items.statement: For w̃ = (w_j t_{λ_j}) ∈ W̃^∨_𝒥, 𝓜(w̃) ∈ Φ-Mod^ét_K(F) is the free étale φ-module over O_{E,K} ⊗ F of rank three such that the matrix of φ^{(j)}_𝓜 : 𝓜(w̃)^{(j)} → 𝓜(w̃)^{(j+1)} with respect to the standard basis is w_j v^{λ_j}.
items.note: Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Proposition 3.3.8 (first isomorphism) — T^*_dd of a semisimple Kisin module
items.statement: Let (s, μ) be a lowest alcove presentation of τ. If 𝔐 ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(F′) is semisimple of shape w̃ ∈ W̃^∨_𝒥, then T^*_dd(𝔐)|_{I_K} ≅ V^*_K(𝓜(w̃ s^* t_{μ^*+η^*}))|_{I_K}. (Both sides are tame, so canonically extend to G_K.)
items.note: Proof: Proposition 3.3.6 combined with Proposition 3.2.1 (the constant diagonal matrix in A^{(f−1)} only changes an unramified twist). Special case n = 3 of [LLHL19, Corollary 3.2.17]. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Proposition 3.3.8 (second isomorphism) — the inertial type of a semisimple Kisin module
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 3.3.8, T^*_dd(𝔐)|_{I_K} ≅ V^*_K(𝓜(w̃ s^* t_{μ^*+η^*}))|_{I_K} ≅ τ̄(w, ν+η), where w ∈ W_𝒥 and ν ∈ X^*(T_𝒥) are determined by w̃ s^* t_{μ^*} = w^* t_{ν^*}.
items.note: Proof: φ^f on ε_0(𝓜(w^*t_{ν^*+η^*})) is ∏_{j=0}^{f−1} w_j^{−1} v^{p^j(ν_j+η_j)} (Prop. 3.2.2); conjugation invariance (fact-eps0-conjugation); (w, ν+η) ∼ (swπ(s)^{−1}, s(ν+η)) with [LLHL19, Prop. 2.2.4], [Her09, Lemma 4.2] reduces to w_i = 1 for i ≠ f−1; then Lemma 3.2.3. The last step needs one more constant conjugation (Lemma 3.2.3 is set up for w = (s_0,1,…,1)) and the form ρ̄|_{I_K} ≅ τ̄(s,λ) of the conclusion of Lemma 3.2.3 (see sourceIssues). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Conjugation invariance of ε_0(𝓜((s t_{ν+η} w π(s)^{−1})^*))
items.note: Π(s)_j = s_{j−1}, s_{−1} = s_{f−1}. Verified by expanding x^* for x = s t_{ν+η} w π(s)^{−1} and telescoping. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Proposition 3.3.9 — semisimple Kisin modules of a fixed shape and inertial restriction
items.statement: (As printed.) Let ρ̄, ρ̄′ be semisimple representations of G_K. Assume that there exists 𝔐 semisimple of shape w̃ such that T^*_dd(𝔐) ≅ ρ̄|_{G_{K∞}}. Then ρ̄′|_{I_K} ≅ ρ̄|_{I_K} if and only if there exists a semisimple 𝔐′ of shape w̃ such that T^*_dd(𝔐′) ≅ ρ̄|_{G_{K∞}}. (Intended: T^*_dd(𝔐′) ≅ ρ̄′|_{G_{K∞}}.)
items.note: Proof: 'counting unramified twists using Proposition 3.3.6'. As printed the right-hand condition always holds (take 𝔐′ = 𝔐): misprint E02. The 'if' direction of the intended statement follows from Proposition 3.3.8. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Lemma 3.3.10 — potentially crystalline lifts pass to ρ̄^ss
items.statement: If ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F) admits a potentially crystalline lift of type (λ, τ), then so does ρ̄^ss (after possibly replacing E with a ramified extension).
items.note: Proof: take a lift ρ of type (λ, τ); after enlarging coefficients there is a lattice with semisimple reduction by [Enn, Lemma 5(2)]. Referred to as 'Proposition 3.3.10' in the proof of Proposition 3.5.6. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: [Enn, Lemma 5(2)] — a lattice with semisimple reduction
items.statement: (As used.) Given a continuous representation ρ : G_K → GL_n(E), after enlarging E there is a G_K-stable lattice whose reduction is semisimple (i.e. ≅ ρ̄^ss).
items.note: Cited, not proved. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Theorem 3.3.11 — shapes of Kisin modules of potentially crystalline lifts
items.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F). Assume that ρ̄ has a potentially crystalline lift of type (λ, τ) where λ ∈ X^*(T_𝒥) is effective. Assume that either (1) τ is a regular principal series type or (2) λ = η and τ is 3-generic. Then, for sufficiently large h, there is a Kisin module 𝔐 ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(F) of shape w̃ = (w̃_0, …, w̃_{f−1}) ∈ Adm^∨(λ) such that T^*_dd(𝔐) ≅ ρ̄|_{G_{K∞}}. In particular, 𝔐 ∈ Y^{λ,τ}(F).
items.note: Cited: 'See [LLHL19, Theorem 3.2.20]'. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Theorem 3.3.12, case (1) — sums of characters admit semisimple Kisin modules
items.statement: Let ρ̄ be a semisimple representation of G_K which is a direct sum of characters, and τ a 1-generic tame type. If there exists a Kisin module 𝔐 ∈ Y^{λ,τ}(F) with T^*_dd(𝔐) ≅ ρ̄|_{G_{K∞}}, then there exist a finite extension F′/F and a semisimple Kisin module 𝔐′ ∈ Y^{λ,τ}(F′) with (after extending scalars) T^*_dd(𝔐′) ≅ ρ̄|_{G_{K∞}}.
items.note: Proof: 𝓜_dd = 𝔐[1/u′] = 𝓜_1⊕𝓜_2⊕𝓜_3 (φ- and descent-stable); the torus T = G_m^3 scaling the factors acts on the projective Kisin variety Y^{λ,τ}_{𝓜_dd}; a fixed point 𝔐′ over some F′ (Borel) splits as ⊕(𝔐′)^{χ_i} (3.4) into rank-one Kisin modules with descent datum, hence is semisimple with shape in Adm^∨(λ). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Theorem 3.3.12, case (2) — the Kisin module of type (η, τ) of a semisimple ρ̄ is semisimple
items.statement: Let ρ̄ be a semisimple representation of G_K, λ = η, and τ a 3-generic tame type. If there exists a Kisin module 𝔐 ∈ Y^{η,τ}(F) with T^*_dd(𝔐) ≅ ρ̄|_{G_{K∞}}, then there exists a semisimple Kisin module 𝔐′ ∈ Y^{η,τ}(F′) with T^*_dd(𝔐′) ≅ ρ̄|_{G_{K∞}}, and one can take F′ = F.
items.locator: §3.3, Theorem 3.3.12 ('Furthermore, we can take F′ = F in case (2)') and proof, pp. 33–35
items.note: The proof shows that 𝔐 itself is semisimple (this stronger form is what the proof of Lemma 3.5.4 uses). Proof: 𝔐 is unique [LLHLM18, Thm 3.2]; over the unramified K̆/K of degree 6, ρ̄ is a sum of characters, so BC(𝔐) is semisimple by case (1) and uniqueness; a gauge basis of 𝔐 induces one of BC(𝔐) which differs from the Prop. 3.3.6 normal-form basis by torus scaling [LLHLM18, Thm 4.16], so the Frobenius matrices of 𝔐 are monomial; monomial elements of I(F)w̃I(F) lie in T(F[[v]])w̃. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Kisin variety Y^{λ,τ}_{𝓜_dd} and its torus action
items.statement: For an étale φ-module with descent datum 𝓜_dd (a semilinear Δ-action), Y^{λ,τ}_{𝓜_dd} is the (projective) Kisin variety parametrizing lattices in 𝓜_dd which lie in Y^{λ,τ}: for principal series τ it is [LLHLM18, Definition 3.1]; in general it is the closed subscheme of fixed points of Y^{λ,τ′}_{𝓜_dd} under the natural action of σ^f. If 𝓜_dd = 𝓜_1⊕𝓜_2⊕𝓜_3 with each 𝓜_i stable under φ and Δ, the torus T = G_m^3 acts on 𝓜_dd by scaling each factor, inducing an algebraic action on Y^{λ,τ}_{𝓜_dd}.
items.note: Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Étale φ-modules over L′ with descent datum ≅ G_{K∞}-representations
items.statement: There is an equivalence of categories between étale φ-modules over L′ with descent datum to K and representations of G_{K∞}.
items.note: Cited: [LLHLM18, page 24] (principal series) and [LLHLM18, Section 6.1] (general). Planned: PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.0 plans étale φ-modules and Fontaine's equivalence.

items.name: Torus actions on projective varieties have fixed points (Borel)
items.statement: (As used.) An algebraic action of a split torus T on a nonempty projective variety over a finite field F has a fixed point defined over some finite extension F′/F.
items.note: Asserted without reference ('Any such action has a fixed point over some finite extension F′/F'): Borel fixed point theorem over F̄ plus finiteness of the field of definition. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Gauge basis [LLHLM18, Definition 2.22]
items.statement: A gauge basis of a Kisin module of type (η, τ) is an eigenbasis in which the partial Frobenius matrices take the normalized form of [LLHLM18, Definition 2.22]; a gauge basis of 𝔐 induces one on its base change.
items.note: Cited; the normal form is not reproduced here. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: [LLHLM18, Theorem 4.16] as used — gauge bases are unique up to torus scaling
items.statement: Two gauge bases of the same Kisin module of type (η, τ̆) differ by embedding-wise scaling by elements of the torus T.
items.note: Cited. Also asserted without proof in the same place: the eigenbasis putting the partial Frobenii in the form of Proposition 3.3.6 is a gauge basis. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Monomial elements of an Iwahori double coset
items.statement: For w̃ ∈ W̃ (embedded in GL3(F((v)))), the monomial matrices lying in I(F) w̃ I(F) are exactly those in T(F[[v]]) w̃.
items.locator: §3.3, end of proof of Theorem 3.3.12, p. 35
items.note: Stated without proof; follows from the Bruhat–Iwahori decomposition (a monomial matrix t_0 v^λ w′ with t_0 ∈ T(F[[v]]) lies in I (t_λ w′) I). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Remark 3.3.13 — semisimple reductions of type (η, τ) and admissible shapes
items.statement: For a fixed 3-generic type τ, Theorems 3.3.11 and 3.3.12 show that the set of semisimple ρ̄|_{I_K} arising as reductions of potentially crystalline representations of type (η, τ) is in bijection (via ρ̄ ↦ w̃(ρ̄, τ)) with a subset of Adm^∨((2,1,0))^f. In fact this admissibility condition exactly captures those semisimple ρ̄ which are reductions of [potentially] crystalline representations of type (η, τ), i.e. the potentially crystalline deformation ring of type (η, τ) of the semisimple ρ̄ corresponding to any w̃ ∈ Adm^∨((2,1,0))^f is nonzero: for ℓ(w̃_i) > 1 for all i by [LLHLM18, Table 7]; for K = Q_p by [LLHLM18, Section 8]; for general unramified K it follows from Theorem 3.5.3.
items.note: Injectivity uses Proposition 3.3.8. Printed 'reductions of crystalline representations' (misprint for potentially crystalline). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Proposition 3.4.1 — V(T^*_dd(𝔐)|_{I_K}) in terms of the shape
items.statement: Let (s, μ) be a lowest alcove presentation of τ. Let 𝔐 ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(F′) be semisimple of shape w̃ = (w̃_j) ∈ W̃^∨_𝒥. Then V(T^*_dd(𝔐)|_{I_K}) = R_{s w̃^*}(μ + η), where R_x(μ) := R_{w_x}(μ + x(0)) for x ∈ W̃_𝒥 with image w_x ∈ W_𝒥 (Definition 2.3.6).
items.note: Proof: Prop. 3.3.8 gives τ̄(w, ν+η) with w̃ s^* t_{μ^*} = w^* t_{ν^*}; [GHS18, Prop. 9.2.3] gives R_w(ν+η); and R_{sw̃^*}(μ+η) = R_w(ν+η) ('easy calculation': applying the antihomomorphism * gives t_μ s w̃^* = t_ν w, so s w̃^* = t_{ν−μ}w). Checked. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [GHS18, Proposition 9.2.3] — V(τ̄(w, μ)) = R_w(μ)
items.statement: For a good pair (w, μ), V(τ̄(w, μ)) ≅ R_w(μ), where V is the map from tame inertial types to Deligne–Lusztig representations of [GHS18, Proposition 9.2.1].
items.note: Cited. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 3.4.2 — W?(ρ̄, τ) as a function of the shape
items.statement: (As printed.) Let τ be a 3-generic type with lowest alcove presentation (s, μ) and let 𝔐 ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(F′) be semisimple of shape w̃ = (w̃_j) ∈ W̃^∨_𝒥. Let ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F) be semisimple and 3-generic and assume that ρ̄|_{G_{K∞}} ≅ T^*_dd(𝔐). Then W?(ρ̄, τ) := W?(ρ̄) ∩ JH(σ̄(τ)) = {σ^{(s,μ+η)}_{(ω,a)} : (ω,a) ∈ Σ_{w̃^*}} ⊂ JH(R̄_s(μ+η)), where Σ_x := Σ ∩ x(r(Σ)) and σ^{(s,μ′)}_{(ω,a)} := F(Tr_{μ′}(sω, a)).
items.note: Proof: Corollary 2.3.11 and Proposition 3.4.1. Consequence used later: #W?(ρ̄,τ) = ∏_j #Σ_{w̃^*_j} (Table 2). Two problems (see sourceIssues): the label should be σ^{(s,μ+η+1̲)} (central characters; second part of Cor. 2.3.11 with μ−1̲ = μ+η), and the proof needs w̃^* ∈ W_a t_η (e.g. w̃ ∈ Adm^∨(η), i.e. 𝔐 ∈ Y^{η,τ}); for other shapes the statement fails. Neither affects the uses in §3.4–3.5, which only need w̃ ∈ Adm^∨(η) and cardinalities. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark 3.4.3 — * exchanges Adm^∨(2,1,0) and Adm(2,1,0)
items.statement: An explicit list of the elements of Adm^∨(2,1,0) is [LLHLM18, Table 1]. The involution w̃ ↦ w̃^* reverses the order of the components, reverses the order of a word in the generators, and turns γ = (13)v^{(1,0,−1)} into γ^+. In particular (·)^* defines a bijection between Adm^∨(2,1,0) and Adm(2,1,0).
items.note: Checked γ^* = t_{(1,0,−1)}(13) = γ^+ (f = 1). Adm(2,1,0) has 25 elements (Figure 2). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Proposition 3.4.4 — type elimination: W?(ρ̄^ss, τ) ≠ ∅
items.statement: Let τ be a 1-generic tame inertial type. If ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F) is 6-generic and arises as the reduction of a potentially crystalline representation of type (η, τ), then W?(ρ̄^ss, τ) ≠ ∅.
items.note: Proof: if τ is 3-generic, Theorem 3.3.11 + Lemma 3.3.10 give 𝔐 ∈ Y^{η,τ}(F) with T^*_dd(𝔐) ≅ ρ̄^ss|_{G_{K∞}}, semisimple of shape w̃ ∈ Adm^∨(η) by Theorem 3.3.12; conclude by Proposition 3.4.2 and Table 2 (all Σ_x, x ∈ Adm(η), are nonempty). If τ is not 3-generic, Proposition 3.4.5 (n = 6) rules out such a lift. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Proposition 3.4.5 — genericity of types of lifts
items.statement: Let n ≥ 4 and assume that ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F) is n-generic. Assume that ρ̄ arises as the reduction of a potentially crystalline representation of type (η, τ) where τ is a 1-generic tame inertial type. Then τ is (n−3)-generic.
items.note: Proof: by Lemma 3.3.10 reduce to ρ̄ semisimple; then [LLHL19, Proposition 3.3.2]. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [LLHL19, Proposition 3.3.2] — genericity of the type of a lift of a semisimple ρ̄
items.statement: (As used.) If ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F) is semisimple and n-generic (n ≥ 4) and has a potentially crystalline lift of type (η, τ) with τ 1-generic tame, then τ is (n−3)-generic.
items.note: Cited. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Unrestricted universal framed deformation ring R^□_ṽ
items.statement: For a finite set S, finite extensions F_ṽ/Q_p (ṽ ∈ S; not necessarily unramified in Definition 3.5.1) with residue fields k_ṽ, and a collection ρ̄_S = (ρ̄_ṽ)_{ṽ∈S} of continuous representations ρ̄_ṽ : G_{F_ṽ} → GL3(F), R^□_ṽ = R^□_{ρ̄_ṽ} denotes the unrestricted universal framed deformation ring of ρ̄_ṽ (over O).
items.note: Planned: LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1 plans framed local deformation rings.

items.name: Patched ring R_∞ = (⊗̂_{ṽ∈S} R^□_ṽ)[[x_1,…,x_h]] and X_∞ = Spf R_∞
items.statement: Fix a natural number h and let R_∞ := (⊗̂_{ṽ∈S} R^□_ṽ)[[x_1, x_2, …, x_h]] (completed tensor product over O of the complete local Noetherian O-algebras R^□_ṽ, all with residue field F) and X_∞ := Spf R_∞. R̄^□_ṽ, R̄_∞, … denote reductions modulo ϖ.
items.note: Rewritten: the checkpoint's statement ('construct the category of complete Noetherian local O-algebras … completed tensor products and their Noetherian/locality theorems') is background the paper uses without stating; the object actually constructed at this locator is R_∞. The standard facts that ⊗̂ of complete local Noetherian O-algebras with residue field F is again complete local Noetherian with residue field F are used implicitly. Planned: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1 plans complete local coefficient rings and completed tensor products.
items.proofOutline: Owned construction, not an acquired proof; R03.1 covers precisely these coefficient operations.

api.name: complete_tensor
api.statement: Construct the completed coefficient tensor with its maps.

api.name: power_series
api.statement: Adjoin formal patching variables.

unitTests: With no factors retain O.
An O factor does not change a completed tensor.
A noncontinuous homomorphism is not a coefficient morphism.

items.name: Framed deformation ring R^{τ_ṽ}_ṽ of inertial type τ_ṽ and Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0)
items.statement: If τ_ṽ is an inertial type for G_{F_ṽ}, R^{τ_ṽ}_ṽ = R^{τ_ṽ}_{ρ̄_ṽ} is the universal framed deformation ring of ρ̄_ṽ of inertial type τ_ṽ and (parallel) Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0).
items.note: As printed the definition does not say 'potentially crystalline'; everywhere else (Remark 3.3.13, proof of Theorem 3.5.3) it is the potentially crystalline ring of type (η, τ): Kisin's [Kis08] reduced, p-torsion-free quotient of R^□_ṽ whose Q̄_p-points are the potentially crystalline lifts of Hodge type η and inertial type τ_ṽ; it may be 0. Its dimension, when nonzero, is given by [Kis08, Theorem 3.3.4] (see cite-Kis08-thm-3-3-4). R̄^τ_ρ̄ := R^τ_ρ̄/ϖ. Planned: LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 plans fixed labeled Hodge-type and inertial-type potentially semistable deformation rings in every rank, with bounded-height lattice moduli and minimally ramified conditions.
items.proofOutline: LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 already owns arbitrary-rank rings and dimensions. No direct entry for that roadmap was found in the reviewed audit; direct library searches found no Kisin deformation-ring construction.

api.name: type_point
api.statement: Characteristic-zero points have the specified Hodge and inertial type.

api.name: type_quotient
api.statement: The type ring is a quotient of the framed ring.

unitTests: Incompatible determinant data can give the zero ring.
A point of wrong Hodge type is excluded.
Framing changes the deformation problem.

items.name: R_∞(τ_S) and X_∞(τ_S)
items.statement: For τ_S = (τ_ṽ)_{ṽ∈S}, R_∞(τ_S) := (⊗̂_{ṽ∈S} R^{τ_ṽ}_ṽ) ⊗_{⊗̂_{ṽ∈S} R^□_ṽ} R_∞ and X_∞(τ_S) := Spf R_∞(τ_S). (Thus R_∞(τ_S) = (⊗̂_ṽ R^{τ_ṽ}_ṽ)[[x_1,…,x_h]] is a quotient of R_∞.)
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The integer d (dim X_∞(τ_S) = d + 1)
items.statement: Let d + 1 be the dimension of X_∞(τ_S); it is independent of τ_S.
items.note: Independence by [Kis08, Theorem 3.3.4] (for those τ_S with X_∞(τ_S) nonempty). d is the dimension of the special fibres R̄_∞(τ_S). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [Kis08, Theorem 3.3.4] — dimension of potentially crystalline framed deformation rings
items.statement: (As used.) If nonzero, the framed potentially crystalline deformation ring R^{τ}_{ρ̄} of ρ̄ : G_{F_ṽ} → GL_n(F) of inertial type τ and regular Hodge type (here (2,1,0)) is equidimensional of dimension 1 + n^2 + [F_ṽ:Q_p]·n(n−1)/2, and R^{τ}_{ρ̄}[1/p] is regular. Consequently dim X_∞(τ_S) does not depend on τ_S.
items.locator: §3.5.1, p. 37; regularity of R_∞(τ_S)[1/p] used in Definition 3.5.1(4)
items.note: Cited; the dimension formula and regularity are the content of Kisin's theorem as used here, not printed in the paper. Planned: LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3 plans Kisin's potentially semistable deformation rings with fixed Hodge and inertial type and their dimension.

items.name: K_ṽ = GL3(O_{F_ṽ}) and K = ∏_ṽ K_ṽ
items.statement: K_ṽ := GL3(O_{F_ṽ}) and K := ∏_{ṽ∈S} K_ṽ.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: σ(τ_ṽ) (inertial local Langlands) and σ(τ_S) = ⊗_ṽ σ(τ_ṽ)
items.statement: Results toward the inertial local Langlands correspondence (Proposition 2.2.6(2); [CEG+16, Theorem 3.7]) associate a Q̄_p-valued K_ṽ-representation σ(τ_ṽ) to a 1-generic tame inertial type τ_ṽ, realizable over O; for 1-generic tame τ_ṽ = τ(s,μ+η) one can take σ(τ_ṽ) = R_s(μ+η). σ(τ_S) := ⊗_{ṽ∈S} σ(τ_ṽ), a K-representation.
items.note: Definition 3.5.1(1) uses σ(τ_ṽ) for arbitrary inertial types, via [CEG+16, Theorem 3.7] as in §2.2. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Definition 3.5.1 — weak minimal patching functor
items.statement: Let Rep_K(O) be the category of continuous K-representations on finitely generated O-modules and Mod(X_∞) the category of coherent sheaves on X_∞. A weak minimal patching functor for ρ̄_S = (ρ̄_ṽ)_{ṽ∈S} is a nonzero covariant exact functor M_∞ : Rep_K(O) → Mod(X_∞) satisfying: (1) for each ṽ ∈ S let τ_ṽ be an inertial type for G_{F_ṽ} and σ(τ_S) := ⊗_{ṽ∈S} σ(τ_ṽ); if σ(τ_S)° is an O-lattice in σ(τ_S), then M_∞(σ(τ_S)°) is p-torsion-free and maximally Cohen–Macaulay over R_∞(τ_S); (2) if M_∞(R_1(μ)) is nonzero, then ρ̄_ṽ has a semistable lift of type τ_ṽ(1, μ_ṽ) for all ṽ ∈ S; (3) if σ is an irreducible ∏_{ṽ∈S} GL3(k_ṽ)-representation over F, then M_∞(σ) is either 0 or maximal Cohen–Macaulay over its support, which is equidimensional of dimension d; (4) the locally free sheaf M_∞(σ(τ_S)°)[1/p] (maximal Cohen–Macaulay over the regular ring R_∞(τ_S)[1/p]) has rank at most one on each connected component.
items.note: Rewritten exactly. Corrections to the checkpoint's statement: axiom (1) is for arbitrary inertial types τ_ṽ (not only tame ones); axiom (2) concerns the Deligne–Lusztig representation R_1(μ) (principal series), whose type is τ(1, μ). F_ṽ need not be unramified here. Imprecisions (issue list): in (2) M_∞ is only defined on O-lattices, so 'M_∞(R_1(μ))' means M_∞ of a lattice in R_1(μ), and 'semistable lift of type τ(1,μ)' means potentially semistable of Hodge type η and inertial type τ(1,μ). Compare [LLHLM18, Definition 7.11] (corrected in §6(11)). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).
items.proofOutline: Keep this arithmetic functor distinct from the already-owned abstract inverse-limit patching construction R03.5. Its global existence is G05.

api.name: patch_exact
api.statement: Short exact sequences of finite K-modules remain exact.

api.name: patch_type_mcm
api.statement: A type lattice maps to a p-torsion-free MCM module.

api.name: patch_rank_bound
api.statement: Generic component rank is at most one.

unitTests: The zero functor is excluded.
A nonzero MCM module on just one component is not automatically faithful.
A patching functor must preserve the nonsplit length-two exact sequence used in 5.1.5.

items.name: W^BM(ρ̄_S) — weights detected by a weak minimal patching functor
items.statement: Assume a weak minimal patching functor M_∞ for ρ̄_S exists. Following [GHS18, Definition 3.2.6], W^BM(ρ̄_S) is the set of irreducible representations σ of G := ∏_{ṽ∈S} GL3(k_ṽ) over F such that M_∞(σ) is nonzero. (A priori this set depends on the choice of M_∞.)
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).
items.proofOutline: Separate the definition from T35, which proves independence under its genericity and semisimplicity hypotheses.

api.name: patch_support_mem
api.statement: Membership is precisely nonvanishing of the patched weight module.

api.name: patch_support_mult
api.statement: Under axiom (3), membership is equivalent to positive fixed-dimension multiplicity.

unitTests: The zero weight module contributes no weight.
A nonzero pure d-dimensional MCM module contributes its weight.
Functor independence is not part of the definition.

items.name: Multiplicity e(M) in the fixed dimension d
items.statement: For a finitely generated R_∞-module M with scheme-theoretic support Spec A of dimension at most d, e(M) is d! times the coefficient of the degree-d term of the Hilbert polynomial of M (considered as an A-module). In particular e(M) is the Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity of M as an A-module when dim A = d, and is 0 otherwise.
items.note: 'Hilbert polynomial' means the Hilbert–Samuel polynomial n ↦ length(M/𝔪^n M) (of degree dim Supp M). e is additive in short exact sequences of modules of dimension ≤ d, which is how it is used with exact M_∞. This is the corrected definition that §6(12) substitutes for the one before [LLHLM18, Prop. 7.14] (issue E112). The paper also writes e(R̄^τ_ρ̄), e(R̃^τ_ρ̄), e(R̄^τ_ρ̄[[X_1,…,X_{3f}]]) in the proof of Theorem 3.5.3, where e must mean the Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity in the ring's own dimension (see sourceIssues). Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).
items.proofOutline: Develop the Hilbert polynomial and additivity under R03.3; do not use the usual multiplicity in the module’s own dimension for every M.

api.name: multiplicity_low_dimension
api.statement: Support dimension below d implies e_d=0.

api.name: multiplicity_exact
api.statement: e_d is additive in finite short exact sequences.

unitTests: A finite-length module contributes zero when d>0.
For d=0 the invariant is its length.
For an exact sequence of equal-dimensional modules the leading coefficients add.

items.name: Theorem 3.5.2 — numerical Breuil–Mézard for weak minimal patching functors
items.statement: Assume F_ṽ/Q_p is unramified for all ṽ ∈ S. Suppose that ρ̄_S is semisimple and 10-generic and that M_∞ is a weak [minimal] patching functor for ρ̄_S. Then for all Serre weights σ, e(M_∞(σ)) = 1 if σ ∈ W?(ρ̄_S) and e(M_∞(σ)) = 0 otherwise.
items.note: Proof: M_∞ ≠ 0 gives σ ∈ W^BM(ρ̄_S) ⊂ W?(ρ̄_S) (Prop. 3.5.6); by Lemma 3.5.12 and induction on the defect there is such σ of defect 0; conclude by Lemma 3.5.11. 'weak patching functor' in the statement means Definition 3.5.1. Rewritten with the unramifiedness hypothesis, which is a standing assumption stated just before the theorem. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).
items.proofOutline: Eliminate extraneous weights via generic lifts and §2.3.13; descend positive defect by the difference 2^(delta+1)−2^delta; propagate from an obvious weight using §3.5.9–12. The full type construction and weight recipe remain G01/G04/G05.

items.name: Theorem 3.5.2 (final assertion) — W^BM(ρ̄_S) = W?(ρ̄_S)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 3.5.2 (F_ṽ unramified, ρ̄_S semisimple and 10-generic, M_∞ a weak minimal patching functor for ρ̄_S), W^BM(ρ̄_S) = W?(ρ̄_S); in particular W^BM(ρ̄_S) does not depend on the choice of M_∞.
items.note: Immediate from T34 (and Proposition 3.5.6). Independence of M_∞ is the evident consequence, not printed as such. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).
items.proofOutline: Use the pure-dimensional MCM axiom: a nonzero weight module has positive dimension-d multiplicity, so multiplicity zero cannot conceal a nonzero lower-dimensional module.

items.name: Theorem 3.5.3 (first assertion) — non-1-generic types give zero rings
items.statement: Let K/Q_p be a finite unramified extension of degree f, ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F) a continuous, 10-generic and semisimple representation, and τ a tame inertial type. If τ is not 1-generic, then R^τ_ρ̄ = 0.
items.note: Proof: reduce by unramified base change to τ principal series; by [LLHL19, Remark 2.2.8] τ is not 2-generic and ρ̄ is 10-generic in the sense of [Enn, Definition 2.2]; then [Enn, Proposition 7] excludes potentially crystalline lifts of type τ and Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0). The claims that unramified restriction preserves 'not 1-generic' and '10-generic' are asserted without proof. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).
items.proofOutline: Uses Enns weight elimination; original theorem and proof are G04.

items.name: Theorem 3.5.3 — number of components of R̄^τ_ρ̄ equals #W?(ρ̄, τ)
items.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite unramified of degree f, ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F) continuous, 10-generic and semisimple, and τ a 1-generic tame inertial type. Then the number of irreducible components of R̄^τ_ρ̄ := R^τ_ρ̄/ϖ equals #W?(ρ̄, τ) (in particular R^τ_ρ̄ = 0 if and only if W?(ρ̄, τ) = ∅).
items.note: Proof: R^τ_ρ̄ ≠ 0 ⟺ W?(ρ̄,τ) ≠ ∅ (thm-3-5-3-nonvanishing); when nonzero, (3.5) e(R̄^τ_ρ̄) = e(M_∞(σ̄(τ)°)) = #W?(ρ̄,τ) (Theorem 3.5.2 with the patching functor of Proposition 3.5.15) together with the comparison ring R̃^τ_ρ̄ and [LLHLM18, Lemma 8.8] gives the component count. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).
items.proofOutline: Match the multiplicity-one weights from T34 to reduced components of the explicit charts; emptiness uses the lift/weight equivalence of §§3.4–3.5, still part of G04.

items.name: Theorem 3.5.3 — R^τ_ρ̄ is a normal domain
items.statement: (As printed.) Let K/Q_p be finite unramified of degree f, ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F) continuous, 10-generic and semisimple, and τ a tame inertial type. The ring R^τ_ρ̄ is a normal domain. (Correct form: if τ is 1-generic and R^τ_ρ̄ ≠ 0, equivalently W?(ρ̄,τ) ≠ ∅, then R^τ_ρ̄ is a normal domain.)
items.note: The printed statement is false when R^τ_ρ̄ = 0 (τ not 1-generic, or W?(ρ̄,τ) = ∅): issue E04. Proof in the nonzero case: R̄^τ_ρ̄ reduced, R^τ_ρ̄ flat over O with R^τ_ρ̄[1/p] regular ⇒ normal, and local ⇒ domain (proof of [LLHLM18, Corollary 8.9]). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).
items.proofOutline: The proof explicitly treats nonzero rings and matches them with reduced equidimensional explicit charts using multiplicities. The zero ring is not a domain. Do not infer normality merely from special-fibre reducedness.

items.name: Theorem 3.5.3 — R^τ_ρ̄ is Cohen–Macaulay
items.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite unramified, ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F) continuous, 10-generic and semisimple, τ a tame inertial type. Then R^τ_ρ̄ is Cohen–Macaulay.
items.note: Nontrivial only when R^τ_ρ̄ ≠ 0; then it follows from R̄^τ_ρ̄[[X_1,…,X_{3f}]] ≅ R̃^τ_ρ̄ being Cohen–Macaulay and ϖ being a nonzerodivisor (proof of [LLHLM18, Cor. 8.9]). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).
items.proofOutline: Identify the nonzero ring with its explicit chart, and prove Cohen–Macaulayness shape by shape. G04 retains the original chart proofs.

items.name: Theorem 3.5.3 — R̄^τ_ρ̄ is reduced
items.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite unramified, ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F) continuous, 10-generic and semisimple, τ a tame inertial type. Then R̄^τ_ρ̄ = R^τ_ρ̄/ϖ is reduced.
items.note: From R̄^τ_ρ̄[[X_1,…,X_{3f}]] ≅ R̃^τ_ρ̄, which is reduced by the argument of Lemma 3.5.4. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).
items.proofOutline: Numerical Breuil–Mézard and explicit charts establish the reduced special-fibre presentation, not just its set of points.

items.name: Theorem 3.5.3 — components of R̄^τ_ρ̄ are formally smooth of the same dimension
items.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite unramified, ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F) continuous, 10-generic and semisimple, τ a tame inertial type. Then the irreducible components of R̄^τ_ρ̄ are formally smooth over F and all of the same dimension.
items.note: From the corresponding property of R̃^τ_ρ̄ (completed tensor product of rings whose components are smooth). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).
items.proofOutline: Use the explicit prime quotients of the shape charts. Proving that their completed tensor products preserve the asserted properties is part of G04.

items.name: Lemma 3.5.4 (claim in proof) — structure of R̄^τ_ρ̄ for shapes of length ≥ 2
items.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite unramified of degree f, ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F) semisimple, τ 5-generic with lowest alcove presentation (s, μ), and assume V(ρ̄|_{I_K}) = R_{s w̃^*}(μ+η) where w̃ = w̃(ρ̄, τ) = (w̃_0,…,w̃_{f−1}) ∈ Adm^∨(η) with ℓ(w̃_j) > 1 for every j. Then R̄^τ_ρ̄ is the completion, at the maximal ideal generated by the variables, of a tensor product over F of rings of the form F[X] and F[X,Y]/(XY), and #Irr(Spec R̄^τ_ρ̄) = ∏_j 2^{4−ℓ(w̃_j)}.
items.note: From the explicit presentations of [LLHLM18, Sections 5.3, 6, Table 7] (valid for ℓ(w̃_j) ≥ 2 and τ 5-generic); 𝔐_ρ̄ is semisimple (Prop. 3.3.9, Thm 3.3.12), hence in the 'special locus' of its shape. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Lemma 3.5.4 — nonvanishing and component count for shapes of length ≥ 2
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 3.5.4 (K/Q_p finite unramified of degree f; ρ̄ semisimple; τ 5-generic with lowest alcove presentation (s, μ); V(ρ̄|_{I_K}) = R_{s w̃^*}(μ+η) with w̃ = w̃(ρ̄,τ) ∈ Adm^∨(η), ℓ(w̃_j) > 1 for every j): R̄^τ_ρ̄ ≠ 0 and the number of irreducible components of R̄^τ_ρ̄ equals #W?(ρ̄, τ).
items.note: Proof: #W?(ρ̄,τ) = ∏_j #Σ_{w̃^*_j} by Proposition 3.4.2, and Table 2 gives #Σ_x = 2^{4−ℓ(x)} for ℓ(x) ∈ {2,3,4} (not for ℓ ≤ 1: #Σ_α = #Σ_id = 6). Checked against Table 2. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Lemma 3.5.4 — R̄^τ_ρ̄ reduced, Cohen–Macaulay, components formally smooth of equal dimension
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 3.5.4, R̄^τ_ρ̄ is reduced and Cohen–Macaulay, and its irreducible components are formally smooth of the same dimension.
items.note: Proof: the tensor product of copies of F[X], F[X,Y]/XY is Cohen–Macaulay, reduced and excellent with smooth components; completion preserves CM [Sta19, Tag 07NX] and reducedness [Sta19, Tag 07NZ], and completions of the (smooth) components stay irreducible and formally smooth. Cohen–Macaulayness of R̄^τ_ρ̄ is stated in the proof, not in the lemma. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Lemma 3.5.4 — R^τ_ρ̄ is a Cohen–Macaulay normal domain
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 3.5.4, the ring R^τ_ρ̄ is a normal domain and is Cohen–Macaulay.
items.note: 'This implies the remaining properties (see the proof of [LLHLM18, Corollary 8.9]). Note that the reducedness of R̄^τ_ρ̄ implies that R^τ_ρ̄ is a normal domain.' (Uses also that R^τ_ρ̄ is O-flat with regular generic fibre [Kis08].) Here R^τ_ρ̄ ≠ 0, so no zero-ring problem. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: [LLHLM18, §§5.3, 6, Table 7] — explicit presentations of R^τ_ρ̄ for shapes of length ≥ 2
items.statement: (As used.) For τ 5-generic and w̃(ρ̄,τ) with ℓ(w̃_j) ≥ 2 for all j, [LLHLM18] gives an explicit presentation of R^τ_ρ̄; for each shape there are at most two cases depending on 𝔐_ρ̄, and in the 'special locus' (𝔐_ρ̄ semisimple) R̄^τ_ρ̄ is (up to formally smooth factors) the completed tensor product over j of F[[X]] or F[[X,Y]]/(XY)-type factors with 2^{4−ℓ(w̃_j)} components in embedding j.
items.locator: §3.5.2, proof of Lemma 3.5.4, p. 39; Remark 3.3.13, p. 34
items.note: Cited, not proved here. Also gives nonvanishing of R^τ_ρ̄ for such shapes (Remark 3.3.13). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: [Sta19, Tag 07NX] — Cohen–Macaulayness passes to the completion
items.statement: (As used.) A Noetherian local ring is Cohen–Macaulay if (and only if) its 𝔪-adic completion is Cohen–Macaulay.
items.note: Cited. Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).

items.name: [Sta19, Tag 07NZ] — completion of a reduced excellent local ring is reduced
items.statement: (As used.) If A is a reduced excellent Noetherian local ring (e.g. a localization of a finite type F-algebra), then its completion is reduced.
items.note: Cited. Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).

items.name: Proof of [LLHLM18, Corollary 8.9] — normality from reduced special fibre
items.statement: (As used.) If R is a complete local Noetherian O-algebra, flat over O, with R[1/p] regular and R/ϖ reduced (and, in the cases at hand, Cohen–Macaulay), then R is a Cohen–Macaulay normal domain.
items.locator: §3.5.2, proof of Lemma 3.5.4, p. 39; proof of Theorem 3.5.3, p. 46
items.note: Cited; the argument is not reproduced. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Corollary 3.5.5 — e(R̄_∞(τ_S)) = #W?(ρ̄_S, τ_S)
items.statement: Suppose that for each ṽ ∈ S, ρ̄_ṽ : G_{F_ṽ} → GL3(F) is a semisimple Galois representation and τ_ṽ is a 5-generic tame inertial type satisfying the hypotheses of Lemma 3.5.4. Let τ_S = (τ_ṽ)_{ṽ∈S}. Then e(R̄_∞(τ_S)) = #W?(ρ̄_S, τ_S).
items.note: Proof: Lemma 3.5.4 (e(R̄^{τ_ṽ}_ṽ) = number of components, as R̄^{τ_ṽ}_ṽ is reduced with formally smooth equidimensional components), [EG14, Lemma 2.2.14] (multiplicativity for completed tensor products) and W?(ρ̄_S,τ_S) = ∏_ṽ W?(ρ̄_ṽ,τ_ṽ). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [EG14, Lemma 2.2.14] — multiplicities of completed tensor products
items.statement: (As used.) Hilbert–Samuel multiplicities are multiplicative for completed tensor products over F of complete local Noetherian F-algebras (and unchanged by adjoining formal power series variables).
items.note: Cited. Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).

items.name: Proposition 3.5.6 — weight elimination for W^BM
items.statement: Suppose that for each ṽ, ρ̄_ṽ : G_{F_ṽ} → GL3(F) is a 10-generic Galois representation (F_ṽ unramified), and let M_∞ be a weak minimal patching functor for ρ̄_S. Then W^BM(ρ̄_S) ⊂ W?(ρ̄^ss_S).
items.note: Proof: W^BM satisfies [Enn, Axiom (WE)] by Definition 3.5.1(2); by [Enn, Thm 8] and [LLHL19, Rem. 2.2.8] any σ ∈ W^BM lies in JH(σ̄(τ_S)) for 1-generic τ_S; Prop. 3.4.5 and Def. 3.5.1(1) force τ_S 7-generic, so σ is 5-deep (Lemma 4.2.13, proved in §4 independently of §3); if σ ∉ W?(ρ̄^ss_S), Corollary 2.3.13 gives τ_S with σ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_S)) and W?(ρ̄^ss_S,τ_S) = ∅; Prop. 3.4.4 and Lemma 3.3.10 (cited as 'Proposition 3.3.10') give X_∞(τ_S) = ∅, so M_∞(σ(τ_S)°) = 0 and M_∞(σ) = 0 by exactness. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [Enn, Theorem 8, Axiom (WE)] — Enns' weight elimination
items.statement: (As used.) If a set W of Serre weights satisfies Enns' weight-elimination axiom [Enn, Axiom (WE)] (which W^BM(ρ̄_S) satisfies by Definition 3.5.1(2)) and ρ̄_S is 10-generic (translated to Enns' convention via [LLHL19, Remark 2.2.8]), then every σ ∈ W is '3-generic', so that σ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_S)) for some collection τ_S of 1-generic tame types (e.g. a tame principal series type containing σ).
items.note: Cited; the content of Axiom (WE) is not restated in LLHLM20 ('3-generic' for a Serre weight is not defined in the paper). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark 3.5.7 — avoiding [Enn]
items.statement: Instead of appealing to [Enn], one can show, provided ρ̄_S is generic enough, that every element of W^BM(ρ̄_S) is a Jordan–Hölder factor of the reduction of some 1-generic tame type: every Serre weight occurs in the reduction of V_λ ⊗ σ(τ_S) for λ sufficiently large (independent of p); the results of §3.3 hold for potentially crystalline representations of type (λ_ṽ + η_ṽ, τ_ṽ)_{ṽ∈S} (possibly with stronger genericity); then the argument of Proposition 3.5.6 applies.
items.note: Sketch only; not used later. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: σ̄(τ_S)° — reduction of a lattice
items.statement: Given a collection τ_S of tame inertial types and an O-lattice σ(τ_S)° in σ(τ_S), σ̄(τ_S)° denotes the reduction of σ(τ_S)° modulo ϖ.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 3.5.8 — e(M_∞(σ̄(τ_S)°)) is 0 or e(R̄_∞(τ_S))
items.statement: Suppose that for each ṽ ∈ S, ρ̄_ṽ : G_{F_ṽ} → GL3(F) is a semisimple Galois representation and τ_ṽ is a 5-generic tame inertial type satisfying the hypotheses of Lemma 3.5.4. Let τ_S = (τ_ṽ)_{ṽ∈S} and let σ(τ_S)° be an O-lattice in σ(τ_S). Then either M_∞(σ̄(τ_S)°) = 0 or e(M_∞(σ̄(τ_S)°)) = e(R̄_∞(τ_S)), and the alternative does not depend on the lattice.
items.note: Proof: the generic fibre of X_∞(τ_S) is irreducible since its special fibre is reduced (Lemma 3.5.4; R_∞(τ_S) is then a normal domain); M_∞(σ(τ_S)°) is MCM over X_∞(τ_S), so has full support or is 0; conclude with the proof of [LLHLM18, Prop. 7.14] and Definition 3.5.1(4) (generic rank ≤ 1). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Proof of [LLHLM18, Proposition 7.14] as used — multiplicity bound from rank ≤ 1
items.statement: (As used.) If M is a p-torsion-free maximal Cohen–Macaulay module over R_∞(τ_S) whose generic fibre has rank ≤ 1 on each component, then e(M/ϖ) ≤ e(R̄_∞(τ_S)), with equality when M has full support and R_∞(τ_S) is a domain.
items.locator: §3.5.2, proof of Lemma 3.5.8, p. 40; proof of Theorem 3.5.3, p. 46
items.note: Cited; with the corrected e of §6(12). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The type τ_S attached to w̃ ∈ Adm(η) (proof of Lemma 3.5.9)
items.statement: Suppose V(ρ̄_S|_{I_{F_S}}) = R_s(μ) with μ − η 7-deep in C_0, and label W?(ρ̄_S) by r(Σ) as in Proposition 2.3.4. For w̃ = (w̃_ṽ)_{ṽ∈S} = (w̃_i)_{i∈𝒥} ∈ Adm(η) with image w ∈ W_𝒥, let τ_S be the tame inertial type with lowest alcove presentation (s w^{−1}, μ + s w̃^{−1}(0) − η) (so σ(τ_S) = R_{s w̃^{−1}}(μ)). Then μ + s w̃^{−1}(0) − η is 5-deep in C_0, so τ_S is 5-generic.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: W?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) for the type attached to w̃ ∈ Adm(η)
items.statement: In the situation of constr-type-tau-w, W?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) = {σ^{(s,μ)}_{r(ω,a)} : r(ω,a) ∈ ∏_{i∈𝒥} r(Σ_{w̃_i^{−1}})}, where Σ_{w̃_i^{−1}} = Σ_0 ∩ w̃_i^{−1}(r(Σ_0)). If ℓ(w̃_i) > 1 for all i, τ_S satisfies the hypotheses of Corollary 3.5.5 (with w̃(ρ̄_S, τ_S) = w̃^*, using ℓ(w̃) = ℓ(w̃^*) by the proof of [LLHL19, Lemma 2.1.3]).
items.note: By Corollary 2.3.11 (first part). Checked: R_{sw^{−1}w̃}(μ+s w̃^{−1}(0)) = R_s(μ), so the shape is w̃^*. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Table 2 facts used for minimal types
items.statement: (a) For each (ω_i, a_i) ∈ Σ^obv_0 there is w̃_i ∈ Adm((2,1,0)) with ℓ(w̃_i) = 4 (a translation) and Σ_{w̃_i^{−1}} = {(ω_i, a_i)}. (b) For each (ω_i, a_i) ∈ Σ^inn_0 there is w̃_i with w̃_i t_{−1̲} ∈ {αβα, βγ^+β, αγ^+α} (length 3) such that Σ_{w̃_i^{−1}} = {(ω_i,a_i), r(ω_i,a_i)}. (c) If ℓ(w̃_{j_0}) = 3 is as in (b) and w̃′_{j_0} ≤ w̃_{j_0} has length 2, then Σ_{w̃_{j_0}^{−1}} ⊂ Σ_{w̃′_{j_0}^{−1}}, the latter has 4 elements, and Σ_{w̃′_{j_0}^{−1}} ∖ Σ_{w̃_{j_0}^{−1}} ⊂ Σ^obv_0. (d) Each of the six pairs of adjacent elements of Σ^obv_0 (Table 1) is Σ_{w̃′^{−1}} for some length-3 nonshadow element w̃′ ([LLHLM18, Table 1]).
items.note: Read off Table 2 and the order-three symmetry. Checked: translations give the six obvious singletons; αβα gives {(0,1),(0,0)}; βα, αβ give 4-element sets containing it; βαγ^+, αβγ^+ give adjacent obvious pairs. The paper prints βγβ, αγα (γ the antidominant generator) in (b): misprint for γ^+. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 3.5.9 (1)–(3) — minimal types and their one-step enlargements
items.statement: Suppose that ρ̄_ṽ : G_{F_ṽ} → GL3(F) is semisimple and 7-generic for all ṽ ∈ S. If σ ∈ W?(ρ̄_S) has defect δ, then there are tame inertial types τ_ṽ and τ′_ṽ satisfying the hypotheses of Corollary 3.5.5 such that, with τ_S = (τ_ṽ)_{ṽ∈S} and τ′_S = (τ′_ṽ)_{ṽ∈S}: (1) σ ∈ W?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) ⊂ W?(ρ̄_S, τ′_S); (2) #W?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) = 2^δ and #W?(ρ̄_S, τ′_S) = 2^{δ+1}; (3) all Serre weights in W?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) and W?(ρ̄_S, τ′_S) have defect at most δ, and if δ > 0, σ is the unique Serre weight in W?(ρ̄_S, τ′_S) with defect δ.
items.note: Proof: write σ = σ^{(s,μ)}_{r(ω,a)}; choose w̃_i by fact-table2-singletons-pairs (a)/(b) according as (ω_i,a_i) is obvious or inner, giving τ_S (constr-type-tau-w); for δ > 0 replace one length-3 component w̃_{j_0} by a length-2 w̃′_{j_0} ≤ w̃_{j_0} to get τ′_S with σ(τ′_S) = R_{s(w̃′)^{−1}}(μ). Checked. The defect is the number of components i with (ω_i,a_i) ∈ Σ^inn_0 (Definition 2.3.8). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 3.5.9 (4) — a type containing exactly two adjacent obvious weights
items.statement: Suppose ρ̄_ṽ is semisimple and 7-generic for all ṽ ∈ S and σ ∈ W?(ρ̄_S) has defect 0. For any σ′ ∈ W?(ρ̄_S) of defect 0 which is adjacent to σ, the type τ′_S of Lemma 3.5.9 (satisfying the hypotheses of Corollary 3.5.5 and (1)–(3)) can be chosen so that W?(ρ̄_S, τ′_S) = {σ, σ′}.
items.note: Proof: σ, σ′ differ in exactly one component j_0, where they form one of the six adjacent obvious pairs; take w̃′_{j_0} of length 3 nonshadow with Σ_{w̃′_{j_0}^{−1}} equal to that pair (printed 'Σ_{w̃_j^{−1}}', misprint), w̃′_i = w̃_i otherwise. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark 3.5.10 — minimal type of σ with respect to ρ̄
items.statement: The type τ_S constructed in Lemma 3.5.9 is uniquely characterized by requiring σ ∈ W?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) and #W?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) = 2^δ (δ the defect of σ); it is called the minimal type of σ with respect to ρ̄.
items.note: Uniqueness 'from Table 2': the product of the #Σ_{w̃_i^{−1}} is 2^δ only if obvious components are singletons and inner components are the unique 2-element sets containing them; implicitly among types with W?(ρ̄_S,τ_S) ≠ ∅, which come from Adm(η). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Reductions of 3-generic tame types are multiplicity free
items.statement: If τ_S is a 3-generic tame type, then σ̄(τ_S)° is multiplicity free for any choice of lattice σ(τ_S)°.
items.note: Asserted without proof or reference ('We observe that'); it follows from the generic decomposition pattern of Jantzen's formula used in Propositions 2.3.4–2.3.7 (9^{#𝒥} distinct constituents, each once). See issue list. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: e(M_∞(σ̄(τ_S)°)) as a sum over predicted weights
items.statement: Let ρ̄_S be 10-generic (so that Proposition 3.5.6 applies), M_∞ a weak minimal patching functor for ρ̄_S, and τ_S a 3-generic tame type with lattice σ(τ_S)°. Then e(M_∞(σ̄(τ_S)°)) = Σ_{σ∈JH(σ̄(τ_S))} e(M_∞(σ)) = Σ_{σ∈W?(ρ̄^ss_S, τ_S)} e(M_∞(σ)).
items.note: First equality: exactness of M_∞, additivity of e in dimension d (Definition 3.5.1(3)) and multiplicity-freeness; second: Proposition 3.5.6. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: W?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) ≠ ∅ ⇒ τ_S 7-generic (as asserted)
items.statement: If ρ̄_S is 10-generic and W?(ρ̄_S, τ_S) is nonempty (τ_S a 1-generic tame type), then τ_S is 7-generic.
items.note: Justified in the paper 'by Proposition 3.4.5', which needs a potentially crystalline lift of type (η,τ_S), not W? ≠ ∅; see sourceIssues. In its only use (Lemma 3.5.11) the type comes from Lemma 3.5.9, which is 8-generic by construction. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 3.5.11 — one defect-0 weight forces multiplicity one everywhere
items.statement: Suppose that ρ̄_ṽ : G_{F_ṽ} → GL3(F) is semisimple and 10-generic for all ṽ ∈ S (F_ṽ unramified), and let M_∞ be a weak minimal patching functor for ρ̄_S. If there exists σ ∈ W^BM(ρ̄_S) with defect 0, then e(M_∞(σ′)) = 1 for all σ′ ∈ W?(ρ̄_S).
items.note: Proof: for defect-0 σ′ induct on d_gph(σ,σ′), using the minimal type (W? = {σ}) and the types of Lemma 3.5.9(4) with Corollary 3.5.5 and Lemma 3.5.8 (e = 1, resp. 2); then induct on the defect using Lemma 3.5.9(2),(3) (e = 2^δ, and 2^δ − 1 lower-defect weights each with e = 1). Uses fact-defect-zero-geodesic. Checked. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 3.5.11 ('In particular') — W^BM(ρ̄_S) = W?(ρ̄_S)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 3.5.11, if some σ ∈ W^BM(ρ̄_S) has defect 0, then W^BM(ρ̄_S) = W?(ρ̄_S).
items.note: ⊇ from e = 1; ⊆ from Proposition 3.5.6. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Geodesics between defect-0 predicted weights stay among defect-0 weights
items.statement: If σ, σ′ ∈ W?(ρ̄_S) both have defect 0 and d := d_gph(σ, σ′) > 0, then there is σ″ ∈ W?(ρ̄_S) of defect 0, adjacent to σ′, with d_gph(σ, σ″) = d − 1.
items.note: Asserted without proof. True: the extension graph is the Cartesian product over 𝒥 of the one-component graphs (d_gph is a sum), and on Σ^obv_0 (a hexagon) the full-graph distance equals the hexagon distance (checked: opposite obvious vertices are at distance 3). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 3.5.12 — defect descent in W^BM
items.statement: Suppose that ρ̄_ṽ : G_{F_ṽ} → GL3(F) is semisimple and 10-generic for all ṽ ∈ S (F_ṽ unramified), and let M_∞ be a weak minimal patching functor for ρ̄_S. If σ ∈ W^BM(ρ̄_S) has defect δ > 0, then there exists σ′ ∈ W^BM(ρ̄_S) with defect less than δ.
items.note: Proof: with τ_S, τ′_S from Lemma 3.5.9, both M_∞(σ(τ_S)°), M_∞(σ(τ′_S)°) ≠ 0; e(M_∞(σ̄(τ′_S)°)) − e(M_∞(σ̄(τ_S)°)) = 2^{δ+1} − 2^δ = 2^δ > 0 is the sum of e(M_∞(σ′)) over W?(ρ̄_S,τ′_S) ∖ W?(ρ̄_S,τ_S), all of defect < δ. Misprints in the proof: first difference printed with τ′_S twice (E03), 'Proposition 3.5.9(1)' for Lemma 3.5.9(1). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark 3.5.13 — support of M_∞(σ) is a union of components
items.statement: The axioms for M_∞ imply that if σ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_S)), then the support of M_∞(σ) is a (possibly empty) union of irreducible components of Spec R̄_∞(τ_S).
items.note: From Definition 3.5.1(1),(3) (support equidimensional of dimension d = dim R̄_∞(τ_S)). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark 3.5.13 — for σ ∈ W^BM the support of M_∞(σ) is irreducible
items.statement: (In the setting of Theorem 3.5.2.) As Spec R_∞(τ_S) is the preimage of Spec ⊗̂_{ṽ∈S} R^{τ_ṽ}_ṽ ⊂ Spec ⊗̂_{ṽ∈S} R^□_ṽ inside Spec R_∞, if σ ∈ W^BM(ρ̄_S) then the scheme-theoretic support of M_∞(σ) is irreducible, with generic point the preimage in R_∞ of a prime ideal of ⊗̂_{ṽ∈S} R^□_ṽ.
items.note: 'We have shown': from e(M_∞(σ)) = 1 (Theorem 3.5.2) and rem-3-5-13-components. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Split ramification outside p; global hypotheses on r̄
items.statement: In the setup of [LLHLM18, §7.1] (CM field F/F^+, set Σ^+_p of places of F^+ above p, unitary group G_{/F^+}, isomorphisms ι_w; see also §5.3), r̄ : G_F → GL3(F) has split ramification outside p if whenever r̄ is ramified at a finite place w ∉ Σ_p of F, w|_{F^+} splits in F. The hypotheses used are: r̄ is automorphic (of some weight) in the sense of [LLHLM18, Definition 7.1]; r̄ satisfies the Taylor–Wiles hypotheses of [LLHLM18, Definition 7.3]; and r̄ has split ramification outside p.
items.note: 'Automorphic' and 'Taylor–Wiles' are imported definitions (the former corrected in §6(11)/(14)). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [LLHLM18, Proposition 7.15] — existence of a weak minimal patching functor M̃_∞ for r̄
items.statement: (As used.) If r̄ : G_F → GL3(F) is automorphic, satisfies the Taylor–Wiles hypotheses and has split ramification outside p, there is a weak minimal patching functor M̃_∞ for r̄ in the sense of [LLHLM18, Definition 7.11] (with an associated integer h).
items.note: Cited; see the §6 addendum items (11), (14) for corrections to [LLHLM18, Def. 7.11, Prop. 7.15]. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: S_p, ρ̄_{S_p} and the associated patching data
items.statement: For each v ∈ Σ^+_p choose a place ṽ of F above v; S_p := {ṽ : v ∈ Σ^+_p}; ρ̄_{S_p} := (ρ̄_ṽ)_{ṽ∈S_p} with ρ̄_ṽ := r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}} : G_{F_ṽ} → GL3(F). R_∞, R_∞(τ_{S_p}), … are defined as in §3.5.1 with the integer h of M̃_∞, and K := ∏_{S_p} K_ṽ.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Proposition 3.5.14 — global weak minimal patching functors
items.statement: In the setting of constr-S-p, let M_∞ : Rep_K(O) → Mod(X_∞) be the functor M̃_∞ ∘ ∏_{ṽ∈S_p} ι_ṽ. Then M_∞ is a weak minimal patching functor for ρ̄_{S_p}.
items.note: Proof: Definition 3.5.1(2) follows from the proof of [LLHL19, Proposition 4.2.6]; the remaining properties follow from the definitions and [LLHLM18, Proposition 7.15]. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Proof of [LLHL19, Proposition 4.2.6] as used — axiom (2) for global patching functors
items.statement: (As used.) For the patching functor M̃_∞ ∘ ∏ ι_ṽ attached to r̄, if M_∞(R_1(μ)) ≠ 0 then each ρ̄_ṽ has a (potentially) semistable lift of type τ_ṽ(1, μ_ṽ) (Hodge type η).
items.locator: §3.5.3, before and in the proof of Proposition 3.5.14, p. 44
items.note: Cited. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Setup for Proposition 3.5.15 — ρ̄ with a formally smooth potentially diagonalizable type
items.statement: Suppose p > 3 and K/Q_p is a finite extension. Let ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F) be a continuous representation with a potentially diagonalizable lift of type (η, τ) such that R^τ_ρ̄ is formally smooth. For example, if ρ̄ is 6-generic and semisimple, one can take τ with w̃(ρ̄, τ) = (w̃_j)_j satisfying ℓ(w̃_j) = 4 for all j.
items.note: The example is asserted without proof (formal smoothness from [LLHLM18, Table 7], potential diagonalizability not argued). With ρ̄ 6-generic the translated type is a priori only 4-generic, while Lemma 3.5.4 uses 5-genericity; harmless since Theorem 3.5.3 has ρ̄ 10-generic. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [EG14, Corollary A.7] — globalisation of local representations
items.statement: (As used.) Given ρ̄ as in def-setup-formally-smooth-type, there are a CM extension F/F^+, a choice of places S_p above Σ^+_p, and an automorphic r̄ : G_F → GL3(F) which satisfies the Taylor–Wiles hypotheses and has split ramification outside p, with K ≅ F_ṽ and r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}} ≅ ρ̄ for all ṽ ∈ S_p.
items.note: Cited. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).
