items.name: R_∞ for a single ρ̄ via globalisation
items.statement: Fix ṽ ∈ S_p (above v ∈ Σ^+_p) and let R_∞ := R^□_ρ̄ ⊗̂ ⊗̂_{v′∈Σ^+_p, v′≠v} R^τ_{ρ̄_{ṽ′}}[[x_1,…,x_h]], identified with R^□_{r̄|G_{F_ṽ}} ⊗̂ ⊗̂_{v′≠v} R^τ_{r̄|G_{F_ṽ′}}[[x_1,…,x_h]]; X_∞ := Spf R_∞; K := GL3(O_K) (abusively); fix a lattice σ(τ)° in σ(τ).
items.note: R_∞ is as in §3.5.1 (for #S = 1) after increasing h, because R^τ_ρ̄ is formally smooth. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Proposition 3.5.15 — a weak minimal patching functor for a single ρ̄
items.statement: Assume the setup above (def-setup-formally-smooth-type, cite-EG14-cor-A-7, constr-R-infty-one-place) and let M̃_∞ be the weak minimal patching functor for r̄ from [LLHLM18, Prop. 7.15]. Let M_∞ : Rep_K(O) → Mod(X_∞) be the functor M̃_∞ ∘ ∏_{v∈Σ^+_p} ι_ṽ ∘ (− ⊗ ⊗̂_{v′∈Σ^+_p, v′≠v} σ(τ)°). Then M_∞ is a [weak minimal] patching functor for ρ̄.
items.note: 'Follows from the construction of r̄ and Proposition 3.5.14' (no separate proof). Printed index 'v ∈ Σ^+_p, v′ ≠ v' under ⊗̂ and 'patching functor' for 'weak minimal patching functor' (misprints). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Corollary 3.5.16 — patching functors for collections
items.statement: Suppose that ρ̄_S is a collection of continuous Galois representations each satisfying the properties of ρ̄ in Proposition 3.5.15. Then there exists a [weak minimal] patching functor for ρ̄_S.
items.note: Proof: 'take the completed tensor product of the patching functors constructed in Proposition 3.5.15 for each ρ̄_ṽ' (sketch). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Nonvanishing criterion (proof of Theorem 3.5.3): R^τ_ρ̄ ≠ 0 ⟺ W?(ρ̄, τ) ≠ ∅
items.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite unramified, ρ̄ : G_K → GL3(F) continuous, 10-generic and semisimple, and τ a 1-generic tame inertial type. Then R^τ_ρ̄ ≠ 0 if and only if W?(ρ̄, τ) ≠ ∅; moreover if R^τ_ρ̄ ≠ 0 then τ is 7-generic.
items.note: ⇒: Proposition 3.4.5 (τ 7-generic) and then Proposition 3.4.4 (the paper cites Proposition 3.4.2, which gives it via Theorems 3.3.11–3.3.12). ⇐: a patching functor for ρ̄ exists by Proposition 3.5.15; for σ ∈ W?(ρ̄,τ), e(M_∞(σ)) = 1 by Theorem 3.5.2, so M_∞(σ(τ)°) ≠ 0 and hence R^τ_ρ̄ ≠ 0. This gives the nontriviality promised in Remark 3.3.13. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Equation (3.5) — e(R̄^τ_ρ̄) = e(M_∞(σ̄(τ)°))
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 3.5.3, if τ is 1-generic and R^τ_ρ̄ ≠ 0, then e(R̄^τ_ρ̄) = e(M_∞(σ̄(τ)°)) for the patching functor M_∞ of Proposition 3.5.15 and any O-lattice σ(τ)° ⊂ σ(τ).
items.note: Here e(R̄^τ_ρ̄) must be the Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity of R̄^τ_ρ̄ in its own dimension (equivalently e(R̄_∞(τ)), since the other factors are formally smooth), not D19 literally. Proof: τ is 7-generic; the comparison ring R̃^τ_ρ̄ satisfies e(R̃^τ_ρ̄) = e(M_∞(σ̄(τ)°)) ([LLHLM18, Table 7, Props 8.5, 8.12] and Theorem 3.5.2), e(M_∞(σ̄(τ)°)) ≤ e(R̄^τ_ρ̄) (proof of [LLHLM18, Prop. 7.14]), and e(R̃^τ_ρ̄) ≥ e(R̄^τ_ρ̄[[X_1,…,X_{3f}]]) = e(R̄^τ_ρ̄) from the surjection. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The comparison ring R̃^τ_ρ̄ (proof of Theorem 3.5.3)
items.statement: There is a ring R̃^τ_ρ̄ of the same dimension as R̄^τ_ρ̄[[X_1,…,X_{3f}]] which is a power series ring over the completed tensor product over F of rings R̃ from [LLHLM18, Section 8] and rings R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐,w̃} (for suitable 𝔐, w̃ from [LLHLM18, Table 7]), and which admits a surjection onto R̄^τ_ρ̄[[X_1,…,X_{3f}]]. R̃^τ_ρ̄ is reduced and Cohen–Macaulay (argument of Lemma 3.5.4), and in fact R̄^τ_ρ̄[[X_1,…,X_{3f}]] ≅ R̃^τ_ρ̄ ([LLHLM18, Lemma 8.8]).
items.note: Obtained 'by a direct generalization of the arguments of [LLHLM18, Section 8]' (there for K = Q_p); only key details are given. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: [LLHLM18, §8: Props 8.5, 8.12, Lemma 8.8] as used
items.statement: (As used.) [LLHLM18, Propositions 8.5 and 8.12, Table 7] compute the multiplicity (number of components) of the rings R̃ and R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐,w̃}; [LLHLM18, Lemma 8.8]: a surjection between complete local Noetherian F-algebras of the same dimension, whose source is reduced (equidimensional) with the same multiplicity as the target, is an isomorphism.
items.note: Cited; paraphrase of Lemma 8.8 inferred from its use here, not printed. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: [Enn, Proposition 7] and [LLHL19, Remark 2.2.8] — no lifts for non-generic principal series types
items.statement: (As used.) If ρ̄ is 10-generic in the sense of [Enn, Definition 2.2] and τ is a principal series type which is not 2-generic in that sense, then ρ̄ has no potentially crystalline lift of type τ and Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0). [LLHL19, Remark 2.2.8] translates: 'not 1-generic' (Definition 2.2.2) ⇒ 'not 2-generic' in Enns' sense, and 10-generic ⇒ 10-generic in Enns' sense.
items.note: Cited. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark 3.5.17 — distinct weights have distinct supports
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 3.5.3 (with M_∞ as in its proof), since #Irr(R̄^τ_ρ̄) = #W?(ρ̄, τ), R̄^τ_ρ̄ is reduced and M_∞(σ̄(τ)°) has full support over R̄_∞(τ), the (irreducible) supports of M_∞(σ) are pairwise different for σ ∈ W?(ρ̄, τ).
items.locator: §3.5.3, Remark 3.5.17, p. 46; also §3.5.3, Remark 3.5.17, published p. 46
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Proposition 3.6.1(1) — canonical labelling of components of R̄^τ_ρ̄ by Serre weights
items.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite unramified of degree f and ρ̄: G_K → GL3(F) continuous, 10-generic and semisimple (as in Theorem 3.5.3). There is a unique assignment σ ↦ 𝔭(σ), for σ ∈ W?(ρ̄), such that 𝔭(σ) ⊂ R^□_ρ̄ is a prime ideal and, for every tame inertial type τ, Spec(R̄^τ_ρ̄) = ⋃_{σ∈W?(ρ̄,τ)} Spec(R^□_ρ̄/𝔭(σ)) (3.6), where the right-hand side is given the reduced scheme structure. Moreover the image of 𝔭(σ) in R̄^τ_ρ̄ is a minimal prime ideal and (3.6) is the decomposition of R̄^τ_ρ̄ into irreducible components.
items.locator: §3.6, Proposition 3.6.1(1) and (3.6), published p. 46; proof pp. 47
items.note: Uniqueness: induction on the defect of σ using the minimal type τ of σ (Lemma 3.5.9, Remark 3.5.10): for defect 0, #W?(ρ̄,τ)=1 and 𝔭(σ)=Ann_{R^□}(R̄^τ); for defect δ>0 there is a unique component of R̄^τ whose ideal is not 𝔭(σ') for a σ' of lower defect. Existence: take a weak minimal patching functor M∞ for ρ̄ (Proposition 3.5.15); by Remark 3.5.13 the support of M∞(σ) has generic point 𝔭'(σ)R∞; since R^τ_ρ̄ is a domain (Theorem 3.5.3), Spec R̄∞(τ) is the support of M∞(σ̄(τ)°), which is filtered by the M∞(σ), giving (3.7) ⋃_{σ∈W?(ρ̄,τ)} Spec(R∞/𝔭'(σ)R∞); Remark 3.5.17 gives irreducible decomposition; descend to R̄^τ_ρ̄. W?(ρ̄) = ⋃_τ W?(ρ̄,τ) is from §2 (Definition 2.2.7). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).
items.proofOutline: Start with defect-zero types selecting individual primes and use the unique minimal type at each higher defect; no arbitrary independent bijection for each type.

items.name: Proposition 3.6.1(2) — support of M∞ on predicted weights
items.statement: Let ρ̄_S = (ρ̄_ṽ)_{ṽ∈S} with each ρ̄_ṽ as in (1) (F_ṽ/Q_p unramified, ρ̄_ṽ 10-generic semisimple). If M∞ is a weak minimal patching functor for ρ̄_S, then for σ_ṽ ∈ W?(ρ̄_ṽ) the scheme-theoretic support of M∞(⊗_{ṽ∈S} σ_ṽ) is Spec(R∞/Σ_{ṽ∈S} 𝔭(σ_ṽ)R∞), with 𝔭 the assignment of part (1).
items.note: The condition σ_ṽ ∈ W?(ρ̄_ṽ) is implicit in the statement (the proof takes σ ∈ W?(ρ̄_S)). Proof: by the proof of Theorem 3.5.2 the support is Spec R∞/(Σ 𝔭(σ)_ṽ R∞) for primes 𝔭(σ)_ṽ ⊂ R^□_ρ̄ṽ; induct on δ = Def_ρ̄S(σ); δ=0: choose τ_S by Lemma 3.5.9 with R̄∞(τ_S) = R∞/𝔭(σ); δ>0: minimal type τ_S, the support of M∞(σ̄(τ_S)°) is (3.8) ⋃_{σ'∈W?(ρ̄_S,τ_S)} Spec(R∞/Σ𝔭(σ'_ṽ)R∞) and e(M∞(σ))=1 forces the claim. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).
items.proofOutline: Use exactness, reduced type support and induction on defect; the primes do not depend on the globalization or patching choices.

items.name: Lemma 3.6.2 — support of M∞ on subquotients of a lattice
items.statement: Assume ρ̄_S is 10-generic. Let τ_S = (τ_ṽ)_{ṽ∈S} be a collection of tame inertial types and V a subquotient of σ̄(τ_S)° for some O-lattice σ(τ_S)° ⊂ σ(τ_S). Let X̄∞(V) ↪ Spec R̄∞ be the reduced closed subscheme underlying ⋃_{σ∈JH(V)} Supp(M∞(σ)). Then the scheme-theoretic support of M∞(V) is X̄∞(V). In particular, if M∞(V) is a cyclic R∞-module then M∞(V) ≅ R∞/I(V), where I(V) := ⋂_{σ∈JH(V)} Ann_{R∞}(M∞(σ)).
items.note: M∞ a weak minimal patching functor for ρ̄_S (Definition 3.5.1). Proof as in the second paragraph of [EGS15, Proposition 8.1.1]: nothing to prove unless τ_S is 7-generic; the support is generically reduced (as for M∞(σ̄(τ_S)°)); M∞(V) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over R̄∞(τ_S) (extensions of MCM modules, Definition 3.5.1(3), dim R̄∞(τ_S)=d), so the support has no embedded primes, hence is reduced. Printed hypothesis says 'ρ̄ is 10-generic' (meaning ρ̄_S). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Matrix A^{(i)} of the i-th partial Frobenius
items.statement: For a Kisin module 𝔐 with descent data of type τ = τ(s,μ) with orientation s_or ∈ W̲ and an eigenbasis β, A^{(i)} := Mat_β(φ^{(i)}_{𝔐, s_or,i+1(3)}), the matrix of the i-th partial Frobenius with respect to β.
items.note: Recalled from [LLHLM18, Definition 2.11 and Section 6] and [LLHL19, discussion after Definition 3.2.8]. Setting of §3.6.1: ρ̄ 10-generic, τ=τ(s,μ) with lowest alcove presentation (s, μ−η), R^τ_ρ̄ ≠ 0 (so τ is 7-generic), 𝔐̄ ∈ Y^{η,τ}(F) the unique Kisin module with T*_dd(𝔐̄) ≅ ρ̄|_{G_K∞}, w̃ = w̃(ρ̄,τ) its shape, ℳ̄ := (𝔐̄[1/u'])^{Δ=1}; gauge basis β̄ of 𝔐̄ ([LLHLM18, Definitions 4.15, 6.11]) and a framing of ρ̄ are fixed. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Groupoids Φ-Mod^ét_ℳ̄, Φ-Mod^{ét,□}_ℳ̄, Ȳ^{η,τ}_𝔐̄, D̄^{τ,β̄}_𝔐̄
items.statement: Φ-Mod^ét_ℳ̄ (resp. Φ-Mod^{ét,□}_ℳ̄) is the groupoid of étale φ-modules deforming ℳ̄ (resp. such deformations with a basis on the associated G_K∞-representation). Ȳ^{η,τ}_𝔐̄ is the groupoid whose value on a local Artinian F-algebra A is the groupoid of pairs (𝔐_A, j_A) with 𝔐_A ∈ Y^{η,τ}(A) and j_A: 𝔐_A ⊗_A F ≅ 𝔐̄ an isomorphism in Y^{η,τ}(F). D̄^{τ,β̄}_𝔐̄ parametrizes the same data plus a gauge basis lifting β̄.
items.note: R̄^{τ,β̄,□}_{𝔐̄,ρ̄} and R̄^{τ,□}_{𝔐̄,ρ̄} are defined in [LLHLM18, Sections 4.3, 5.2, 6.2] (there μ denotes this paper's η). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: [LLHLM18, Thms 4.17, 6.12, §6.2] — representability of D̄^{τ,β̄}_𝔐̄ and the torus quotient
items.statement: There is an action of Ĝ_m^{3f} on D̄^{τ,β̄}_𝔐̄ by scaling the gauge basis, and [D̄^{τ,β̄}_𝔐̄/Ĝ_m^{3f}] ≅ Ȳ^{η,τ}_𝔐̄. D̄^{τ,β̄}_𝔐̄ is representable by R̄^{τ,β̄}_𝔐̄ = ⊗̂_i (R^{expl}_{w̃_i})^{p-flat,red}/ϖ, which is a quotient of the power series ring over F in (suitable modifications of) the coefficients of the entries of the universal partial Frobenius matrices A^{(i),univ} by 'finite height' equations; ι'_τ sends 𝔐^univ to (𝔐^univ[1/u'])^{Δ=1}.
items.note: Cited, not proved: [LLHLM18, Theorem 6.12] (Ĝ_m^{3f}-quotient) and [LLHLM18, Theorem 4.17 and Section 6.2] (representability). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Canonical diagram (3.9) relating deformation rings, explicit rings and étale φ-modules
items.statement: There is a commutative diagram (cf. [LLHLM18, Diagram (5.9)]) with top row Spf(R̄^{τ,β̄,□}_{𝔐̄,ρ̄}) →(f.s.) Spf(R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃}) ↪ D̄^{τ,β̄}_𝔐̄, middle row Spf(R̄^τ_ρ̄) = Spf(R̄^{τ,□}_{𝔐̄,ρ̄}) →(f.s.) [Spf(R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃})/Ĝ_m^{3f}] ↪ Ȳ^{η,τ}_𝔐̄, bottom row Φ-Mod^{ét,□}_ℳ̄ →(f.s.) Φ-Mod^ét_ℳ̄; vertical maps from the top row to the middle row are formally smooth, Spf(R̄^τ_ρ̄) ↪ Φ-Mod^{ét,□}_ℳ̄, ι_τ: [Spf R̄^{expl,∇}/Ĝ_m^{3f}] ↪ Φ-Mod^ét_ℳ̄ and ι'_τ: Ȳ^{η,τ}_𝔐̄ → Φ-Mod^ét_ℳ̄; the top squares and the bottom-left square are Cartesian. Justification: (i) there is a canonical isomorphism [Spf(R̄^{τ,β̄,□}_{𝔐̄,ρ̄})/ĜL3] ≅ Spf(R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃}); (ii) the Ĝ_m^{3f}-action on D̄^{τ,β̄}_𝔐̄ preserves Spf(R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃}); with (𝔐_{w̃,τ}, β_{w̃,τ}) the restriction of (𝔐^univ, β^univ), ι_τ sends 𝔐_{w̃,τ} to ℳ_{w̃,τ} := (𝔐_{w̃,τ}[1/u'])^{Δ=1}; (iii) the second row is the quotient of the first by Ĝ_m^{3f} (scaling the gauge basis); (iv) the second column is the quotient of the first by ĜL3 (changing the framing).
items.locator: §3.6.1, diagram (3.9) and its justification, published pp. 49–54
items.note: (i) is [LLHLM18, Theorem 5.12, Theorem 6.14 and Table 7] when ℓ(w̃_i) > 1 for all i; when ℓ(w̃_i) ≤ 1 for some i it follows from the arguments of [LLHLM18, Section 8] together with Theorem 3.5.2, as in the proof of Theorem 3.5.3. Objects with superscript □ carry a ĜL3-action (change of framing). The remaining ingredient, that ι'_τ is a monomorphism, is Proposition 3.6.3. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Explicit ring R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_i} for ℓ(w̃_i) > 1
items.statement: R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃} = ⊗̂_i R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_i}. When ℓ(w̃_i) > 1, R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_i} is the quotient of the power series ring over F generated by (suitable modifications of) the coefficients of the entries of A^{(i),univ} by the explicit list of relations of [LLHLM18, Section 5.3 and Table 7]; in this case there are also rings R^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_i} over O and diagram (3.9) lifts to O with the same properties ([LLHLM18, Diagram (5.9)]). [LLHLM18, Table 7] only lists w̃_i in a set of representatives for the outer automorphisms of W̃_a.
items.note: Here (a,b,c) ∈ F_p^3 is the mod p reduction of s^{-1}_{f−1−i}(μ_{f−1−i}) ∈ X*(T) ≅ Z^3. The rings for the representatives are listed in Tables 3 and 4. Cited from [LLHLM18]. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Explicit ring R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_i} for ℓ(w̃_i) = 1 (shape α)
items.statement: When ℓ(w̃_i) = 1, by symmetry w̃_i = αt_1, and A^{(i),univ} = [[c11, c12 + v c12*, c13], [v c21*, c22 + v d22, c23], [v c31, v c32, c33 + v c33*]]. Set c̃32 := (c32 c21* − d22 c31)/c21*. Define R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_i} to be the quotient of F[[c11, c12, c13, c22, c23, c31, c̃32, c33, d22, c12* − [c̄12*], c21* − [c̄21*], c33* − [c̄33*]]] by the relations c11c23 = 0; c33* c11 c̃32 = c13 c31 c̃32; c11 d22 c33* = ((b−c)/(a−b)) c21* c13 c̃32; c13 c23 c̃32 = 0; c23 c31 c̃32 = 0; c21* c33 = c31 c23; c12 c33* = ((a−c)/(a−b)) c13 c̃32; c22 c33* = ((−1−a+c)/(−1−a+b)) c23 c̃32; and (a−b) c13 c31 d22 + (c−b) c13 c̃32 c21* + (−1−a+c) c23 c31 c12* = 0. In particular R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_i} is a formal power series ring (formally smooth of relative dimension 3) over the ring R̃ of [LLHLM18, Proposition 8.11].
items.locator: §3.6.1, item (4)(2), published pp. 50–53; repeated in §3.6.2 Case αt_1, pp. 64–65
items.note: The equations come from [LLHLM18, Proposition 8.11] and its proof by restoring the units c12*, c21*, c33* (set to 1 there): the first six from the statement (d22 = c'22 there), the seventh and eighth from the proof, the last implicit (obtained by solving c33 via p-saturation of the 2×2 minor condition). Checked (Singular, a,b,c generic): with these relations det A = v³·(−c12*c21*c33*) and all constant 2×2 minors vanish; the ring is reduced with six minimal primes (Table 3, α row), all of the same dimension. Notation: F is the residue field of O, ϖ a uniformiser; v = u^{e'} is the variable of Kisin modules with descent data; cij, dij denote non-unit coordinates and cij* unit coordinates of a chart (cij* − [c̄ij*] is the formal variable, [·] the Teichmüller lift); (a,b,c) ∈ F_p^3 is the mod p reduction of s_i^{-1}(μ_i) (for the ring attached to w̃_{f−1−i}); (a',b',c') the analogous constants for τ'. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Explicit ring R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_i} for ℓ(w̃_i) = 0 (identity shape)
items.statement: When ℓ(w̃_i) = 0, A^{(i),univ} = [[c11 + v c11*, c12, c13], [v c21, c22 + v c22*, c23], [v c31, v c32, c33 + v c33*]], and R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_i} is the quotient of F[[c_ij, c_kk* − [c̄_kk*], 1 ≤ i,j,k ≤ 3]] by the relations c_ii c_jj = 0 for i ≠ j; c11c23 = 0; c31c22 = 0; c33c12 = 0; c12c23 = c22c13; c11c32 = c12c31; c21c33 = c31c23; (−1−a+c) c22* c33 + (−1−a+b) c22 c33* − (−1−a+c) c23 c32 = 0; (a−b) c33* c11 + (−1−b+c) c33 c11* − (a−b) c13 c31 = 0; (b−c) c11* c22 + (a−c) c11 c22* − (b−c) c12 c21 = 0; c11 c22* c33* + c22 c11* c33* + c33 c11* c22* − c11* c23 c32 − c22* c13 c31 − c33* c12 c21 + c13 c32 c21 = 0. It is a formal power series ring (formally smooth of relative dimension 3) over the ring R̃ of [LLHLM18, Corollary 8.4].
items.locator: §3.6.1, item (4)(3), published p. 53; repeated in §3.6.2 Case t_1, p. 67
items.note: From [LLHLM18, Corollary 8.4] by restoring the units c_kk*, adding c12c33 = 0 (said to be missing in loc. cit., obtained from the 2×2 minor condition). Checked (Singular, a,b,c generic, units inverted): det A = v³ c11*c22*c33*; constant 2×2 minors vanish; reduced with six minimal primes of equal dimension; the ideal is invariant under conjugation by δ̃ = (123)t_{(0,0,−1)} (indices i ↦ i+1, (a,b,c) ↦ (b,c,a+1)); c12c33 already lies in the ideal generated by the other relations (so the addition is harmless). Notation: F is the residue field of O, ϖ a uniformiser; v = u^{e'} is the variable of Kisin modules with descent data; cij, dij denote non-unit coordinates and cij* unit coordinates of a chart (cij* − [c̄ij*] is the formal variable, [·] the Teichmüller lift); (a,b,c) ∈ F_p^3 is the mod p reduction of s_i^{-1}(μ_i) (for the ring attached to w̃_{f−1−i}); (a',b',c') the analogous constants for τ'. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Proposition 3.6.3 — ι'_τ is a monomorphism
items.statement: Assume τ is 3-generic and 𝔐̄ ∈ Ȳ^{η,τ}(F) is semisimple of shape w̃ = (w̃_j). Let β̄ be a gauge basis for 𝔐̄. Then ι'_τ: Ȳ^{η,τ}_𝔐̄ → Φ-Mod^ét_ℳ̄ is a monomorphism.
items.note: Proof: need full faithfulness on F[ε]/(ε²)-points Ȳ^{η,τ}_𝔐̄(F[ε]/ε²) → Φ-Mod^ét_ℳ̄(F[ε]/ε²), which is [LLHL19, Proposition 3.2.18] (the target is equivalent to Rep_{F[ε]/ε²}(G_K∞)_ρ̄ there). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Bijections Irr(R̄^τ_ρ̄) ↔ ∏_i Irr(R̄^{expl,∇}_{w̃_i}) and ∏_i Σ_{w̃_i*} ↔ W?(ρ̄,τ)
items.statement: Diagram (3.9) gives a bijection between the set of minimal primes Irr(Spec R̄^τ_ρ̄) and Irr(Spec R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃}) = ∏_i Irr(Spec R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_i}); by Proposition 3.6.1 this set is in bijection with {𝔭(σ) : σ ∈ W?(ρ̄,τ)}. By Proposition 3.4.2 there is a bijection ∏_i Σ_{w̃_i*} ≅ W?(ρ̄,τ), (ω,a) ↦ σ^{(s,μ)}_{(ω,a)}.
items.note: Σ_{w̃*} ⊂ Σ_0 and σ^{(s,μ)}_{(ω,a)} are from §2 (Corollary 2.3.11, Proposition 3.4.2); p. 48 phrases the same description via Corollary 2.3.11 with Σ_w̃. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Theorem 3.6.4 — explicit labelling of components by Table 3
items.statement: Assume ρ̄ is 10-generic (τ = τ(s,μ), R^τ_ρ̄ ≠ 0, w̃ = w̃(ρ̄,τ)). Via the above bijections, ∏_{i=0}^{f−1} Σ_{w̃_i*} ≅ ∏_i Irr(Spec R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_i}) ≅ Irr(Spec R̄^τ_ρ̄) is given by ((ω_i,a_i))_i ↦ (c_{(ω_{f−1−i},a_{f−1−i})} R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_i})_i ↦ 𝔭(σ^{(s,μ)}_{(ω,a)}), where c_{(ω_i,a_i)} is the minimal prime of R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_{f−1−i}} given by Table 3.
items.note: Proof: by Proposition 3.6.9 and the proof of Proposition 3.6.1, for σ with minimal type τ' one must show that ⋂_{(ω,a)} (Σ_i c_{(ω_i,a_i)}) = Σ_i (⋂_{(ω_i,a_i)∈Σ_0∩z̃_i*(Σ_0)} c_{(ω_i,a_i)}) corresponds to ⋂_{σ'∈W?(ρ̄,τ')} 𝔭(σ'); this follows from Corollary 3.6.7 (embedding by embedding) and the explicit matchings of §3.6.2. Several matchings are only asserted as similar; the Table 3 entry c_(0,1) for the identity shape is misprinted. Table 3 lists only representatives under outer automorphisms (Remark 3.6.5). Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Remark 3.6.5 — representatives up to outer automorphisms suffice
items.statement: Table 3 gives the ideals c_{(ω_i,a_i)} ⊆ R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_{f−1−i}} only for a set of representatives of w̃_{f−1−i} ∈ Adm^∨((2,1,0)) for the action of the outer automorphisms of W̃^∨; this suffices because this action corresponds to changing the lowest alcove presentation of τ.
items.note: Explicit form of the outer automorphism: Remark 3.6.17. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Lemma 3.6.6 — matching lemma
items.statement: Let τ = τ(s,μ) and τ' = τ(s',μ') with R^τ_ρ̄, R^{τ'}_ρ̄ ≠ 0, ρ̄ 10-generic. Consider diagram (3.9) for R̄^τ_ρ̄ and R̄^{τ'}_ρ̄ (objects for τ' decorated with ′). Assume there are ideals I of R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃} and I' of R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄',w̃'} such that: I, I' are intersections of minimal primes; there is an isomorphism R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃}/I ≅ R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄',w̃'}/I'; and there is an isomorphism of étale φ-modules between the base change of ℳ_{w̃,τ} to R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃}/I and that of ℳ_{w̃',τ'} to R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄',w̃'}/I' compatible with this ring isomorphism. Let J (resp. J') be the intersection of the minimal primes of R̄^τ_ρ̄ (resp. R̄^{τ'}_ρ̄) corresponding to I (resp. I'). Then J and J' induce the same ideal of R̄^□_ρ̄.
items.note: Proof: the hypotheses give the isomorphism (3.10) over Φ-Mod^ét_ℳ̄; pulling back along Φ-Mod^{ét,□} → Φ-Mod^ét gives (3.11); Spf(R̄^□_ρ̄) → Φ-Mod^{ét,□}_ℳ̄ is a monomorphism by [LLHLM18, Proposition 3.12] (ρ̄ 10-generic ⇒ ad(ρ̄) cyclotomic free), so Spf(R̄^τ/J) and Spf(R̄^{τ'}/J') define the same subfunctor. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: [LLHLM18, Proposition 3.12] — Spf(R̄^□_ρ̄) → Φ-Mod^{ét,□}_ℳ̄ is a monomorphism
items.statement: If ad(ρ̄) is cyclotomic free (e.g. ρ̄ 10-generic), the natural map Spf(R̄^□_ρ̄) → Φ-Mod^{ét,□}_ℳ̄ (restriction to G_K∞) is a monomorphism.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Lemma 3.6.6, published p. 56
items.note: Cited, not proved. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: [LLHL19, Proposition 3.2.18] — full faithfulness on tangent groupoids
items.statement: For τ 3-generic and 𝔐̄ semisimple of shape w̃, the functor Ȳ^{η,τ}_𝔐̄(F[ε]/(ε²)) → Rep_{F[ε]/ε²}(G_K∞)_ρ̄ ≃ Φ-Mod^ét_ℳ̄(F[ε]/(ε²)) is fully faithful.
items.locator: Used in the proof of Proposition 3.6.3, published p. 54
items.note: Cited, not proved; statement as used here. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Corollary 3.6.7 — matching by partial Frobenius matrices
items.statement: Keep the setting of Lemma 3.6.6. Assume there exists z̃ = (z̃_i)_i ∈ W̲_a^∨ with corresponding z̃* = (z̃_i*)_i ∈ W̲_a, z the image of z̃ in W̲^∨, such that s' = s z* and μ' = μ + s z̃*(0). Write (I_i)_i for the ideals of R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_i} giving rise to I, A^{(i)} for the matrix of the i-th partial Frobenius of 𝔐_{w̃,τ} w.r.t. β_{w̃,τ}, and (I'_i)_i, A'^{(i)} the analogues for τ'. Assume (a) the isomorphism R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃}/I ≅ R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄',w̃'}/I' is induced by isomorphisms R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃_i}/I_i ≅ R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄',w̃'_i}/I'_i; and (b) for each i, A^{(f−1−i)} mod I_{f−1−i} = A'^{(f−1−i)} z̃_{f−1−i} mod I'_{f−1−i} via these isomorphisms. Then the conclusion of Lemma 3.6.6 holds.
items.note: Proof: Lemma 3.6.6, Proposition 3.2.1 and z̃ s* t_{μ*} = s'* t_{μ'*}. In the matchings of §3.6.2, z̃_{f−1−i} is written as a monomial matrix diag(v^ν)·P_w, which is t_ν w, and (a',b',c') = w(a,b,c) + ν. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Remark 3.6.8 — normalising gauge bases so that Ā^{(i)} = Ā'^{(i)} z̃_i
items.statement: Condition (b) of Corollary 3.6.7 implies (Ā^{(i)})_i = (Ā'^{(i)} z̃_i)_i (3.12) for the reductions modulo the maximal ideal. If ρ̄ is semisimple and τ, τ', z̃ are as in Proposition 3.6.9, then w̃ = w̃' z̃ (3.13); for any gauge bases β, β' one has Ā^{(i)} ∈ T(F) w̃_i and Ā'^{(i)} ∈ T(F) w̃'_i (Proposition 3.3.6), and after replacing β_𝔐 by a gauge basis β_𝔐' obtained by scaling by an element of T̲(F) ([LLHL19, Proposition 3.2.22]) one can ensure (3.12). All matchings in §3.6.2 assume the gauge bases are so chosen.
items.note: Argument: let 𝔐'_{w̃,τ} ∈ Y^{η,τ}(F) have partial Frobenii (Ā'^{(i)} z̃_i)_i (it has shape w̃ ∈ Adm^∨(η)); since z̃ s* t_{μ*} = s'* t_{μ'*}, (𝔐'_{w̃,τ})^{Δ=1} ≅ (𝔐_{w̃',τ'})^{Δ=1} (Proposition 3.2.1), so T*_dd(𝔐') ≅ ρ̄ and by triviality of the Kisin variety [LLHLM18, Theorem 3.2] 𝔐' ≅ 𝔐_{w̃,τ}. items.name: [LLHLM18, Theorem 3.2] — triviality of the Kisin variety
items.statement: For ρ̄ (sufficiently) generic and τ generic, there is at most one Kisin module 𝔐 ∈ Y^{η,τ}(F) with T*_dd(𝔐) ≅ ρ̄|_{G_K∞} (up to isomorphism).

items.statement: Any two gauge bases of 𝔐̄ ∈ Y^{η,τ}(F) (τ generic) differ by scaling by an element of T̲(F).

items.name: Proposition 3.6.9 — minimal types and the element z̃*
items.statement: Assume ρ̄ is 10-generic. Let τ = τ(s,μ) be a tame inertial type with R^τ_ρ̄ ≠ 0 and w̃ = w̃(ρ̄,τ) = (w̃_i)_i. Let (ω,a) = ((ω_i,a_i))_i ∈ ∏_i Σ_{w̃_i*} and σ = σ^{(s,μ)}_{(ω,a)} ∈ W?(ρ̄,τ). Let τ' be the minimal type of σ with respect to ρ̄ (Remark 3.5.10). Then: for z̃* = (z̃_i*)_i ∈ W̲̃_a as given by Table 3, τ' = τ(s',μ') with s' = s z* and μ' = μ + s z̃*(0); w̃(ρ̄,τ') z̃ = w̃; and W?(ρ̄,τ') ⊂ W?(ρ̄,τ).
items.note: Proof: 'immediate by computing the pairwise intersections among Σ_0, w̃_i*(r(Σ_0)) and z̃_i*(Σ_0)' (combinatorics of §2, not written out). Table 3 caption: τ' = τ(sz*, μ + sz̃*(0)) and w̃(ρ̄,τ') = w̃(ρ̄,τ) z̃^{-1}. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Normal-crossings chart R_N → R^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃} and the primes 𝔭^expl(σ)
items.statement: Let w̃ = w̃(ρ̄,τ) and suppose ℓ(w̃_i) ≥ 2 for all 0 ≤ i ≤ f−1. Let N := Σ_i (4 − ℓ(w̃_i)) and R_N := ⊗̂_{j=1}^N O[[x_j, y_j]]/(x_j y_j − p). Then there exists a formally smooth map R_N → R^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃}, which is fixed; R_N is regarded as a subalgebra. For σ ∈ W?(ρ̄,τ) let 𝔭^expl(σ) ⊂ R^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃} be the prime ideal corresponding to σ. The minimal primes of R^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃} containing ϖ are of the form ((z_j)_{j=1}^N + (ϖ)) R^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃} with z_j ∈ {x_j, y_j} for all j; z_j(σ) is defined by 𝔭^expl(σ) = ((z_j(σ))_{j=1}^N + (ϖ)) R^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃}.
items.note: 'Follows from Theorem 3.6.4'; the existence of the formally smooth map R_N → R^{expl,∇} rests on the explicit O-rings of [LLHLM18, §5.3, Table 7] (e.g. for αβ: c12((a−b)c31c'23 + (b−c)c21*c'33) = pz*, p. 61). In the special fibre each shape of length 3 contributes one pair (e.g. c11c22 = 0 for βαγ) and each shape of length 2 two pairs (αβ: c22·c31 = 0 and c12·((b−c)d33c21* + (a−b)c31d23) = 0). items.name: Lemma 3.6.10 — symmetric difference of chosen variables equals twice the graph distance
items.statement: Assume ρ̄ is 10-generic and ℓ(w̃_i) ≥ 2 for all 0 ≤ i ≤ f−1. For σ1, σ2 ∈ W?(ρ̄,τ), #({z_j(σ1)}_{j=1}^N Δ {z_j(σ2)}_{j=1}^N) = 2 d_gph(σ1,σ2), where Δ is the symmetric difference.
items.note: Proof: from the αβα, αβ and βα rows of Table 3, 𝔭^expl(σ1) + 𝔭^expl(σ2) is a prime of R^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,w̃} of height d_gph(σ1,σ2) + 1, while the height of the sum ((z_j)_j + (ϖ)) + ((z'_j)_j + (ϖ)) is ½#({z_j}Δ{z'_j}) + 1 (the printed proof says 'intersection'; see source issue). The height computation in R_N is elementary (quotient by one variable from each agreeing pair and both variables from each differing pair). d_gph is the extension-graph distance of §2; the βαγ, αβγ rows (also length 3) are not mentioned but are analogous. items.name: Lemma 3.6.11 — surjection criterion
items.statement: Suppose g: S ↠ R is a surjection of rings. Assume R and S are equidimensional of dimension d, have the same number of minimal primes, and S is reduced. Then g is an isomorphism.
items.note: Proof: the first two hypotheses imply ker g is nilpotent (g induces a homeomorphism Spec R ≅ Spec S: every minimal prime of R, of coheight d, is a minimal prime of S, and the counts agree), and S is reduced. Implicitly d < ∞ and the number of minimal primes is finite (the rings in question are complete Noetherian local). Used in (3.14) (p. 61, via a multiplicity comparison) and in Lemmas 3.6.13 and 3.6.15. Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).
items.proofOutline: Each minimal prime of R pulls back to a minimal prime of S: a strict containment over a minimal prime would reduce dimension. Equality of finite counts makes the pullback set exhaustive. The kernel lies in every minimal prime of S, hence in its zero nilradical. No assertion for arbitrary infinite sets of minimal primes.

items.name: Lemma 3.6.13 — triple intersection in R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,id}
items.note: Proof: pass to R̃ (same presentation with all c_ij* = 1; R̄^{expl,∇}_{𝔐̄,id} is a power series ring in three variables over R̃ by [LLHLM18, Corollary 8.4]). (c22,c33) ⊆ the intersection, giving the surjection (3.15) R̃/(c22,c33) ↠ R̃/(𝔴_0 ∩ c_(ε1,0) ∩ c_(ε2,0)); the target is equidimensional of dimension 3 with four minimal primes; R̃/(c22,c33) is the quotient of F[[c11, c_ij (i≠j)]] by c11c23, c12c23, c11c32 − c12c31, c31c23, c23c32, κc11 − c21c12, c11 − c13c31, c11 − c12c21 − c13c31 − c23c32 + c21c13c32 (κ = (a−c)/(b−c) ∈ F^×), which is isomorphic to the monomial ring of item T32; conclude by Lemma 3.6.11. Verified by Singular. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).
items.proofOutline: Set all three unit parameters equal to one, as permitted by the source formal-power-series decomposition. Eliminate c11 and set a=c12−c13 c32, b=kappa c31−c21 c32, c=c23, d=c13, e=c21, f=c32, where kappa is the nonzero scalar of the source presentation (published p.70). The resulting quotient has ideal (ab,ac,ae,bc,bd,cf), so T32 proves reducedness, dimension three and four minimal primes. Apply T31 to the surjection onto the intersection quotient. The full chart presentation and its coefficient calculation remain G04.

items.name: Monomial ring in the proof of Lemma 3.6.13
items.statement: With c̃12 := c12 − c13c32 and c̃31 := κc31 − c21c32: R̃/(c22, c33) ≅ F[[c̃12, c̃31, c23, c13, c21, c32]]/(c̃12 c̃31, c̃12 c23, c̃12 c21, c̃31 c23, c̃31 c13, c23 c32). This ring is reduced (square-free monomial ideal), equidimensional of dimension 3, with four minimal primes (c̃12, c̃31, c23), (c̃12, c̃31, c32), (c̃12, c23, c13), (c̃31, c23, c21).
items.note: Intermediate step: R̃/(c22,c33) ≅ F[[c_ij, i≠j]]/(c31c23, c23c32, c12c23, c31(c12 − c13c32), c13(κc31 − c21c32), c21(c12 − c13c32)) after eliminating c11 = c13c31; checked by hand. The minimal primes are the minimal vertex covers of the graph with edges c̃12c̃31, c̃12c23, c̃12c21, c̃31c23, c̃31c13, c23c32 (listed explicitly here; the paper says 'easily seen'). Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).
items.proofOutline: The ideal equals the intersection of the four coordinate ideals: a monomial is in each iff its support hits each of the four variable triples, equivalently it is divisible by one listed degree-two generator. Each prime quotient is a three-variable power-series domain. The same monomial-support test applies to series coefficientwise. Minimal-prime enumeration independently executed.

items.statement: Let δ̃ := (123)t_(0,0,−1) and w̃ ↦ δ̃ w̃ δ̃^{-1} the corresponding outer automorphism of W̃^∨; δ acts on Σ_0, and the ideal relations of Lemmas 3.6.15 and 3.6.16 hold for shape β with c_{(ω_i,a_i)} replaced by c_{((δ̃*)^{-1}(ω_i),a_i)}. items.name: §4.1.1 — filtrations, graded pieces, semisimple filtrations and their length
items.statement: A decreasing (resp. increasing) filtration 𝓕 on M is a family of subobjects 𝓕ⁿ(M) ⊂ M (resp. 𝓕_n(M) ⊂ M), n ∈ ℤ, with 𝓕ⁿ⁺¹(M) ⊂ 𝓕ⁿ(M) (resp. 𝓕_n(M) ⊂ 𝓕_{n+1}(M)) for all n. It is exhaustive and separated if 𝓕ⁿ(M) = 0 for n ≫ 0 and 𝓕ⁿ(M) = M for n ≪ 0 (resp. 𝓕_n(M) = 0 for n ≪ 0 and = M for n ≫ 0); this is always assumed. grⁿ_𝓕(M) := 𝓕ⁿ(M)/𝓕ⁿ⁺¹(M) (resp. gr^𝓕_n(M) := 𝓕_n(M)/𝓕_{n−1}(M)). 𝓕 is semisimple if every graded piece is semisimple. After shifting, one assumes grⁿ_𝓕(M) = 0 (resp. gr^𝓕_n(M) = 0) for n < 0 and gr⁰_𝓕(M) ≠ 0 (resp. gr^𝓕_0(M) ≠ 0). The length of 𝓕 is the largest ℓ ∈ ℤ with gr^{ℓ−1}_𝓕(M) ≠ 0 (resp. gr^𝓕_{ℓ−1}(M) ≠ 0).
items.note: The printed text says 'for all i' and 'for i sufficiently large' where n is meant (see source issue). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.1.1 — basic properties of radical and socle filtrations
items.statement: The radical (resp. socle) filtration of M is a decreasing (resp. increasing) semisimple filtration, with gr⁰_rad(M) = cosoc(M) and gr^soc_0(M) = soc(M). Since formation of the cosocle (resp. socle) is right (resp. left) exact, the filtration induced by the radical (resp. socle) filtration of M on a quotient object (resp. subobject) of M is the radical (resp. socle) filtration of that quotient (resp. subobject). The radical and socle filtrations of M have the same length.
items.note: Standard facts, stated without proof. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.1.1 — Loewy length and Loewy series
items.statement: The common length of the radical and socle filtrations of M is the Loewy length ℓℓ(M). Every semisimple filtration of M has length ≥ ℓℓ(M); a semisimple filtration is a Loewy series if its length equals ℓℓ(M).
items.note: Rigidity, previously bundled here, is split off as def-rigid. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: First prove that the two lengths coincide and are minimal among lengths of exhaustive separated semisimple filtrations. The definition does not assert every module is rigid.

S⊕F[t]/t^2 has ell=2 and is not rigid: its radical omits the direct simple summand in soc_0.

items.name: (4.1) — a Loewy series lies between the radical and socle filtrations
items.statement: If 𝓕 is a decreasing Loewy series of M, then radⁿ(M) ⊆ 𝓕ⁿ(M) ⊆ soc_{ℓℓ(M)−n−1}(M) for all n ∈ {0, …, ℓℓ(M)}.
items.note: Standard; stated without proof. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.1.1 — rigid object
items.statement: M is rigid if radⁿ(M) = soc_{ℓℓ(M)−n−1}(M) for all n (equivalently, the radical and socle filtrations agree up to the reindexing n ↦ ℓℓ(M)−n−1).
items.note: Split from the previous D09. For a rigid M, (4.1) shows that the Loewy series is unique. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.1.1 — multiplicity-free object
items.statement: M is multiplicity free if every Jordan–Hölder factor of M occurs with multiplicity one.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.1.1 — 'points to' relation on JH(M)
items.statement: Let M be multiplicity free. For σ, σ′ ∈ JH(M), σ points to σ′ if some subquotient of M is isomorphic to a nontrivial extension of σ by σ′, that is, to a nonsplit E with 0 → σ′ → E → σ → 0.
items.note: Convention: 'extension of σ by σ′' has σ′ as subobject and σ as quotient, so arrows point from the upper to the lower constituent. The definition of closed subsets, previously bundled here, is now def-closed-subset. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: Direction is from quotient to subobject. Multiplicity-freeness is essential for the reconstruction theorem; use composition-factor sets only after proving it.

api.name: extension_arrow
api.statement: An arrow produces the specified nonsplit exact sequence.

api.name: closed_intersection
api.statement: Intersections of closed vertex sets are closed.

unitTests: For a split sum S⊕T the two-vertex graph has no edges.
A nonsplit extension of S by T has arrow S→T.
S⊕S is rejected as not multiplicity free.

items.name: §4.1.1 — closed subsets of JH(M)
items.statement: Let M be multiplicity free. A subset S ⊂ JH(M) is closed if σ ∈ S and σ points to σ′ imply σ′ ∈ S.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 4.1.1 — subobjects of a multiplicity-free object correspond to closed subsets
items.statement: Let M be a multiplicity-free object of 𝒞. The assignment N ↦ JH(N) is a bijection between subobjects N ⊂ M and closed subsets of JH(M).
items.note: Proof: JH(N) is closed; for closed S, take the minimal N with S ⊂ JH(N); if σ ∈ JH(N)∖S, replace σ by a σ′ ∈ JH(N) pointing to it until none exists (this terminates because Γ(M) is acyclic), let N′ be the maximal subobject of N with σ ∉ JH(N′), and show N/N′ ≅ σ, contradicting minimality. Injectivity (JH(N₁) = JH(N₂) ⇒ N₁ = N₂, via JH(N₁∩N₂) = JH(N₁)∩JH(N₂) for multiplicity-free M) and the acyclicity used in the replacement step are not written out (see source issue). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: For surjectivity take a minimal subobject containing the chosen factors; an extra factor maximal in the arrow order would give a removable simple quotient. For injectivity multiplicity-freeness identifies intersections by their factors.

items.name: §4.1.1 — degree of a constituent in a filtration
items.statement: Let M be multiplicity free and 𝓕 a decreasing (resp. increasing) filtration on M. For σ ∈ JH(M), d^M_𝓕(σ) (resp. d_M^𝓕(σ)) is the unique n such that Hom_𝒞(σ, grⁿ_𝓕(M)) ≠ 0 (resp. Hom_𝒞(σ, gr^𝓕_n(M)) ≠ 0). We write d^M_rad and d^soc_M for the radical and socle filtrations.
items.note: Well defined only for semisimple 𝓕, which is how it is used; for a non-semisimple 𝓕 no such n need exist (see source issue E16). The F-points-to relation and the filtered graphs, previously bundled here, are now def-F-points-to and def-extension-graphs. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: Require semisimple filtration for the Hom-to-grade definition; for arbitrary grades a factor need not be in the socle of its grade.

api.name: filtered_arrow_grades
api.statement: A filtered arrow relates consecutive relevant grades.

api.name: subquotient_full_graph
api.statement: Subquotients inherit the full digraph on their vertices and the restricted filtration.

unitTests: The nonsplit length-two extension has depths 0 and 1 for the radical filtration.
The same extension reverses depth order under the socle filtration.
A split sum has no filtered arrows even if placed in distinct grades.

items.name: §4.1.1 — '𝓕-points to'
items.statement: Let M be multiplicity free and 𝓕 a semisimple filtration on M. For σ, σ′ ∈ JH(M), σ 𝓕-points to σ′ if σ points to σ′ and the (shifted) filtration induced by 𝓕 on the subquotient isomorphic to a nontrivial extension of σ by σ′ has length 2. 'rad-points' and 'soc-points' refer to the radical and socle filtrations.
items.note: For decreasing 𝓕 this means d_𝓕(σ′) = d_𝓕(σ)+1; for increasing 𝓕, d^𝓕(σ) = d^𝓕(σ′)+1. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.1.1 — extension graphs Γ(M), Γ_𝓕(M), Γ^𝓕(M)
items.statement: If M is multiplicity free, Γ(M) is the directed graph with vertex set JH(M) and an arrow σ → σ′ iff σ points to σ′. For a decreasing (resp. increasing) semisimple filtration 𝓕, Γ_𝓕(M) (resp. Γ^𝓕(M)) is the subgraph with the same vertices and an arrow σ → σ′ iff σ 𝓕-points to σ′. Γ_rad(M) and Γ^soc(M) denote the cases of the radical and socle filtrations.
items.note: The paper calls Γ(M) a 'directed acyclic graph'; see fact-gamma-acyclic. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.1.1 — acyclicity of Γ(M)
items.statement: If M is multiplicity free, the directed graph Γ(M) has no directed cycles.
items.locator: §4.1.1, published p. 76 ('we can attach a directed acyclic graph Γ(M)')
items.note: Asserted without proof. It follows from the closedness part of Proposition 4.1.1: if σ₁ → … → σ_k → σ₁ were a cycle, let N be the minimal subobject with σ₁ ∈ JH(N) and N′ ⊂ N a maximal subobject. Then σ₁ ∉ JH(N′) but σ_k ∈ JH(N′), and closedness of JH(N′) forces σ₁ ∈ JH(N′), a contradiction. It is used in the proof of Proposition 4.1.1 and in the proof of Theorem 4.2.7(3). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.1.1 — extension paths
items.statement: An extension path in M is a directed path in Γ(M); an extension path in a semisimple filtration 𝓕 is a directed path in Γ_𝓕(M) (resp. Γ^𝓕(M)). Its length is its number of arrows.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 4.1.2 — extension graphs of subquotients
items.statement: Let M be multiplicity free and N a subquotient of M. A semisimple filtration 𝓕 on M induces a semisimple filtration on N, and Γ(N) (resp. Γ_𝓕(N), Γ^𝓕(N)) is the full subgraph of Γ(M) (resp. Γ_𝓕(M), Γ^𝓕(M)) on the vertex set JH(N).
items.note: Stated as 'immediate from the definitions'. The nontrivial direction (an arrow of Γ(M) between constituents of N is realised inside N) uses Proposition 4.1.1: if σ points to σ′ in M, no τ lies strictly between them along a path, so the relevant length-2 subquotient can be cut out of N. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.1.3 — predecessors in the Loewy filtrations
items.statement: Let M be multiplicity free and σ ∈ JH(M). If d^M_rad(σ) > 0, there is σ′ ∈ JH(M) with d^M_rad(σ′) = d^M_rad(σ) − 1 such that σ′ rad-points to σ. Dually, if d^soc_M(σ) > 0, there is σ′ with d^soc_M(σ′) = d^soc_M(σ) − 1 such that σ soc-points to σ′.
items.note: Proof: with d = d_rad(σ), look at rad^{d−1}(M)/rad^{d+1}(M), which has Loewy length 2. If no σ′ in its top pointed to σ, then σ would split off and not lie in its radical gr^d_rad(M). Corollary 4.1.4, previously bundled here, is now cor-4-1-4. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: Successively select a nonsplit extension with a factor in the adjacent grade; otherwise that factor would split off earlier.

items.name: Corollary 4.1.4 — extension paths realising Loewy depth
items.statement: Let M be multiplicity free and σ ∈ JH(M). There is an extension path in the radical filtration of length d^M_rad(σ) ending with σ, and an extension path in the socle filtration of length d^soc_M(σ) beginning with σ.
items.note: Induction on the depth using Lemma 4.1.3. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.1.5 — arrows strictly decrease the degree in an increasing semisimple filtration
items.statement: Let M be multiplicity free and 𝓕 an increasing semisimple filtration on M. If σ points to σ′, then d^𝓕_M(σ) > d^𝓕_M(σ′).
items.note: Proof: 𝓕_{d(σ)}(M) is a subobject containing σ, hence σ′ by Proposition 4.1.1, so d(σ) ≥ d(σ′). If they were equal, gr_d would contain σ ⊕ σ′ as a subquotient, which contradicts closedness. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Proposition 4.1.6 — rigidity criterion via extension paths
items.statement: Let M ∈ 𝒞 be multiplicity free. Then M is rigid if and only if for every σ ∈ JH(M) there is an extension path in the radical filtration of length ℓℓ(M) − 1 − d^M_rad(σ) beginning with σ; equivalently, if and only if for every σ there is an extension path in the socle filtration of length ℓℓ(M) − 1 − d^soc_M(σ) ending with σ.
items.note: Proof: if M is rigid, the radical path from Corollary 4.1.4 is also a socle path. Conversely, Lemma 4.1.5 applied along the path gives d_soc(σ) ≥ ℓℓ−1−d_rad(σ), and (4.1) gives the reverse inequality, so rad^n = soc_{ℓℓ−1−n}. Each direction is written for one of the two dual versions. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: Arrow paths bound the opposite filtration depth from below; equation (4.1) gives the reverse inequality. Equality for every factor gives equality of subobjects via multiplicity-freeness.

items.name: Proposition 4.1.7 — duality reverses extension graphs
items.statement: Let M ∈ 𝒞 be multiplicity free. Then the dual object M* in the dual abelian category 𝒞* is multiplicity free; a decreasing filtration 𝓕 on M gives an increasing filtration 𝓕* on M*; and σ ↦ σ* induces isomorphisms of directed graphs Γ(M) ≅ Γ(M*)ᵀ and Γ_𝓕(M) ≅ Γ^{𝓕*}(M*)ᵀ, where ᵀ is the transpose (all arrows reversed). In particular, if σ₀ → σ₁ → ⋯ → σₙ is an extension path in 𝓕, then σₙ* → σ*_{n−1} → ⋯ → σ₀* is an extension path in 𝓕*.
items.note: Corrected statement: the paper prints 'Γ(M) ≅ Γ(M*)' without the transpose (E10) and 'Γ^{𝓕*}(M)*' for Γ^{𝓕*}(M*)* (new misprint). Called 'self-evident': an exact contravariant duality turns 0→σ′→E→σ→0 into 0→σ*→E*→σ′*→0. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: Dualise 0→T→E→S→0 to 0→S*→E*→T*→0. Both unrestricted and filtered graphs require transposition.

items.name: [Her09, Appendix, Theorem 3.4] — generic Deligne–Lusztig representations are residually multiplicity free
items.statement: Let R be a 2-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation of G = ∏_{v∈S} GL₃(k_v) over E. Then R is residually multiplicity free: the reduction mod ϖ of an O-lattice in R is multiplicity free.
items.note: Cited, not proved (via the proof of Proposition 2.3.5). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.1.2 — the lattices R^σ with irreducible cosocle
items.statement: Let R be a 2-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation of G over E (E large enough). For each σ ∈ JH(R̄) there is an O-lattice R^σ ⊆ R, unique up to homothety, such that its reduction R̄^σ := R^σ ⊗_O 𝔽 has irreducible cosocle isomorphic to σ.
items.note: Cited from [EGS15, Lemma 4.1.1], which applies because R is residually multiplicity free (cite-her09-multiplicity-free). The elements of JH(R̄) are p-regular (Lemma 4.2.13). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: The original EGS15 §4.1 proof was read: residual multiplicity-freeness gives existence and uniqueness of the cosocle lattice up to homothety. The Deligne–Lusztig multiplicity-free input and unramified coefficient descent remain G02.

api.name: cosocle_lattice
api.statement: cosoc(R^sigma/varpi)=sigma.

api.name: homothety_unique
api.statement: Two such lattices differ by an E-scalar.

unitTests: For a one-dimensional representation there is one homothety class.
Changing a lattice by varpi preserves its reduced isomorphism type.
Repeated residual factors do not satisfy the multiplicity-free input.

items.name: §4.1.2 — notation d^σ_rad
items.statement: With R fixed as in §4.1.2 and σ ∈ JH(R̄), for σ′ ∈ JH(R̄) write d^σ_rad(σ′) := d^{R̄^σ}_rad(σ′), the radical-filtration degree of σ′ in R̄^σ (see D11).
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Definition 4.1.8 — graph predicted by the extension graph
items.statement: Let V be a set of (isomorphism classes of) Serre weights σ = F(μ) with μ p-regular, σ ∈ V, and Γ a directed graph with vertex set V. Γ is predicted by the extension graph with respect to σ if, for all κ₁, κ₂ ∈ V, there is an edge κ₁ → κ₂ if and only if d_gph(κ₁, κ₂) = 1 and d_gph(σ, κ₁) ≤ d_gph(σ, κ₂).
items.note: D_gph is the graph distance of Definition 2.1.8. Since the extension graph is bipartite (Remark 2.1.11), '≤' is effectively '<' on edges. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Theorem 4.1.9(1), first assertion — radical depth equals graph distance
items.statement: Let R be a 13-generic Deligne–Lusztig representation of G = ∏_{v∈S} GL₃(k_v) over E and σ ∈ JH(R̄). Then d_gph(σ, κ) = d^σ_rad(κ) for all κ ∈ JH(R̄).
items.note: Proved at the end of §4.3 (defect-zero lower-alcove case in Theorem 4.2.16, then induction on defect). By Remark 4.1.10, (1) follows from (3) and Proposition 4.1.1. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: T24 plus T20. No generalisation to nongeneric types or arbitrary groups is claimed.

items.name: Theorem 4.1.9(1), second assertion — Loewy length formula
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of T25, ℓℓ(R̄^σ) = 2·Def_R(σ) + 3(f − Def_R(σ)) + 1 (= 3f − Def_R(σ) + 1), where f = #𝒥 = Σ_{v∈S} [k_v : 𝔽_p] and Def_R(σ) is the defect of Definition 2.3.8.
items.note: Follows from T25 together with T02: every maximal geodesic from σ in JH(R̄) has length 3f − Def_R(σ). Per embedding the maximal distance is 2 at inner and 3 at outer components. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: Take maximum radical depth using T02, then add one for zero-based grades.

items.name: Theorem 4.1.9(2) — radical extension graph is predicted
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of T25, Γ_rad(R̄^σ) is predicted by the extension graph with respect to σ: for κ₁, κ₂ ∈ JH(R̄), κ₁ rad-points to κ₂ in R̄^σ iff d_gph(κ₁, κ₂) = 1 and d_gph(σ, κ₁) ≤ d_gph(σ, κ₂).
items.note: Follows from (3) and Proposition 4.1.1 (Remark 4.1.10). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: Apply T17 to T25.

items.name: Theorem 4.1.9(3) — full extension graph is predicted
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of T25, Γ(R̄^σ) is predicted by the extension graph with respect to σ: for κ₁, κ₂ ∈ JH(R̄), κ₁ points to κ₂ in R̄^σ iff d_gph(κ₁, κ₂) = 1 and d_gph(σ, κ₁) ≤ d_gph(σ, κ₂).
items.note: The key assertion. Combined with Proposition 4.1.1 it classifies the submodules of R̄^σ. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: T27 supplies every outward edge. T09 permits only graph edges. A reversed edge would create a two-cycle, impossible for the extension graph of a multiplicity-free finite-length object.

items.name: Theorem 4.1.9(4) — rigidity
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of T25, R̄^σ is rigid.
items.note: Follows from (1), (2), Proposition 4.1.6 and Proposition 2.3.5 (Remark 4.1.10). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: Every directed path extends to maximum possible length using the product model T02; apply T05 to T25 and T27.

items.name: Theorem 4.1.9(5) — p-power relation between saturated lattices
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of T25, if κ ∈ JH(R̄) and R^κ ↪ R^σ is a saturated inclusion, then p^{d_gph(κ,σ)} R^σ ↪ R^κ is a saturated inclusion.
items.note: 'Saturated inclusion' (Λ′ ⊆ Λ with Λ′ ⊄ ϖΛ) is not defined in the paper; its meaning is implicit in Definition 4.3.4 and Remark 4.3.5 (§4.3). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: T24 and T18 identify d_sat with graph distance. The exponent is of p; replacing it with varpi changes the assertion after ramified coefficient extension.

items.name: Remark 4.1.10 — reductions among the parts of Theorem 4.1.9
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 4.1.9: item (4) follows from items (1) and (2) together with Proposition 4.1.6 (using T02); and item (3) together with Proposition 4.1.1 classifies the submodules of R̄^σ, from which items (1) and (2) follow. Hence to prove (1)–(4) for a given σ it suffices to prove (3).
items.note: Used in the proof of Theorem 4.2.16. For (4): given κ, extend a geodesic from σ through κ to a maximal one (length ℓℓ−1 by T02). By (1) and (2) it is a radical extension path of length ℓℓ−1−d_rad(κ) from κ, so Proposition 4.1.6 applies. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Remark 4.1.10 (first sentence) — maximal geodesics from σ in JH(R̄) have equal length
items.statement: Let R be a generic Deligne–Lusztig representation as in Theorem 4.1.9 and σ ∈ JH(R̄). Every maximal (non-extendable) geodesic for d_gph that starts at σ and has all its vertices in JH(R̄) has the same length, namely 3f − Def_R(σ).
items.note: The length value is implicit from Theorem 4.1.9(1). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: Prove one nine-point factor by enumeration and extend using sums. Executed finite checks for |J|=1,2 are evidence, not a proof for arbitrary products.

items.name: §4.2 — general reductive setting for injective envelopes
items.statement: G₀ is a connected reductive group over 𝔽_p and G := G₀ ×_{𝔽_p} 𝔽, assumed split and isomorphic to G_s ×_{𝔽_p} 𝔽 for a connected split reductive G_s over 𝔽_p. G₀^der is the derived subgroup of G₀, assumed simply connected, and G^der := G₀^der ×_{𝔽_p} 𝔽. The finite groups are G := G₀(𝔽_p) and G^der := G₀^der(𝔽_p). F : G → G is the relative Frobenius with respect to G_s; π is an automorphism of G_s (and of its based root datum) such that F∘π is the relative Frobenius with respect to G₀. h is the Coxeter number of G. The main case is G a product of copies of GL₃ (h = 3).
items.note: Algebraic groups are underlined in the paper and finite groups are roman; here 'G' is used for both when the context is clear. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: [Alp86, §6, Theorems 4 and 6] — projective covers equal injective envelopes over 𝔽[G]
items.statement: For an irreducible 𝔽[G]-module σ, let Proj(σ) be its projective cover and Inj(σ) its injective envelope in the category of 𝔽[G]-modules. Since 𝔽[G] is a Frobenius (indeed symmetric) algebra, Proj(σ) ≅ Inj(σ).
items.note: Cited, not proved. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.2.1 — Frobenius kernels, L₁(μ), L̂₁(μ) and Q̂₁(μ)
items.statement: G₁ is the Frobenius kernel of G and G₁T the product of T and G₁ in G; G₁^der and G₁^der T^der are defined similarly. For μ ∈ X₁(T), L₁(μ) := L(μ)|_{G₁} and L̂₁(μ) := L(μ)|_{G₁T}. Q̂₁(μ) is the injective envelope of L̂₁(μ) in the category of G₁T-modules; its restriction to G₁ is an injective envelope of L₁(μ) in G₁-modules, and it is also a projective cover of L₁(μ).
items.note: The irreducibility of L(μ)|_{G₁T} and L(μ)|_{G₁} is cite-jan03-restricted-irreducible. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: [Jan03, II.3.10 and II.9.6] — restricted simple modules stay simple on G₁T and G₁
items.statement: For μ ∈ X₁(T), the G-module L(μ) remains irreducible when restricted to G₁T and to G₁.
items.note: Cited from Jantzen's book, not proved. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: [Jan03, II.11.11] — G-structure on Q̂₁(λ)
items.statement: If p ≥ 2h − 2, then for every λ ∈ X₁(T) the G₁T-module Q̂₁(λ) admits a structure of G-module extending its G₁T-structure, unique up to isomorphism.
items.note: Cited from Jantzen's book ('well known'); the paper states it under p > 2(h−1) and no A₁ factors. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Theorem 4.2.1 (first part) — the G-module Q₁(μ)
items.statement: Assume p > 2(h−1) and that G has no factors of type A₁. For μ ∈ X₁(T), Q̂₁(μ) has a unique (up to isomorphism) G-module structure extending its G₁T-structure, denoted Q₁(μ). In particular soc_G Q₁(μ) ≅ L(μ), since L(μ) is the unique G-module extending L̂₁(μ).
items.note: Cited from [Jan03, II.11.11] (cite-jan03-II-11-11). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Theorem 4.2.1 (4.2) — Q₁(μ) restricts to the projective/injective hull over G(𝔽_p)
items.statement: Assume p > 2(h−1), G has no factors of type A₁, and μ ∈ X₁(T) is (h−2)-deep. Then Q₁(μ)|_G ≅ Proj(F(μ)) ≅ Inj(F(μ)) as 𝔽[G]-modules, where F(μ) = L(μ)|_G.
items.note: Deduced from [Pil93, Lemma 6.1] (semisimple case, also valid when non-split) via Claims 1 and 2: Q₁(μ)|_{G^der} ≅ Inj(F(μ)|_{G^der}) (4.5). Injectivity over G uses exactness of G/G^der-invariants, and the socle comparison uses Claim 1. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: [Pil93, Lemma 6.1] — Q₁(μ) restricted to the finite group is an injective hull (semisimple case)
items.statement: For G semisimple and simply connected, p > 2(h−1) and μ ∈ X₁(T) (h−2)-deep, Q₁(μ)|_{G(𝔽_p)} is an injective hull of F(μ) = L(μ)|_{G(𝔽_p)}; the statement also holds in the non-split case (final remark of [Pil93, §11]). Applied to G^der it gives (4.5): Q₁(μ)|_{G^der} ≅ Inj(F(μ)|_{G^der}).
items.note: Cited, not proved; the hypotheses are the ones the paper uses. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: (4.3) — Ext over G_• versus its derived subgroup (diagonalizable quotient)
items.statement: Let Z := G/G^der and Z₁ := G₁/G₁^der. For • ∈ {∅, 1}, Z_• is diagonalizable, and restriction induces canonical isomorphisms Ext^i_{G_•}(M, N) ≅ H⁰(Z_•, Ext^i_{G_•^der}(M|_{G_•^der}, N|_{G_•^der})) for all i ∈ ℕ and all G_•-modules M, N.
items.locator: §4.2.1, proof of Theorem 4.2.1, Claim 1, (4.3), published p. 80
items.note: From the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence [Jan03, I.6.9(3)] (cited) and the vanishing of higher cohomology of diagonalizable groups. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: (4.4) — Ext over G(𝔽_p) versus G^der(𝔽_p)
items.statement: Since Z := G/G^der (finite groups) has order prime to p, restriction induces canonical isomorphisms Ext^i_G(M, N) ≅ H⁰(Z, Ext^i_{G^der}(M|_{G^der}, N|_{G^der})) for all i ∈ ℕ and all 𝔽[G]-modules M, N.
items.note: |G/G^der| is prime to p because G₀^der is simply connected (Lang), so G/G^der embeds in the 𝔽_p-points of a torus. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Theorem 4.2.1, Claim 1 — socles commute with restriction to derived subgroups
items.statement: Let M be a G-module. Then soc_{G^der}(M|_{G^der}) = soc_G(M)|_{G^der}. The analogous statements hold for G₁T and G₁^der T^der, and for the finite groups G and G^der.
items.locator: §4.2.1, proof of Theorem 4.2.1, Claim 1, published pp. 80–81
items.note: Proof: irreducible G_•-modules stay irreducible on G_•^der, so by (4.3) (resp. (4.4)) restriction commutes with socles and cosocles; [Jan03, II.9.6(11)] handles G₁T. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Theorem 4.2.1, Claim 2 — Q̂₁(ν) stays an injective envelope on G₁^der T^der
items.statement: Let ν be a p-restricted weight. Then Q̂₁(ν)|_{G₁^der T^der} is the injective envelope of L̂₁(ν)|_{G₁^der T^der} as a G₁^der T^der-module.
items.locator: §4.2.1, proof of Theorem 4.2.1, Claim 2, published p. 81
items.note: Proof: the socle is right by Claim 1. For injectivity, by [Jan03, II.9.4] it suffices to check on G₁^der, and restriction from the finite group scheme G₁ to its closed subgroup scheme G₁^der preserves injectives, since it has an exact left adjoint [Jan03, I.3.5, I.8.16]. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: [Jan03, II.9.4; I.3.5; I.8.16; II.9.6(11)] — injectivity and socle tools for G₁T-modules
items.statement: (a) A G₁T-module is injective iff its restriction to G₁ is injective [Jan03, II.9.4]. (b) If H ⊂ K are finite group schemes with H closed in K, restriction from K-modules to H-modules has an exact left adjoint and so preserves injectives [Jan03, I.3.5, I.8.16]. (c) The G₁T-socle of a G₁T-module is computed by its G₁-socle [Jan03, II.9.6(11)].
items.locator: §4.2.1, proof of Theorem 4.2.1 (Claims 1 and 2), published pp. 80–81
items.note: Cited black boxes; the paper gives only the section numbers, so the wording here paraphrases how they are used. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.2.1 — p-bounded modules
items.statement: An irreducible G-module L(κ), κ ∈ X*_+(T), is p-bounded if ⟨κ, α^∨⟩ < 2(h−1)p for all coroots α^∨ ∈ R^∨. A G-module is p-bounded if all its Jordan–Hölder factors are p-bounded.
items.note: Introduced with 'Recall', but this is the first occurrence in the paper. Q₁(μ) is p-bounded for μ ∈ X₁(T), since its highest weight 2(p−1)ρ + w₀μ pairs to at most 2(p−1)(h−1). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.2.1 — m-deep G-modules
items.statement: A G-module is m-deep if the highest weights of all its Jordan–Hölder factors are m-deep (Definition 2.1.9: λ is m-deep if for each positive coroot α^∨ there is m_α ∈ ℤ with p·m_α + m < ⟨λ+η, α^∨⟩ < p(m_α+1) − m).
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.2 [Pil97, Lemma 3.1] — Loewy filtrations commute with restriction to G(𝔽_p)
items.statement: Let M be a G-module that is 3(h−1)-deep and p-bounded. Then soc_i^G(M)|_G = soc_i^G(M|_G) and rad^i_G(M)|_G = rad^i_G(M|_G) for all i, where on each side the first G is the algebraic group and the second the finite group G(𝔽_p).
items.note: Cited from [Pil97, Lemma 3.1] and adapted: the socle case for G^der comes from Pillen's proof with n = 1, using L(pλ₁)|_{G^der} ≅ L(πλ₁)|_{G^der} in the non-split case. The radical case follows by duality, and the general case from Claim 1. The printed duality identity is wrong (see source issue), but the argument works with soc_{i−1}(M*) = (M/rad^i M)*. The paper writes 'p-bounded highest weight'; p-boundedness of all JH factors is what is meant. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Corollary 4.2.3 — Loewy filtrations of Inj(F(μ)) come from Q₁(μ)
items.statement: Let μ ∈ X₁(T) be such that Q₁(μ) is 3(h−1)-deep (with p > 2(h−1) and no A₁ factors, so that Q₁(μ) is defined). Then soc_i^G(Q₁(μ))|_G = soc_i^G(Inj(F(μ))) and rad^i_G(Q₁(μ))|_G = rad^i_G(Inj(F(μ))) for all i.
items.note: From Theorem 4.2.1 and Lemma 4.2.2 (Q₁(μ) is automatically p-bounded). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.2.1 — weight multiplicities m_κ(ν)
items.statement: For ν, κ ∈ X*(T), m_κ(ν) := dim_𝔽 (L(κ))_ν, the dimension of the ν-weight space of L(κ); 'ν ∈ L(κ)' abbreviates (L(κ))_ν ≠ 0.
items.note: Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.4(1) — translation principle for simple modules
items.statement: Assume p ≥ 2(h−1). Let λ, ξ ∈ X₁(T) be such that for every weight ν ∈ L(ξ) the weight λ + ν lies in the same alcove as λ. Then L(λ) ⊗_𝔽 L(ξ) ≅ ⊕_{ν∈L(ξ)} L(λ+ν)^{⊕ m_ξ(ν)} as G-modules.
items.note: Proof: the isomorphism holds on the derived group by [Pil93, Lemma 5.1] and extends to G via (4.3), because both sides have the same central character. The printed proof says 'G₁^der' where G^der is meant (source issue). Used throughout (e.g. L(λ⁰)⊗L(πω)|_G decompositions). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.4(2) — translation principle for Q₁
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 4.2.4(1) (and with Q₁ defined, i.e. no A₁ factors), Q₁(λ) ⊗_𝔽 L(ξ) ≅ ⊕_{ν∈L(ξ)} Q₁(λ+ν)^{⊕ m_ξ(ν)} as G-modules.
items.note: Proof: [Pil93, Lemma 5.1] gives the G₁T-isomorphism (4.6) Q̂₁(λ)⊗L̂₁(ξ) ≅ ⊕ Q̂₁(λ+ν)^{m_ξ(ν)}. Item (1) and soc Q₁(λ) ≅ L(λ) give the socle embedding (4.7). Claim (4.8) (Hom_G(−, Q₁(λ)⊗L(ξ)) is exact on p-bounded modules) extends it to an injection ⊕Q₁(λ+ν)^{m} ↪ Q₁(λ)⊗L(ξ), which is an isomorphism by (4.6). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: [Pil93, Lemma 5.1] — translation principle (semisimple simply connected case)
items.statement: For G semisimple and simply connected and λ, ξ ∈ X₁(T) such that λ + ν lies in the alcove of λ for all ν ∈ L(ξ): L(λ)⊗L(ξ) ≅ ⊕_{ν∈L(ξ)} L(λ+ν)^{m_ξ(ν)} and, as G₁T-modules, Q̂₁(λ)⊗L̂₁(ξ) ≅ ⊕_{ν∈L̂₁(ξ)} Q̂₁(λ+ν)^{m_ξ(ν)} (4.6).
items.note: Cited, not proved; stated here in the form the paper uses. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: (4.8) — Q₁(λ)⊗L(ξ) is injective among p-bounded G-modules
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 4.2.4, Ext¹_G(L(κ), Q₁(λ) ⊗_𝔽 L(ξ)) = 0 for every irreducible p-bounded G-module L(κ). Equivalently, Hom_G(−, Q₁(λ)⊗L(ξ)) is exact on the full subcategory of p-bounded G-modules.
items.note: Proof: write κ = κ^(0) + pω_κ with κ^(0) ∈ X₁(T) and ⟨ω_κ, α^∨⟩ < 2(h−1). Since Q̂₁(λ) is G₁-injective, the Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence [Jan03, I.6.6(3), I.6.5(2)] and (4.6) reduce to Ext¹_G(L(ω_κ), L((λ+ν−κ^(0))/p)) with (λ+ν−κ^(0))/p ∈ X⁰(T), which vanishes. The printed justification ('2(h−1) ≤ p−2', 'ω_κ lies in the lower alcove') is flawed but the vanishing holds (source issue). Reused in Lemma 4.2.11 ('by the proof of (4.8)'). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: [Jan03, I.6.6(3), I.6.5(2)] — Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for G₁ ⊲ G
items.statement: For G-modules V, W there is a spectral sequence E₂^{i,j} = Ext^i_{G/G₁}(k, Ext^j_{G₁}(V, W)) ⇒ Ext^{i+j}_G(V, W). If W is injective as a G₁-module, it degenerates to Ext^i_G(V, W) ≅ Ext^i_{G/G₁}(k, Hom_{G₁}(V, W)).
items.note: Cited from Jantzen's book, in the form it is applied: with V = L(κ^(0)) ⊗ L(ω_κ)^{[1]}, Ext¹_G(L(κ), W) ≅ Ext¹_{G/G₁}(L(pω_κ), Hom_{G₁}(L₁(κ^(0)), W)). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.2.2 — alcove labels 𝒜 = {A,…,J} and elements w̃_X
items.statement: G₀ = ∏_{v∈S} Res_{k_v/𝔽_p} GL₃ as in §1.4 and f := #𝒥. Using the alcove labelling for SL₃ of [Hum06, §13.9], 𝒜 := {A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J} (A = C₀ the lowest alcove and B = C₁ the upper p-restricted alcove). For X ∈ 𝒜, w̃_X ∈ W_a is the unique element with w̃_X · C₀ = X (p-dot action). For i ∈ 𝒥, w̃_{X,i} ∈ W_a is w̃_X in the i-th factor and the identity elsewhere, and for X = (X_i) ∈ 𝒜^𝒥, w̃_X := (w̃_{X_i})_i.
items.note: Table 5 pins down the labels via explicit elements: C = (123)t_{−α₂}·A, D = (132)t_{−α₁}·A, E = (12)t_{α₂}·A, F = (23)t_{α₁}·A, G = t_{η′}·A, J = (13)t_{−2η′}·A, with conventions w̃ = w t_λ acting by x ↦ w(x + pλ + η) − η and (s x)_k = x_{s⁻¹(k)}. In pairing coordinates (⟨·+η, α₁^∨⟩, ⟨·+η, α₂^∨⟩, ⟨·+η, α₀^∨⟩) this gives C ⊂ (0,p)×(p,2p)×(p,2p), D ⊂ (p,2p)×(0,p)×(p,2p), E ⊂ (0,p)×(p,2p)×(2p,3p) and F ⊂ (p,2p)×(0,p)×(2p,3p). Table 6 and the proof of Proposition 4.2.12 use the mirror labelling (C↔D, E↔F); see source issue. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.2.2 — μ^op, the Weyl modules V_{μ_i} and V_μ, and Q₁(μ)
items.statement: Assume p ≥ 5 and μ ∈ X₁(T) is 2-deep. Set μ^op := w̃_B · μ = Σ_i μ_i^op. For each i, Q₁(μ_i) is the GL₃-module of Theorem 4.2.1, and V_{μ_i} := V(μ_i^op + pη′_i) is the Weyl module of highest weight μ_i^op + pη′_i (extended from GL_{3/𝔽_p}), which is a submodule of Q₁(μ_i) through its Weyl filtration. Then Q₁(μ) := ⊗_i Q₁(μ_i) and V_μ := ⊗_i V_{μ_i} as G = ∏_i GL₃-modules.
items.note: Η′_i = (1,0,−1) in the i-th coordinate. For μ_i ∈ B, μ_i^op ∈ A and μ_i^op + pη′_i = 2(p−1)ρ + w₀μ_i is the highest weight of Q₁(μ_i). The embedding V_{μ_i} ⊂ Q₁(μ_i) comes from the Weyl filtration [Jan03, II.11.13, II.11.5(5), II.4.19; Hum06, §13.9]. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: [Hum06 §13.9; AM01 Prop. 8.4; Jan03 II.11.13, II.11.5(5), II.4.19, II.D.4] — structure of Q₁(μ_i) for GL₃
items.statement: For p ≥ 5 and μ_i ∈ X₁(T) 2-deep (GL₃), Q₁(μ_i) is rigid of Loewy length 6 + 1 = 7, has a Weyl filtration with V_{μ_i} = V(μ_i^op + pη′_i) as a submodule, and its socle filtration is known explicitly.
items.note: Cited, not proved. The paper writes 'ℓℓ(Q₁(μ)) = 6+1' where Q₁(μ_i) is meant (source issue). The published bibliography lists AM01 as 'H. H. Andersen and K. Masaharu'; the authors are H. H. Andersen and M. Kaneda. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: [BDM15, §4] and Table 6 — socle layers of V_{μ_i}
items.statement: For p ≥ 5 and μ_i 2-deep, the socle filtration of the Weyl module V_{μ_i} = V(μ_i^op + pη′_i) is known: V_{μ_i} has maximal length and Loewy length 3 + 1 = 4, and it is a multiplicity-free submodule of Q₁(μ_i). Its extension graph for μ_i ∈ B, resp. A, is Table 6.
items.note: Cited from [BDM15, §4] (Bowman–Doty–Martin, SL₃ tensor products for p ≥ 5). 2-depth is what guarantees maximal length. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.2.2 — rigidity and Loewy series of Q₁(μ) and V_μ
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of def-mu-op-V-mu, Q₁(μ) is rigid with ℓℓ(Q₁(μ)) = 6f + 1, and its socle filtration is the tensor product of the socle filtrations of the Q₁(μ_i), i ∈ 𝒥. The graph Γ(V_μ) is the product ∏_i Γ(V_{μ_i}); in particular V_μ is rigid. Fil denotes the unique increasing Loewy series of Q₁(μ); its restriction to V_μ is the unique Loewy series of V_μ.
items.note: Stated without proof (external tensor products over a product group). Fil is used for gr_d(V_μ) in Theorem 4.2.7. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.2.2 — n-deep 𝔽[G]-modules
items.statement: An irreducible 𝔽[G]-module F is n-deep if F ≅ L(μ)|_{G(𝔽_p)} for some n-deep μ ∈ X₁(T). An 𝔽[G]-module is n-deep if all its Jordan–Hölder constituents are n-deep.
items.note: Same notion as for Serre weights in §2.1. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.5 (first claim) — depth is preserved by the extended affine Weyl group
items.statement: Let μ ∈ X*(T), n ∈ ℕ and w̃ ∈ W̃. If μ is n-deep in alcove a, then w̃·μ is n-deep in alcove w̃·a.
items.note: 'Easy': the p-dot action permutes the root hyperplanes. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.5 (second claim) — Q₁(μ) and V_μ are as deep as μ
items.statement: If μ ∈ X₁(T) is n-deep, then the G-modules Q₁(μ) and V_μ are n-deep.
items.note: Their constituents are L(w̃·μ) with w̃ ∈ W_a (linkage), so this follows from the first claim. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.5 (third claim) — restrictions to G(𝔽_p) lose at most 2 of depth
items.statement: If μ ∈ X₁(T) is (n+2)-deep, then Q₁(μ)|_G and V_μ|_G are n-deep.
items.note: Proof: Q₁(μ)|_G and V_μ|_G have the same constituents. For L = L(λ) ∈ JH(V_μ) with λ = λ⁰ + pω_λ, L|_G ≅ (L(λ⁰)⊗L(πω_λ))|_G ≅ ⊕_{ε∈L(πω_λ)} L(λ⁰+ε)|_G^{m(ε)} by Lemma 4.2.4(1), and |⟨ε, α^∨⟩| ≤ 2. The printed formula 'L|_G ≅ L(λ⁰+πω_λ) ≅ ⊕ L(λ+ε)' is a misprint (source issue). This depth loss matters for the depth bookkeeping in §4.2.3–4.2.4 (source issue). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.2.2 — socle filtration of Inj(F(μ)) for μ 6-deep
items.statement: Assume μ ∈ X₁(T) is 6-deep. The socle filtration of Inj(F(μ)) is (Fil_n Q₁(μ))|_G. Inj(F(μ)) is rigid, so this is its unique increasing Loewy series. Lemma 4.2.4 can be used to compute gr_n Inj(F(μ)).
items.note: From Corollary 4.2.3 (Q₁(μ) is 6-deep by Lemma 4.2.5). The paper justifies rigidity by 'it is isomorphic to Proj(F(μ))', which is not enough; rigidity follows from Corollary 4.2.3 and rigidity of Q₁(μ) (source issue). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.6 — Ext¹ between Serre weights is detected by the extension graph
items.statement: Let G = ∏_{v∈S} GL₃(k_v) and μ ∈ X₁(T) with every μ_i 6-deep, and σ := F(μ). For every Serre weight κ: d_gph(σ, κ) = 1 (κ adjacent to σ) if and only if Ext¹_G(κ, σ) ≠ 0, in which case dim_𝔽 Ext¹_G(κ, σ) = 1.
items.locator: §4.2.2, Lemma 4.2.6, published p. 85; restated as Theorem 2.1.10 (published p. 15)
items.note: Proof: Q₁(μ)|_G ≅ Inj(σ) with socle filtration Fil|_G, so Ext¹_G(κ,σ) ≅ Hom_G(κ, gr₁). gr₁Q₁(μ) = ⊕_i gr₁Q₁(μ_i) ⊗ ⊗_{j≠i} L(μ_j) has 3f constituents L(w̃·μ) (fact-gr1-Q1), and (4.9)–(4.10) identify L(w̃·μ)|_G with the multiplicity-free sum of F(Tr_{λ+η}(ω, π(w̃_{B,i}w̃_μ·A))), ω a permutation of πω_−. These are exactly the 7f neighbours of σ. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).
items.proofOutline: Use Q1(mu)|G=Inj(F(mu)), compute its first socle layer by translation (4.9) and compare weights via (4.10). This needs Frobenius-kernel injectives, Jantzen/Pillen and the translation theorem: G03.

items.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2.6 — the second socle layer of Q₁(μ)
items.statement: Let μ ∈ X₁(T) be 6-deep and w̃_μ ∈ W_a with λ := w̃_μ⁻¹·μ ∈ A. Then gr₁Q₁(μ) = ⊕_i (gr₁Q₁(μ_i)) ⊗ ⊗_{j≠i} L(μ_j) has length 3f, with constituents L(w̃·μ) for 3f elements w̃ = t_{ω_−} w̃_+. Here ω_− ∈ {0, ε′_{1,i}, ε′_{2,i}} for some i ∈ 𝒥, and w̃_+ ∈ W̃₁⁺ is the unique element with t_{ω_−}w̃_+ ∈ W_a and w̃_+w̃_μ·A = w̃_{B,i}w̃_μ·A.
items.note: Relies on the cited structure of Q₁ (cite-q1-gl3-structure). For f = 1 and μ ∈ A the constituents lie in alcoves B, E, F (Table 5, rows B, E, F). For μ ∈ B they lie in A, C, D. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: (4.9)–(4.10) — restriction of L(t_{ω_−}w̃_+·μ) to G in chart coordinates
items.statement: With notation as in fact-gr1-Q1 and w̃ = t_{ω_{−,i}} w̃_+: L(w̃·μ)|_G ≅ (L(w̃_+·μ) ⊗ L(πω_{−,i}))|_G ≅ ⊕_{ω∈L(πω_{−,i})} F(w̃_+·μ + ω)^{⊕ m_{πω_{−,i}}(ω)} (4.9). If t_ω π(w̃_+w̃_μ) ∈ W_a, then (ω, π(w̃_+w̃_μ·A)) = β(ω, w̃_+w̃_μ) (Lemma 2.1.1) and F(Tr_{λ+η}(ω, π(w̃_+w̃_μ·A))) ≅ F(w̃_+w̃_μ·(λ+ω)) ≅ F(w̃_+·μ + w₊w_μ ω) (4.10), where w₊w_μ is the image of w̃_+w̃_μ in W.
items.locator: §4.2.2, proof of Lemma 4.2.6, (4.9) and (4.10), published pp. 85–86
items.note: (4.9) is the Steinberg tensor product theorem (L(pω)|_G ≅ L(πω)|_G) plus Lemma 4.2.4(1). (4.10) unwinds the definition of Tr (§2.1). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.2.3 — the hexagon Λ_{η′}
items.statement: Λ_{η′} ⊆ Λ_W is the convex hull of the W-orbit of η′. Explicitly, Λ_{η′} = {(ν_i)_i ∈ Λ_W : ν_i ∈ {0, ±ε_{1,i}, ±ε_{2,i}, ±η′_i, ±(ε_{1,i} − ε_{2,i}), ±(2ε_{1,i} − ε_{2,i}), ±(ε_{1,i} − 2ε_{2,i})} for all i}.
items.note: In §4.2.3, G₀ = Res_{k_v/𝔽_p} GL₃ (a single place). Λ_W = X*(T^der), ε_{1}, ε_{2} are the images of ε′₁ = (1,0,0) and ε′₂ = (0,0,−1). Per embedding there are 13 points: 0, the six minuscule weights ±ε₁, ±ε₂, ±(ε₁−ε₂) and the six roots ±η′, ±(2ε₁−ε₂), ±(ε₁−2ε₂). Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: §4.2.3 — the vertex set Λ_{⪯(η′,0)}
items.statement: Λ_{⪯(η′,0)} := {(ω, a) ∈ Λ_{η′} × 𝒜 : a_i = 0 whenever ω_i = wη′_i for some w ∈ W}, where 𝒜 = {0,1}^𝒥 is the set of p-restricted alcoves: roots carry only the lower-alcove label.
items.note: Per embedding: 7 points with both labels plus 6 roots with label 0, so 20 points. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Theorem 4.2.7(1) — Jordan–Hölder constituents of V_μ|_G
items.statement: Let μ ∈ X₁(T) be 2-deep in alcove B (at every embedding). The translation map Tr_{μ^op+η} : Λ_W^{(μ^op+η)} × 𝒜 → X₁(T)/(p−π)X⁰(T) (§2.1) induces a bijection Tr_{V_μ} : Λ_{⪯(η′,0)} → JH(V_μ|_G), (ω, a) ↦ σ_{(ω,a)} := F(Tr_{μ^op+η}(ω, a)).
items.note: Proof (with (2)): for a constituent L(w̃·μ) of V_μ, write w̃ = t_{ω_−}w̃_+ with ω_{−,i} ∈ {0, ε′_{1,i}, ε′_{2,i}, η′_i} (w̃_{+,i} = w̃_{B,i} when ω_{−,i} = η′_i). Then L(w̃·μ)|_G ≅ ⊕_{ε∈L(πω_−)} F(w̃_+·μ+ε)^{m(ε)} (Lemma 4.2.4), and each summand is some σ_{(ω,a)} with (ω,a) ∈ Λ_{⪯(η′,0)}. The printed identification 'σ_{(w₀ε, π(w̃_+w̃_h·A))}' is off by w₊⁻¹ (source issue); this is harmless because the sets are W-stable. σ_{(0,1)} = F(μ) is the socle. Checked for f = 1 against Tables 5–6. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Theorem 4.2.7(2) — the layers of V_μ|_G are governed by graph distance
items.statement: Let μ ∈ X₁(T) be 2-deep in alcove B. For all (ω, a) ∈ Λ_{⪯(η′,0)} and d: [gr_d(V_μ)|_G : σ_{(ω,a)}] = 1 if d = d_gph(σ_{(0,1)}, σ_{(ω,a)}), and = 0 if d < d_gph(σ_{(0,1)}, σ_{(ω,a)}), where gr is taken for the Loewy series Fil of V_μ.
items.note: Proof: define n_i(w̃_i) by [gr_{n_i(w̃_i)}(V_{μ_i}) : L(w̃_i·μ_i)] ≠ 0. A case analysis with the fifth column of Table 5 and the socle layers of V_{μ_i} [BDM15] shows that the distance from the π i-th coordinate to (0_i,1_i) equals n_{π⁻¹i}(w̃_{π⁻¹i}), and that permutation weights of L(πω_−) occur once. Occurrences with d > d_gph are allowed, e.g. the zero weight of L(η′) in the top layer. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Theorem 4.2.7(3)(a)–(c) — a multiplicity-free submodule U ⊂ V_μ|_G
items.statement: Let μ ∈ X₁(T) be 6-deep in alcove B. There is a G-submodule U ⊂ V_μ|_G such that (a) U is multiplicity free; (b) JH(U) = JH(V_μ|_G); (c) for the restricted filtration Fil|_U and every σ ∈ JH(U), [gr_d(U) : σ] = 1 if and only if d = d_gph(σ_{(0,1)}, σ).
items.note: (a)–(c) are Lemma 4.2.8, which only needs μ 2-deep. Missing: routed to the Part II ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups (route 4).

items.name: Theorem 4.2.7(3)(d) — the extension graph of U is predicted
items.statement: Let μ ∈ X₁(T) be 6-deep in alcove B and U as in (a)–(c). For (ω, a), (ω′, a′) ∈ Λ_{⪯(η′,0)}, σ_{(ω,a)} points to σ_{(ω′,a′)} in U if and only if d_gph(σ_{(0,1)}, σ_{(ω,a)}) ≥ d_gph(σ_{(0,1)}, σ_{(ω′,a′)}) and d_gph(σ_{(ω,a)}, σ_{(ω′,a′)}) = 1. In particular Γ(U)^op (all arrows reversed) is predicted by the extension graph with respect to σ_{(0,1)} = F(μ).
items.note: Proof (p. 97): let Γ be the predicted graph (edges σ₁→σ₂ iff d(σ₀₁,σ₁) > d(σ₀₁,σ₂) and d(σ₁,σ₂) = 1). Γ ⊆ Γ(U): take the unique length-2 algebraic subquotient M of Fil_{d₁}(V_μ)/Fil_{d₂−1}(V_μ) (every possible extension occurs, Table 6) and apply Proposition 4.2.10. Conversely, any acyclic Γ′ ⊇ Γ whose edges join adjacent weights equals Γ (bipartiteness), and Γ(U) is such a graph by Lemmas 4.2.5–4.2.6. At the stated depth the appeal to Lemma 4.2.6 is not covered (constituents of U are only 4-deep): see the depth-bookkeeping source issue.
