unitTests: For O[[x,y]]/(xy−p), remove the closed crossing locus.
If the special fibre is irreducible and smooth, no crossing is removed.
With ramified O, reduction is modulo varpi, not p.

items.name: X∞(τ_𝒮) is normal and Cohen–Macaulay
items.statement: In the setting of D20, X∞(τ_𝒮) = Spec R∞(τ_𝒮) is a normal and Cohen–Macaulay scheme.
items.note: Asserted 'by (the proof of) Theorem 3.5.3': each R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ} is a normal Cohen–Macaulay domain with reduced special fibre whose components are formally smooth, and R∞(τ_𝒮) ≅ (⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ})[[x₁,…,x_h]]; the completed tensor product needs the proof, not only the statement, of Theorem 3.5.3. Consequence used implicitly in Theorem 5.2.3: R∞(τ_𝒮) is a local normal ring, hence a domain (when nonzero), so a cyclic module of full support is free of rank one, and R∞(τ_𝒮) = Γ(U, 𝒪_U) (depth ≥ 2 along Z). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: U and j are pulled back from the local deformation space
items.statement: Let U₀ ⊂ Spf(⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}) be defined in the same way as U (complement of the locus of points lying on two irreducible components of the special fibre) and j₀ : U₀ ↪ Spf(⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}) the open immersion. Then j and U are obtained by pulling back j₀ and U₀ along the formally smooth map X∞(τ_𝒮) → Spf(⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}).
items.note: Stated without proof ('Note that'). Justification: the map is R∞(τ_𝒮) ≅ (⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ})[[x₁,…,x_h]] (formally smooth, same residue field), and T62 shows that the minimal primes of the special fibre extend and the crossing locus pulls back. 'Spf' is used for the underlying ordinary spectrum as a point set; j_{0*}, j₀^* are taken on Spec(⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 5.2.1 — U is regular
items.statement: In the setting of D20, the scheme U = X∞(τ_𝒮) \ Z is regular.
items.note: Proof as printed (checked): the irreducible components of the special fibre of X∞(τ_𝒮) are formally smooth over 𝔽 and the special fibre is reduced (last part of Theorem 3.5.3), so the special fibre Ū of U (points on exactly one component) is regular; at a characteristic-p point x, dim_k T_xU ≤ dim_k T_xŪ + 1, and by p-flatness dim 𝒪_{U,x} = dim 𝒪_{Ū,x} + 1, so U is regular at x; the generic fibre of U equals that of X∞(τ_𝒮), which is regular (R∞(τ_𝒮)[1/p] regular). Correct. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).
items.proofOutline: The special fibre is smooth at these points; flatness and tangent-space dimension imply regularity there. The characteristic-zero fibre is regular by the potentially crystalline deformation theorem.

items.name: Notation j^*, j_* on quasi-coherent sheaves
items.statement: j^* : QCoh(X∞(τ_𝒮)) → QCoh(U) is restriction and j_* : QCoh(U) → QCoh(X∞(τ_𝒮)) is pushforward. For an R∞(τ_𝒮)-module M, j_*j^*M̃ is the quasi-coherent sheaf associated with the R∞(τ_𝒮)-module Γ(U, M̃) (D23); for an ideal I ⊂ R∞(τ_𝒮), j_*j^*I is the ideal H_U(I) of D24, and for a submodule N of a module M with j_*j^*M = M, j_*j^*N denotes the corresponding submodule of M.
items.note: The paper uses sheaf and module language interchangeably on the affine scheme X∞(τ_𝒮) (L08). The submodule/ideal interpretation of j_*j^*(·) is implicit in Theorem 5.2.3 and Remark 5.2.4. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The prime ideal p(θ) of a Serre weight θ = ⊗θ_ṽ
items.statement: For θ = ⊗_{ṽ∈𝒮} θ_ṽ ∈ W?(ρ̄_𝒮), p(θ) := Σ_{ṽ∈𝒮} p(θ_ṽ), where p(θ_ṽ) ⊂ R_ṽ^□ is the prime ideal attached to θ_ṽ ∈ W?(ρ̄_ṽ) by Proposition 3.6.1(1) (unique assignment with Spec(R̄_ṽ^{τ}) = ∪_{σ∈W?(ρ̄_ṽ,τ)} Spec(R_ṽ^□/p(σ)) for every tame τ); the sum is formed in ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^□ and extended to R∞ and R∞(τ_𝒮).
items.note: Π ∈ p(θ). By Proposition 3.6.1(2) the scheme-theoretic support of M∞(θ) is Spec(R∞/p(θ)R∞); for θ ∈ W?(ρ̄_𝒮,τ_𝒮) the image of p(θ) in R∞(τ_𝒮) is the height-one prime of the component of the special fibre labelled θ. ∏_θ p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮) is an ordinary product of ideals. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Multiplicity m(θ) of θ in the cokernel of a saturated injection
items.statement: Let σ, κ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮)) and ι : σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ↪ σ(τ_𝒮)^σ a saturated injection of 𝒪-lattices (σ(τ_𝒮)^σ = the lattice, unique up to homothety, with irreducible cosocle σ). For θ ∈ W?(ρ̄_𝒮), m(θ) is the multiplicity with which θ appears (as a Jordan–Hölder factor) in coker ι.
items.note: Coker ι is a K-module of finite length killed by a power of ϖ (ι ⊗ E is an isomorphism). m(θ) = 0 unless θ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮)); σ̄(τ_𝒮) is multiplicity free for 13-generic τ_𝒮, but coker ι can contain θ several times. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Lemma 5.2.2 — image of j^*M∞(ι) on the regular locus
items.statement: Let σ, κ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮)) and let ι : σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ↪ σ(τ_𝒮)^σ be a saturated injection. For any θ = ⊗_{ṽ∈𝒮} θ_ṽ ∈ W?(ρ̄_𝒮), let m(θ) be the multiplicity with which θ appears in the cokernel of ι. Then the induced injection j^*M∞(ι) : j^*M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ) ↪ j^*M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ) has image j^*(∏_{θ∈W?(ρ̄_𝒮)} p(θ)^{m(θ)} M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)), where p(θ) = Σ_{ṽ∈𝒮} p(θ_ṽ).
items.note: Proof: both sheaves are locally free of rank one on U (lemma-5-2-2-locally-free); the image is J ⊗_{𝒪_U} j^*M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ) with J the ideal sheaf of the Cartier divisor of the cokernel, and J = j^*(∏ p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮)) (lemma-5-2-2-divisor-ideal, asserted as 'easily seen'); finally J ⊗ j^*M∞(σ^σ) ≅ J·j^*M∞(σ^σ) = j^*(∏ p(θ)^{m(θ)} M∞(σ^σ)) because j^*M∞(σ^σ) is locally free. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).
items.proofOutline: On U both patched modules are line bundles by MCM regular-local freeness. Their quotient gives a Cartier divisor whose coefficients are the lengths at the corresponding special-fibre components.

items.name: Patched lattices are line bundles on U (step in Lemma 5.2.2)
items.statement: j^*(M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)) and j^*(M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)) are locally free of rank one on U, since they are Cohen–Macaulay of full support over the regular scheme U (Definition 3.5.1).
items.note: Definition 3.5.1(1): M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)°) is p-torsion free and maximal Cohen–Macaulay over R∞(τ_𝒮) (a domain, so full support). At x ∈ U the localization has depth = dim 𝒪_{U,x} (T57), hence is free over the regular local ring 𝒪_{U,x} (general-mcm-regular-free). Rank ≤ 1 by Definition 3.5.1(4) and ≥ 1 by full support; so rank one. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The Cartier divisor of coker j^*M∞(ι) (step in Lemma 5.2.2)
items.statement: The image of j^*M∞(ι) is J ⊗_{𝒪_U} j^*(M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)), where J is the ideal sheaf of the Cartier divisor corresponding to the cokernel of j^*M∞(ι), and J = j^*(∏_{θ∈W?(ρ̄_𝒮)} p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮)).
items.note: The second equality is asserted as 'easily seen' (recorded as a gap). Argument: coker(j^*M∞(ι)) = j^*M∞(coker ι) by exactness of M∞, and M∞(coker ι) is filtered by M∞(θ') for θ' ∈ JH(coker ι) with multiplicity; M∞(θ') = 0 unless θ' ∈ W?(ρ̄_𝒮), and then it is supported on Spec(R∞/p(θ')) with e(M∞(θ')) = 1 (Theorem 3.5.2, Proposition 3.6.1(2)), so its length at the generic point of V(p(θ)) is δ_{θθ'}; the divisor is therefore Σ_θ m(θ)[V(p(θ)) ∩ U], and on the regular scheme U each p(θ)𝒪_U is the invertible ideal of a prime divisor (general-cartier-divisor-line-bundles). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Theorem 5.2.3 — gauge: the image of M∞(ι) is an ideal times M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)
items.statement: With the notation of Lemma 5.2.2 (σ, κ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮)), ι : σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ↪ σ(τ_𝒮)^σ saturated, m(θ), p(θ)), suppose further that σ is as in Theorem 5.1.1, i.e. σ = F(λ) ∈ W?(ρ̄_𝒮, τ_𝒮) with λ_{π^{-1}(i)} ∈ X₁(T) in alcove C₁ for every i ∈ 𝒥 with ℓ(w̃*_i) ≤ 1 (condition (5.1)). Then the induced injection M∞(ι) : M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ) ↪ M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ) has image j_*j^*(∏_{θ∈W?(ρ̄_𝒮)} p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮)) · M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ).
items.note: Proof: (i) for a maximal Cohen–Macaulay sheaf ℳ on X∞(τ_𝒮), j_*j^*ℳ = ℳ (thm-5-2-3-step-extension, cf. [HK04, Prop. 3.5]); applied to im M∞(ι) ≅ M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ) this and Lemma 5.2.2 give im M∞(ι) = j_*j^*(∏ p(θ)^{m(θ)} M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)); (ii) M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ) is free of rank one over R∞(τ_𝒮) by Theorem 5.1.1, so j_*j^*(I·M) = (j_*j^*I)·M (T61). j_*j^*I is the ideal H_U(I) of D24. The point stressed in §5.3: the image is an ideal times a free module, which is what makes Theorem 5.3.5 work. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).
items.proofOutline: The source module of the injected patching map is full-support MCM, so T58 extends it uniquely from U. T43 computes that restriction as the product ideal times the target. T40 makes the target free of rank one, and T61 converts extension of its product submodule to the embedded Hartogs ideal. The initial product ideal itself need not be MCM.

items.name: Extension across Z for maximal Cohen–Macaulay sheaves (step in Theorem 5.2.3)
items.statement: As printed: 'If ℳ is a Cohen–Macaulay sheaf on X∞(τ_𝒮), then j_*j^*ℳ = ℳ since the codimension of Z is two (cf. [HK04, Proposition 3.5]).' Form actually valid and used: if ℳ is a coherent sheaf on X∞(τ_𝒮) which is Cohen–Macaulay of full support (maximal Cohen–Macaulay over R∞(τ_𝒮)), then the natural map ℳ → j_*j^*ℳ is an isomorphism.
items.note: The printed statement is false for Cohen–Macaulay sheaves supported on a component of the special fibre (recorded as an issue); it is applied only to im M∞(ι) ≅ M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ), which is maximal CM by Definition 3.5.1(1). Proof of the valid form: for P ∈ Z, depth ℳ_P = dim 𝒪_P ≥ 2 (T57), so depth_I(ℳ) ≥ 2 for I with V(I) = Z (T65), hence H⁰_I(ℳ) = H¹_I(ℳ) = 0 (T56) and the exact sequence 0 → H⁰_I(ℳ) → ℳ → Γ(U, ℳ) → H¹_I(ℳ) → 0 gives the claim. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark 5.2.4 — the gauge ideal is defined over the local deformation rings
items.statement: As j comes from pulling back j₀ via X∞(τ_𝒮) → Spf(⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}) and the p(θ) are ideals of ⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}, the ideal j_*j^*(∏_{θ∈W?(ρ̄_𝒮)} p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮)) = j_{0*}j₀^*(∏_{θ∈W?(ρ̄_𝒮)} p(θ)^{m(θ)} ⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}) · R∞(τ_𝒮) comes from an ideal in ⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^□.
items.note: The displayed equality is flat base change of sections over the quasi-compact open (T54, T60) along ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ} → R∞(τ_𝒮) = (⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ})[[x₁,…,x_h]], with U the preimage of U₀ (T62). 'Comes from an ideal in ⊗̂R^□' = it is the extension of the preimage in ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^□ of an ideal of the quotient ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}. The ideal depends only on local data (ρ̄_𝒮, τ_𝒮, σ, κ, ι). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).
items.proofOutline: Set A=completed tensor_v R_v^tau, B=A[[x_1,…,x_h]], and use ordinary Spec A and Spec B. T62 identifies the crossing opens. The weight-prime product is extended from A. A is normal CM in the source setup, so A→sections(U_A,O) is an isomorphism by T58. T60 identifies the two embedded Hartogs ideals. Pull back this finite ideal through the surjection from the completed tensor of unrestricted framed rings.

items.name: Sections of a module over a quasi-compact open of an affine scheme
items.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I = (f₁,…,f_r) ⊂ A, U = Spec A \ V(I), and M an A-module. Define Sec_U(M) := Γ(U, M̃). By the sheaf axiom for the cover U = ∪_i D(f_i), Sec_U(M) is the kernel of ∏_i M_{f_i} → ∏_{i<j} M_{f_if_j}, (m_i)_i ↦ (m_i − m_j)_{i<j} (images in M_{f_if_j}). For r = 0 (U = ∅), Sec_U(M) = 0.
items.locator: general; used as the meaning of j_*j^* in Theorem 5.2.3 and Remark 5.2.4 (published p. 120)
items.note: Used: j_*j^*M̃ on the affine X∞(τ_𝒮) is the sheaf associated with Sec_U(M), U = X∞(τ_𝒮) \ Z. Standard. Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 (route 6).
items.proofOutline: All intersections of the chosen opens are affine. Restriction identifies the module on each principal open with localization; compatible tuples are precisely sections.

api.name: sections_restrict
api.statement: Construct the natural restriction M→Sec_U(M).

api.name: sections_change_generators
api.statement: Canonical identification for two finite lists defining the same open U.

api.name: sections_flat_base_change
api.statement: Use T54 for an A-flat algebra B.

unitTests: A one-element unit cover gives Sec_U(M)=M.
For A=k[x,y] and U=D(x) union D(y), a Laurent monomial lies in both localizations exactly when both exponents are nonnegative.
For I=0, U is empty and sections are zero.

items.name: Hartogs closure H_U(J) of an ideal
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring and U ⊂ Spec A a quasi-compact open such that the restriction A → Γ(U, 𝒪_U) is an isomorphism. For an ideal J ⊂ A, H_U(J) is the image of Γ(U, J̃|_U) ↪ Γ(U, 𝒪_U) ≅ A; it is an ideal of A containing J. The embedding into A (not only the isomorphism class of Γ(U, J̃|_U)) is part of the construction.
items.locator: general; this is the ideal j_*j^*(∏ p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮)) of Theorem 5.2.3 and Remark 5.2.4, published p. 120
items.note: Used with A = R∞(τ_𝒮) (normal CM, so A = Γ(U, 𝒪) because codim Z ≥ 2) and A = ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}. Replaces the HK04 citation by a self-contained module-theoretic definition. Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 (route 6).
items.proofOutline: The inclusion J-tilde→O induces an injection on sections. Its image is an A-submodule of A, hence an ideal; Noetherianness makes it finite.

api.name: ideal_le_hartogs
api.statement: J⊂H_U(J) via restriction.

api.name: hartogs_restrict
api.statement: The associated sheaf of H_U(J) restricts to J-tilde on U; use quasi-coherence of a quasi-compact open pushforward.

api.name: hartogs_flat
api.statement: For flat B, identify H_U(J)B with H_(U_B)(JB) under the induced structure-sheaf isomorphism.

unitTests: U=Spec A gives H_U(J)=J.
For A=k[x,y], U punctured at (x,y), H_U((x,y))=A.
For the same U, H_U((x))=(x); a codimension-one divisor is not erased.

items.name: Torsion-free specialization of a module at an 𝒪-point
items.statement: Let A → 𝒪 be a ring map to a discrete valuation ring and M a finitely generated A-module. Set M_𝒪^{tf} := (M ⊗_A 𝒪)/T, where T is the 𝒪-torsion submodule (elements killed by a nonzero element of 𝒪). In general M_𝒪^{tf} differs from M ⊗_A 𝒪.
items.locator: general; used in the proof of Theorem 5.3.5 ('(the p-torsion-free part of)' before (5.9)), published p. 126
items.note: In the paper A = R∞(τ_𝒮), A → 𝒪 = R∞/λ, M = M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ); the paper writes M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)/λ ≅ 𝒪 where only M_𝒪^{tf} ≅ 𝒪 holds (issue). Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).
items.proofOutline: Use the existing torsion-submodule and quotient constructions. The new interface records the specialization order and the particular image comparison T63.

api.name: specialize_tf_map
api.statement: An A-linear map induces a map on torsion-free specializations.

api.name: specialize_tf_generic
api.statement: Tensoring M_O^tf with Frac(O) agrees with tensoring M with Frac(O).

api.name: specialize_tf_rank_one
api.statement: Use T63 for a lattice image containing a nonzero power of the coefficient uniformizer.

unitTests: M=A gives O.
M=A⊕A/(pi), with pi mapping to a nonzero nonunit, gives O after removing torsion.
For A=O[[t]], I=(pi,t), t↦0, the raw specialization is O⊕O/(pi), while its torsion-free quotient maps isomorphically onto pi O.

items.name: Flat base change for sections over a quasi-compact open
items.statement: Let A → B be a flat ring map, U ⊂ Spec A a quasi-compact open, U_B its preimage in Spec B, and M an A-module. Then the natural map Sec_U(M) ⊗_A B → Sec_{U_B}(M ⊗_A B) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: general (degree-zero case of flat base change for quasi-coherent cohomology; Stacks Tag 02KH as given by the earlier checkpoint); used in Remark 5.2.4, published p. 120
items.note: Used for ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ} → R∞(τ_𝒮), which is flat (power series ring). Proof in degree 0: Sec_U(M) is the kernel in D23 and ⊗_A B is exact on it. Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 (route 7).
items.proofOutline: Use a finite principal-open cover. Tensoring with B preserves its equalizer because B is flat, and preserves the finite products. Localization commutes with tensor. These identifications also identify the restriction maps, so this is the canonical base-change map. No properness or formal-scheme theorem is needed.

items.name: Depth ≥ 2 kills H⁰_I and H¹_I
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring, M a finitely generated A-module and I ⊂ A an ideal. If depth_I(M) ≥ 2 then H⁰_I(M) = H¹_I(M) = 0. If IM = M (depth_I(M) = ∞) both groups vanish as well.
items.locator: general; input for [HK04, Prop. 3.5] in the proof of Theorem 5.2.3, published p. 120 (Stacks reference from the earlier checkpoint: Tag 0AVY, not re-verified)
items.note: Standard: H^i_I(M) = 0 for i < depth_I(M). Not stated in the paper; it is the content behind 'j_*j^*ℳ = ℳ'. Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).
items.proofOutline: A regular sequence in I of length two gives Ext_A^q(A/I^n,M)=0 for q<2 for every n, using equality of depth for I and I^n. Pass to the Ext colimit. Equivalently use the regular-element induction in 47.11.1. If IM=M, finite generation gives support disjoint from V(I), so these groups vanish.

items.name: Localizations of full-support Cohen–Macaulay modules have full depth
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian local ring and M a finitely generated Cohen–Macaulay A-module with Supp(M) = Spec A. Then for every P ∈ Spec A, M_P is Cohen–Macaulay with depth_{A_P}(M_P) = dim A_P. In particular depth M_P ≥ 2 for every prime P of height ≥ 2.
items.locator: general; used in Lemma 5.2.2 (local freeness on U) and Theorem 5.2.3 (depth along Z), published pp. 119–120 (Stacks Lemma 10.103.11 and Definition 10.103.8 as given by the earlier checkpoint)
items.note: Localization of a CM module is CM, and dim Supp(M_P) = dim A_P when Supp M = Spec A. Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).
items.proofOutline: CM localizes by 10.103.11. Support localizes to all of Spec A_P by the full-support assumption. Thus the CM depth equals dim A_P. This supplies the stalkwise condition and avoids the false inference from MCM to support on every component in general.

items.name: The Hartogs closure is a coherent ideal extending J
items.statement: In the situation of D24 (A Noetherian, U quasi-compact, A ≅ Γ(U, 𝒪_U)), H_U(J) is a finitely generated ideal of A whose associated sheaf is j_*(J̃|_U) and which restricts to J̃ on U. If depth_{A_P}(J_P) ≥ 2 for every P ∈ Spec A \ U, then H_U(J) = J.
items.locator: general; the ideal in Theorem 5.2.3 and Remark 5.2.4, published p. 120
items.note: J is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so j_*(J̃|_U) is quasi-coherent and is a subsheaf of j_*𝒪_U = 𝒪_X; the last claim is T56/T65 applied to J. In the paper H_U(∏p(θ)^{m(θ)}) is typically strictly larger than ∏p(θ)^{m(θ)}: this is why the gauge ideal is written with j_*j^*. Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 (route 6).
items.proofOutline: The finite principal-cover equalizer commutes with localization, so its sheaf is the open pushforward and restricts correctly. As a submodule of Noetherian A it is finite. For the final assertion apply absolute Hartogs to J-tilde. Do not claim an arbitrary initial product ideal is already MCM.

items.name: Hartogs closure commutes with flat base change
items.statement: Let A → B be a flat map of Noetherian rings, U ⊂ Spec A a quasi-compact open with A ≅ Γ(U, 𝒪_U), and U_B ⊂ Spec B its preimage. Then B ≅ Γ(U_B, 𝒪) canonically, and for every ideal J ⊂ A, H_U(J)·B = H_{U_B}(JB) as ideals of B.
items.note: From T54 applied to M = A and M = J (flatness gives J ⊗_A B = JB). This is the displayed equality of Remark 5.2.4, with A = ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ}, B = R∞(τ_𝒮), U = U₀ (and U_B = U by T62). Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 (route 7).
items.proofOutline: Apply T54 first to A and then to J. Flatness identifies J tensor_A B with JB and H_U(J) tensor_A B with its embedded extension ideal. The comparison is compatible with both inclusions into B. This proves equality of ideals, not merely an abstract module isomorphism.

items.name: Hartogs closure times a free module
items.statement: Let A, U be as in D24, J ⊂ A an ideal and L a finite free A-module. Then Γ(U, (JL)~) = H_U(J)·L inside Γ(U, L̃) = L. For L of rank one this is H_U(J)·L and does not depend on the choice of basis.
items.locator: general; last displayed equality in the proof of Theorem 5.2.3, published p. 120
items.note: Used with L = M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ), free of rank one over R∞(τ_𝒮) by Theorem 5.1.1: j_*j^*(∏p^m M∞(σ^σ)) = j_*j^*(∏p^m R∞(τ_𝒮))·M∞(σ^σ). Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 (route 6).
items.proofOutline: After a basis choice both sides are finite direct sums of the same ideal-section module; the equalizer commutes with finite sums. Naturality under GL(L) makes the isomorphism independent of basis. In rank one rescaling the generator by a unit preserves the embedded ideal.

items.name: Crossing loci pull back along adjunction of formal variables
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian complete local flat 𝒪-algebra with A/ϖ reduced, and let P₁,…,P_n ⊂ A be the preimages of the minimal primes of A/ϖ. Put B = A[[t₁,…,t_h]]. Then the minimal primes of B/ϖ = (A/ϖ)[[t]] are the P_iB/ϖB, and for Z_A := ∪_{i<j} V(P_i + P_j) ⊂ Spec A, its preimage in Spec B is Z_B := ∪_{i<j} V(P_iB + P_jB), the crossing locus of the special fibre of Spec B. Hence U_B := Spec B \ Z_B is the preimage of U_A := Spec A \ Z_A. (All spectra are ordinary spectra of the complete rings.)
items.locator: general; justifies 'j and U come from pulling back j₀' (§5.2, published p. 119) and Remark 5.2.4
items.note: Applied with A = ⊗̂_ṽ R_ṽ^{τ_ṽ} and B = R∞(τ_𝒮). Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).
items.proofOutline: A→B is flat and finite intersections extend under a flat map. Each quotient B/P_iB=(A/P_i)[[t]] is a domain. Since the intersection of the P_i modulo varpi is zero, these extended primes are exactly the minimal primes. The ideals of pairwise intersections extend to their sums. The paper has precisely B=A[[x_1,…,x_h]] for the type quotient; no general equivalence of open subsets of Spec and Spf is claimed.

items.name: Specializing an ideal-shaped lattice map at an 𝒪-point
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring, π ∈ A, u : M → A an injective A-linear map from a finitely generated module, I = u(M), and suppose π^nA ⊂ I for some n. Let a : A → 𝒪 be a ring map to a discrete valuation ring with a(π) ≠ 0. Then the induced map M ⊗_A 𝒪 → 𝒪 has image I𝒪 ≠ 0 and 𝒪-torsion kernel; hence it identifies M_𝒪^{tf} (D25) with the nonzero ideal I𝒪, which is free of rank one, even when M ⊗_A 𝒪 has torsion.
items.locator: general; clarifies (5.9) in the proof of Theorem 5.3.5, published p. 126
items.note: Applied with A = R∞(τ_𝒮) ≅ M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ), M = M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ), π = p (coker M∞(ι) = M∞(coker ι) is killed by a power of p), a = the point λ. The torsion of M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)/λ maps to zero, so the image of (5.9) is the image of j_*j^*(∏p^m R∞(τ_𝒮)) in 𝒪. Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).
items.proofOutline: After inverting pi, u becomes an isomorphism because its cokernel is killed by pi^n. After tensoring with Frac(O) it remains an isomorphism. Consequently the specialized kernel is O-torsion, and every torsion element maps to zero in O, so the kernel is exactly the torsion submodule. Right exactness gives image IO, containing a(pi)^n. A nonzero ideal of a DVR is free of rank one. This does not supply the separately required Schikhof-duality identification of the automorphic lattice.

items.name: Stalkwise depth ≥ 2 gives a regular sequence of length two in the support ideal
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring, M a finitely generated A-module and I ⊂ A an ideal with depth_{A_P}(M_P) ≥ 2 for every P ∈ V(I) ∩ Supp(M). If IM ≠ M then I contains an M-regular sequence of length two (depth_I(M) ≥ 2); if IM = M, depth_I(M) = ∞ by convention.
items.locator: general; input for [HK04, Prop. 3.5] in Theorem 5.2.3, published p. 120
items.note: Standard: depth_I(M) = min_{P∈V(I)} depth M_P (prime avoidance). Not stated in the paper. Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).
items.proofOutline: No associated prime of M contains I, since at an associated prime the nonzero localized module has depth zero. Finiteness of Ass(M) and prime avoidance choose x∈I outside all associated primes, so x is M-regular. At P∈V(I) in the support of M/xM, the regular-element depth formula gives depth((M/xM)_P)≥1. Thus no associated prime of M/xM contains I; prime avoidance chooses y∈I regular on M/xM. Since IM≠M, the final quotient is nonzero. The finite-associated-prime/zero-divisor criterion and the regular-element depth formula are shared R03.3 prerequisites, not supplied by the existing localCohomology carrier.

items.name: Local cohomology as a colimit of Ext
items.statement: For a commutative ring A, an ideal I ⊂ A and q ∈ ℕ, the local cohomology functor H^q_I on A-modules is M ↦ colim_n Ext^q_A(A/I^n, M).
items.locator: general (mathlib: Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/LocalCohomology.lean, definition localCohomology, commit 082e2d37); background for [HK04, Prop. 3.5] in Theorem 5.2.3
items.note: Not used explicitly by the paper; it enters only through the standard proof of the cited extension statement (T56). Library: localCohomology at the pinned commits.
items.proofOutline: Read the entire pinned file. Its comparison to derived torsion/Čech cohomology and long exact sequences are explicitly future work; those statements are not supplied by this carrier.

api.statement: Use its functor map for A-linear module maps.

api.name: change_support_radical
api.statement: Use L07 when the defining ideal changes without changing its radical.

For I=0 the cofinal positive powers give H^0=M and H^q=0 for q>0.
An A-linear identity induces the identity map by the functor laws.

items.name: Local cohomology depends only on the radical of the ideal
items.statement: For a Noetherian commutative ring A and ideals I, J ⊂ A with √I = √J, the functors H^q_I and H^q_J are naturally isomorphic for every q.
items.locator: general (mathlib: localCohomology.isoOfSameRadical, commit 082e2d37); background for Theorem 5.2.3
items.note: Needed because Z is given only as a closed subset (V(I) for any I with the right radical). Not used explicitly by the paper. Library: localCohomology.isoOfSameRadical at the pinned commits.
items.proofOutline: The pinned statement constructs the natural isomorphism via the cofinal diagram of ideals whose radical contains I.

items.name: Modules versus quasi-coherent sheaves on an affine scheme
items.statement: For a commutative ring A, M ↦ M̃ is an equivalence from A-modules to quasi-coherent 𝒪_{Spec A}-modules.
items.locator: general (mathlib: AlgebraicGeometry.tildeEquiv, Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Tilde.lean, commit 082e2d37); used implicitly in §5.2
items.note: The paper passes freely between R∞(τ_𝒮)-modules and quasi-coherent sheaves on X∞(τ_𝒮) (Lemma 5.2.2, Theorem 5.2.3). Library: AlgebraicGeometry.tildeEquiv at the pinned commits.
items.proofOutline: Read the declaration and isQuasicoherent_iff_isIso_fromTildeΓ immediately above it. Coherence and Hartogs extension require additional results.

api.statement: Use the functor of tildeEquiv for finite modules.

api.statement: Use the inverse/global-sections functor and unit.

api.statement: Transport A-linear maps to sheaf maps using the equivalence.

Zero corresponds to zero.
An isomorphism of modules induces an isomorphism of associated sheaves.

items.name: Depth, Cohen–Macaulay, maximal Cohen–Macaulay, full support
items.statement: For a Noetherian ring A, an ideal I and a finitely generated A-module M, depth_I(M) is the supremum of the lengths of M-regular sequences in I (= ∞ if IM = M). For A local, depth(M) := depth_𝔪(M). A nonzero finitely generated M over a Noetherian local ring is Cohen–Macaulay if depth(M) = dim Supp(M), and maximal Cohen–Macaulay if depth(M) = dim A. M has full support if Supp(M) = Spec A (for A a domain, maximal Cohen–Macaulay implies full support).
items.locator: general; used in Definition 3.5.1(1),(3), Lemma 5.2.2 ('Cohen–Macaulay of full support') and Theorem 5.2.3 (published pp. 119–120); Stacks 10.103 and 47.11 as given by the earlier checkpoint
items.note: The paper's 'maximally Cohen–Macaulay over R∞(τ_𝒮)' (Def. 3.5.1(1)) and 'Cohen–Macaulay of full support' (Lemma 5.2.2) agree because R∞(τ_𝒮) is a domain. Planned: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3 plans depth, Cohen–Macaulay modules and Auslander–Buchsbaum.
items.proofOutline: The reviewed R03.3 audit finds regular sequences and Rees Ext-vanishing infrastructure, but no depth or CM predicate. Import that owner; do not create a GL3-specific depth theory.

api.name: depth_regular_sequence
api.statement: A regular sequence in I of length n gives depth_I(M)≥n.

api.name: cm_localize
api.statement: Apply T57 to localizations.

api.name: full_support_not_automatic
api.statement: Require full support when replacing dim Supp(M_P) by dim A_P.

unitTests: A nonzero finite free module over a regular local ring of dimension d has depth d.
For A=k[[x,y]], A/(x) is CM of dimension one but not MCM over A.
For M=0 or IM=M use infinity and do not invoke a nonexistent first nonzero local-cohomology degree.

items.name: Image of an injective map of line bundles on a regular scheme
items.statement: Let U be a regular Noetherian scheme and f : ℒ₁ → ℒ₂ an injective map of invertible sheaves. Then im f = 𝒪_U(−D)·ℒ₂, where D = Σ_x length_{𝒪_{U,x}}((coker f)_x) · [\overline{{x}}] over the points x of codimension one, and 𝒪_U(−D) = ∏_x 𝓘_x^{n_x} with 𝓘_x the (invertible) ideal sheaf of the prime divisor \overline{{x}}.
items.locator: general; implicit in the proof of Lemma 5.2.2 ('the ideal sheaf of the Cartier divisor corresponding to the cokernel'), published p. 119
items.note: Regular local rings are UFDs (Auslander–Buchsbaum), so height-one primes are locally principal. Standard. Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 (route 6).

items.name: [Bre14, Conjectures B.1 and 1.2] — Dembélé's mod p multiplicity one and Breuil's lattice conjecture (context)
items.statement: §5.3 deduces generalizations of the conjectures of Dembélé (mod p multiplicity one) and Breuil (lattices in completed cohomology depend only on the local Galois representations), [Bre14, Conjectures B.1 and 1.2], stated there for GL₂: Theorem 5.3.4 is the GL₃ mod p multiplicity one statement and Theorem 5.3.5 the GL₃ lattice statement.
items.note: Cited for context only; nothing from [Bre14] is used in the proofs. The paragraph also records that Theorem 5.3.4 follows immediately from Theorem 5.1.1 and that Theorem 5.3.5 needs the image in Theorem 5.2.3 to be an ideal times a free module (which relies on Theorem 5.1.1). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Global setup — CM field and definite unitary group
items.statement: (Setup of [LLHLM18, §7.1].) F/ℚ is a CM field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺ ≠ ℚ; Σ_p⁺ (resp. Σ_p) is the set of places of F⁺ (resp. of F) above p. G/F⁺ is a reductive group which is an outer form of GL₃, quasi-split at all finite places of F⁺, split over F, and definite: G(F⁺_v) ≅ U₃(ℝ) for all v | ∞.
items.note: Definiteness makes G(F⁺)\G(𝔸^∞_{F⁺})/U finite, so the spaces S(U,W) below are finite 𝒪-modules ('algebraic automorphic forms'). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [EGH13, §7.1] — integral model 𝒢 and the isomorphisms ι, ι_w (5.7)
items.statement: G admits a reductive model 𝒢 defined over 𝒪_{F⁺}[1/N], for some N ∈ ℕ prime to p, together with an isomorphism ι : 𝒢_{/𝒪_F[1/N]} ⥲ GL_{3/𝒪_F[1/N]} (5.7), which specializes to ι_w : 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺_v}) ⥲ 𝒢(𝒪_{F_w}) ⥲ GL₃(𝒪_{F_w}) for all places w ∈ Σ_p with w|_{F⁺} = v.
items.note: Cited ('Recall from [EGH13, Section 7.1]'). The ι_ṽ are used to transport K = ∏_{ṽ∈𝒮} GL₃(𝒪_{F_ṽ})-representations to 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})-representations (σ ↦ σ ∘ ∏ι_ṽ), and also at ṽ₁ and at the places of Σ₀⁺. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: S(U, W) — algebraic automorphic forms on the definite unitary group
items.statement: Let U = U^pU_p ≤ G(𝔸^{(∞,p)}_{F⁺}) × 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) be a compact open subgroup and W a finite 𝒪-module endowed with a continuous action of U. Then S(U, W) := {f : G(F⁺)\G(𝔸^∞_{F⁺}) → W | f(gu) = u^{-1}f(g) for all g ∈ G(𝔸^∞_{F⁺}), u ∈ U}.
items.note: 'Finite 𝒪-module' is used in the sense of finitely generated (W is often an 𝒪-lattice such as W_{Σ₀⁺} ⊗ σ°). U acts on W through its components at Σ₀⁺ (via ι_ṽ on σ(τ_v)°) and at p. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: S(U^p, W) — forms of tame level U^p and infinite level at p
items.statement: S(U^p, W) := lim→_{U_p} S(U^pU_p, W), where U_p ≤ 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) runs over the compact open neighbourhoods of 1 ∈ 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}).
items.note: For the colimit to make sense W must carry a U^pU_p-action for all U_p (e.g. the p-part acts trivially, W = W_{Σ₀⁺}, as in §5.3.4). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: S̃(U^p, W) — ϖ-adically completed cohomology
items.statement: S̃(U^p, W) := lim←_s S(U^p, W/ϖ^s), with S(U^p, W/ϖ^s) = lim→_{U_p} S(U^pU_p, W/ϖ^s) as in def-S-Up-W.
items.note: Carries commuting actions of 𝕋^univ and of G(F⁺_p) ⊃ 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) ≅ K (via ∏ι_ṽ). Used with W = W_{Σ₀⁺} in §5.3.4 (S̃(U^p,W)[λ], Schikhof dual S̃(U^p,W)^d). Planned: CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.1–CC.2 and CC.8 plan the completed towers and their unitary adapters.
items.proofOutline: Specialisation of CC.1, CC.2 and CC.8; finite-level arithmetic identification remains a consumer proof.

api.name: tower_actions
api.statement: Hecke and local-group actions commute.

api.name: tower_residue
api.statement: Relate finite-level coefficients to the completed tower.

unitTests: The p-level runs toward the identity.
Coefficient reduction uses varpi^s.
Fixing the away-p coefficient lattice is part of the input.

items.name: 𝒫_U and the universal Hecke algebra 𝕋_𝒫
items.statement: For U as above, 𝒫_U is the set of finite places w of F whose restriction v := w|_{F⁺} splits in F and at which U is unramified. For 𝒫 ⊂ 𝒫_U of finite complement, the universal Hecke algebra 𝕋_𝒫 = 𝒪[T_w^{(i)} : w ∈ 𝒫, 0 ≤ i ≤ n] on 𝒫 acts naturally on S(U, W).
items.note: N is not defined in the paper; n = 3 (GL₃) is meant (issue). The T_w^{(i)} are the usual unramified Hecke operators at w (transported via ι_w); their definition is not restated. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The maximal ideal 𝔪 of 𝕋_𝒫 attached to r̄ (Hecke normalisation)
items.statement: Let r̄ : G_F → GL₃(𝔽) be a continuous Galois representation. 𝔪 ⊆ 𝕋_𝒫 is the maximal ideal which is the kernel of the system of Hecke eigenvalues ᾱ : 𝕋_𝒫 → 𝔽 associated with r̄, i.e. ᾱ satisfies det(1 − r̄^∨(Frob_w)X) = Σ_{j=0}^{3} (−1)^j (𝐍_{F/ℚ}(w))^{\binom{j}{2}} ᾱ(T_w^{(j)}) X^j for all w ∈ 𝒫.
items.note: Normalisation: the dual r̄^∨ and the factor 𝐍(w)^{j(j−1)/2}. The same formula (with α, r, λ) defines λ in §5.3.4 and 𝔪̄ in Definition 6.0.1. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: r̄ automorphic (§5.3)
items.statement: r̄ is automorphic if S(U, W)_𝔪 is nonzero for some U and W (as in def-algebraic-automorphic-forms, with 𝒫 ⊂ 𝒫_U).
items.note: Refined in Definition 6.0.1 (automorphic of weight V, level U and coefficients W; W(r̄) ≠ ∅). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [CEG+16, §2.3] — the auxiliary place v₁
items.statement: A place v₁ of F⁺ is chosen 'for technical reasons' as in [CEG+16, Section 2.3].
items.note: Cited; the required properties of v₁ are not restated in this paper. v₁ enters the level (Iwahori-type level at v₁) and 𝕋^univ (operators T_{v₁}^{(j)}). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The fixed tame level U^p
items.statement: U^p ≤ G(𝔸^{(∞,p)}_{F⁺}) is the subgroup with: (1) (U^p)_v = 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺_v}) for all finite places v of F⁺ which split in F and do not belong to Σ_p⁺ ∪ {v₁}; (2) (U^p)_{v₁} is the preimage of the upper triangular matrices under 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺_{v₁}}) → 𝒢(k_{v₁}) →^{ι_{ṽ₁}} GL₃(k_{ṽ₁}); (3) (U^p)_v is hyperspecial maximal compact in G(F⁺_v) if v is inert in F.
items.note: Places of Σ₀⁺ (split, by split ramification) get maximal level 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺_v}); ramification at Σ₀⁺ is carried by the coefficient module W_{Σ₀⁺}. No finite place ramifies in F/F⁺ by hypothesis (i). In arXiv v3 the places of Σ₀⁺ were excluded from (1). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Σ₀⁺ — ramified places away from p
items.statement: For an automorphic r̄, Σ₀⁺ is the set of finite places of F⁺ which are restrictions of the finite places of F away from p where r̄ ramifies.
items.note: By split ramification (ii) every v ∈ Σ₀⁺ splits in F. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [CHT08, Definition 2.4.14] — minimally ramified lifts and types (as used)
items.statement: For a place ṽ ∤ p of F, the notion of a minimally ramified lift of r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}} ([CHT08, Definition 2.4.14]). As used: for v ∈ Σ₀⁺, τ_ṽ is 'the minimally ramified type in the sense of [CHT08, Definition 2.4.14] corresponding to r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}}' (the inertial type of its minimally ramified lifts), and a characteristic-0 r is minimally ramified at ṽ if r|_{G_{F_ṽ}} is a minimally ramified lift.
items.note: Cited, not restated. That all minimally ramified lifts have one and the same inertial type is implicit in 'the minimally ramified type'. Planned: LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2 plans minimally ramified deformation conditions away from p; LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 plans fixed labeled Hodge-type and inertial-type potentially semistable deformation rings in every rank, with bounded-height lattice moduli and minimally ramified conditions.

items.name: Minimal types σ(τ_v) at Σ₀⁺ and the coefficient lattice W_{Σ₀⁺}
items.statement: For each v ∈ Σ₀⁺ (with a chosen ṽ | v), τ_ṽ is the minimally ramified type corresponding to r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}} and σ(τ_ṽ) is the GL₃(𝒪_{F_ṽ})-representation over E associated with it (cf. the beginning of §5.3.1); σ(τ_v) := σ(τ_ṽ) ∘ ι_ṽ, a 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺_v})-representation independent of the choice of ṽ | v. For each v ∈ Σ₀⁺ fix an 𝒪-lattice σ(τ_v)° ⊂ σ(τ_v), and put W_{Σ₀⁺} := ⊗_{v∈Σ₀⁺} σ(τ_v)°.
items.note: The independence of ṽ is asserted without proof. 'cf. the beginning of §5.3.1' points to Proposition 2.2.6/[CEG+16, Thm 3.7], stated there for tame types at places above p; for ṽ ∤ p the analogous inertial local Langlands types are meant. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: 𝕋^univ, its action on S(U^pU_p, W_{Σ₀⁺} ⊗ V), and 𝔪 ⊆ 𝕋^univ
items.statement: 𝕋^univ is the abstract Hecke algebra over 𝒪 generated by formal variables T_w^{(j)}, where w runs over the finite places of F such that w|_{F⁺} is split in F and w|_{F⁺} ∉ Σ₀⁺ ∪ Σ_p⁺ ∪ {v₁}, and by T_{v₁}^{(j)} for j = 1, 2, 3. For a module V over 𝒪 with an action of the p-adic group (printed: 'a G(𝔸^{(∞,p)}_{F⁺})-module V'), 𝕋^univ acts naturally on S(U^pU_p, W), S(U^p, W) and S̃(U^p, W), where W = W_{Σ₀⁺} ⊗ V (cf. [CEG+16, §2.3]); 𝔪 ⊆ 𝕋^univ is 'the maximal ideal as before' (kernel of the eigensystem ᾱ of r̄ given by the characteristic-polynomial formula of def-m-rbar).
items.note: Two issues recorded: V must be a 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})- (or U_p-) module, not a G(𝔸^{(∞,p)}_{F⁺})-module; and the formula determines ᾱ only on the T_w^{(j)}, not on T_{v₁}^{(j)}. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Standing assumption: S(U, W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 for some V
items.statement: From this point on it is assumed that S(U, W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 (U = U^pU_p, W = W_{Σ₀⁺} ⊗ V) for some choice of V. The paper remarks: 'In fact, one can show, by the proof of Proposition 6.0.2, that this is a consequence of the hypothesis that r̄ is automorphic.'
items.note: This assumption (nonvanishing at the fixed minimal tame level and coefficients) is what makes the patching functor M̃∞ nonzero (cf. §6(11), (16)). The remark's justification needs the hypotheses of Proposition 6.0.2 (split ramification, Taylor–Wiles, automorphy of a reachable weight); recorded as a minor gap. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Global hypotheses (i)–(iv) of §5.3
items.statement: In the remainder of §5.3, r̄ : G_F → GL₃(𝔽) is an automorphic Galois representation that satisfies the Taylor–Wiles conditions of [LLHLM18, Definition 7.3], and furthermore: (i) the extension F/F⁺ is unramified at all finite places; (ii) (split ramification) if r̄ is ramified at a place w of F, then v = w|_{F⁺} splits as ww^c; (iii) p is unramified in F⁺ and all places of F⁺ above p split in F; (iv) r̄|_{G_{F_w}} is semisimple for all w ∈ Σ_p.
items.note: Compared with [LLHLM18], 'p splits completely in F⁺' is relaxed to (iii) (Remark 5.3.2) at the cost of (iv). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: 𝒮, ρ̄_𝒮 and K in the global setting
items.statement: For each v ∈ Σ_p⁺ choose a place ṽ | v of F and let 𝒮 := {ṽ | v ∈ Σ_p⁺}. ρ̄_ṽ := r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}}, ρ̄_𝒮 := (ρ̄_ṽ)_{ṽ∈𝒮}, and K := ∏_{ṽ∈𝒮} GL₃(𝒪_{F_ṽ}).
items.note: By (iii) each F_ṽ/ℚ_p is unramified, so the local results of §§3–5.2 apply to ρ̄_𝒮. ∏ι_ṽ identifies 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) with K. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [LLHLM18, Definition 7.11, Proposition 7.15] — the weak minimal patching functor M̃∞ for r̄
items.statement: M̃∞ is the weak minimal patching functor for r̄ in the sense of [LLHLM18, Definition 7.11], constructed in [LLHLM18, Proposition 7.15]: an exact covariant functor from continuous 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})-representations on finitely generated 𝒪-modules to coherent sheaves on X∞ = Spf R∞, R∞ = ⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^□[[x₁,…,x_h]], built by patching the spaces S(U^pU_p, W_{Σ₀⁺} ⊗ −).
items.note: Cited. As corrected in §6: the definition depends on the fixed level U and coefficients W (§6(11)); here U = U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) and W = W_{Σ₀⁺} (§6(14)); its nonvanishing needs Proposition 6.0.2 or the standing assumption (§6(16)); e(M) as in §6(12). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: M∞ := M̃∞ ∘ ∏ι_ṽ — the patching functor for ρ̄_𝒮
items.statement: M∞ := M̃∞ ∘ ∏_{ṽ∈𝒮} ι_ṽ (a K-representation V is sent to M̃∞(V ∘ ∏_ṽ ι_ṽ)), which is a weak minimal patching functor for ρ̄_𝒮 in the sense of Definition 3.5.1 by Proposition 3.5.14.
items.note: With this M∞ all of §§5.1–5.2 (Theorems 5.1.1, 5.2.3) apply. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Ring homomorphism R∞ → 𝕋^univ(W_{Σ₀⁺})_𝔪 and the ideal 𝔪 ⊂ R∞ ([CEG+16, §2.8], [Le18, §4.2], [LLHLM18, §7.3])
items.statement: Along with the construction of M̃∞ (cf. [CEG+16, Section 2.8], [Le18, Section 4.2], [LLHLM18, Section 7.3]) one has a ring homomorphism R∞ = ⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^□[[x₁,…,x_h]] → 𝕋^univ_{U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})}(W_{Σ₀⁺})_𝔪, where 𝕋^univ_{U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})}(W_{Σ₀⁺}) is the image of 𝕋^univ in End_𝒪(S(U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}), W_{Σ₀⁺})). 𝔪 also denotes the pullback to R∞ of the maximal ideal of 𝕋^univ_{U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})}(W_{Σ₀⁺})_𝔪.
items.note: Cited. As printed the target is the Hecke algebra of forms of trivial weight at p, which is 0 for 10-generic ρ̄_𝒮 (issue); in effect 𝔪 ⊂ R∞ is the maximal ideal of the local ring R∞, which is all that (5.8) and Theorem 5.3.4 use. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: (5.8) — patched modules mod 𝔪 compute 𝔪-torsion in mod p automorphic forms ([Le18, Theorem 4.1.5])
items.statement: If W̄_{Σ_p⁺} is a smooth finite-dimensional 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p})-representation over 𝔽, then (M̃∞(W̄_{Σ_p⁺})/𝔪)^∨ = S(U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}), W̄_{Σ₀⁺} ⊗ W̄_{Σ_p⁺}^∨)[𝔪], where ·^∨ denotes Pontryagin dual (on the left) and W̄_{Σ₀⁺} = W_{Σ₀⁺}/ϖ.
items.note: Cited 'cf. [Le18, Theorem 4.1.5]'. On the right, W̄_{Σ_p⁺}^∨ is the contragredient and [𝔪] the 𝔪-torsion for 𝕋^univ. Used in Theorems 5.3.3 (W^BM(ρ̄_𝒮) vs W(r̄)) and 5.3.4. In arXiv v3 the '[𝔪]' was missing. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Pontryagin dual
items.statement: For a discrete ϖ-power-torsion 𝒪-module M, M^∨ := Hom_𝒪(M, E/𝒪) (= Hom_𝔽(M, 𝔽) if ϖM = 0, e.g. M finite-dimensional over 𝔽); M^∨∨ ≅ M for M of finite length.
items.note: The symbol ^∨ is also used for contragredients of representations (σ^∨, W̄^∨) and for the dual Galois representation r̄^∨. Planned: CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.3 plans continuous and Pontryagin duals and completed homology.

items.name: σ(τ_ṽ) — the K-type of a tame inertial type (Proposition 2.2.6 as used)
items.statement: For ṽ ∈ 𝒮 and a 1-generic tame inertial type τ_ṽ for I_{F_ṽ}, σ(τ_ṽ) is a smooth GL₃(𝒪_{F_ṽ})-representation over E associated with τ_ṽ as in [CEG+16, Theorem 3.7] ('results towards inertial local Langlands'); σ(τ_𝒮) := ⊗_{ṽ∈𝒮} σ(τ_ṽ). By Proposition 2.2.6, if τ_𝒮 = τ_𝒮(s, μ) with μ − η 1-deep in C₀, the Deligne–Lusztig representation R_s(μ) (inflated to K) is irreducible ([DL76, Thm 6.8]) and σ(τ_𝒮) can be taken to be R_s(μ) ([LLHL19, Cor. 2.3.5]).
items.locator: §5.3.1, first paragraph, published p. 123 (recalling Proposition 2.2.6 and the paragraph before it, published p. 17)
items.note: The text says 'Recall from Proposition 2.2.6 … we defined σ(τ_ṽ)'; the definition is in the paragraph preceding Proposition 2.2.6. σ(τ_ṽ) can be realized over 𝒪 (§3.5); lattices σ(τ_𝒮)^σ with irreducible cosocle σ are unique up to homothety (§4.1.2). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Global/local Langlands normalisation used in Theorem 5.3.1
items.statement: For a regular algebraic conjugate self-dual cuspidal (RACSDC) automorphic representation π of GL₃(𝔸_F) and a fixed isomorphism ι : \overline{ℚ}_p ≅ ℂ, r_ι(π) : G_F → GL₃(\overline{ℚ}_p) denotes the associated Galois representation and r̄_ι(π) its (semisimplified) reduction; 'trivial infinitesimal character' is the weight corresponding to Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0); ⊗_{ṽ∈𝒮} σ(τ_ṽ) is a K-type for ⊗_{ṽ∈𝒮} π_ṽ if Hom_K(⊗_ṽ σ(τ_ṽ), ⊗_ṽ π_ṽ) ≠ 0. Hecke eigenvalues of a characteristic-0 r are normalised by det(1 − r^∨(Frob_w)X) = Σ_{j=0}^3 (−1)^j 𝐍_{F/ℚ}(w)^{\binom{j}{2}} α(T_w^{(j)}) X^j.
items.note: Not defined in this paper; conventions are those of [LLHLM18, §7] (and [CHT08], [EGH13]). The polarization r^c ≅ r^∨ε^{−2} and the Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0) fix the twist. The inertial type of a p-adic Galois representation is read off from its Weil–Deligne representation as in §2 (covariant convention of [CDT99, App. B.1]). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Theorem 5.3.1 — automorphy lifting
items.statement: (Global setup of §5.3: F/F⁺, G, 𝒮, K; F/F⁺ unramified at all finite places, p unramified in F⁺, all places above p split in F.) Let r : G_F → GL₃(E) be an absolutely irreducible Galois representation such that (1) for all places w ∈ Σ_p, r̄|_{I_{F_w}} is semisimple and 10-generic; (2) r is unramified almost everywhere and satisfies r^c ≅ r^∨ε^{−2}; (3) for all ṽ ∈ 𝒮, r|_{G_{F_ṽ}} is potentially crystalline, with parallel Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0) and with tame inertial type τ_ṽ ([LLHLM18, Definition 2.1]); (4) r̄ satisfies the Taylor–Wiles conditions as above and r̄ has split ramification; and (5) r̄ ≅ r̄_ι(π) for a RACSDC representation π of GL₃(𝔸_F) with trivial infinitesimal character such that ⊗_{ṽ∈𝒮} σ(τ_ṽ) is a K-type for ⊗_{ṽ∈𝒮} π_ṽ. Then r is automorphic in the sense of [LLHLM18, Section 7.2].
items.note: Proof as printed: 'Given Theorems 5.3.3 and 3.5.3, the proof of [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.4] goes through unchanged' — but by §6(16) that proof was omitted in [LLHLM18] (issue). Theorem 3.5.3 supplies connectedness (irreducibility) of the generic fibre of R^{τ}_{ρ̄} for semisimple 10-generic ρ̄; Theorem 5.3.3 supplies nonvanishing of M∞ on the relevant component. On (1): with 10-genericity, r̄|_{I_{F_w}} semisimple is equivalent to r̄|_{G_{F_w}} semisimple (inflation–restriction, no common inertial constituents), consistent with Remark 5.3.2 and hypothesis (iv). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).
items.proofOutline: Uses T37 connected generic fibres and T46 in the proof of LLHLM18 Theorem 7.4. The source cross-reference must still be expanded with its corrected level-lowering argument; G07.

items.name: [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.4] — automorphy lifting when p splits completely (cited; proof omitted there)
items.statement: [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.4] is the automorphy lifting theorem for potentially crystalline lifts of Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0) and generic tame type under the hypothesis that p splits completely in F⁺ (without semisimplicity at p). Its proof 'was omitted' in [LLHLM18] and uses the same level-lowering techniques ([Tay08]) as Proposition 6.0.2 (§6(16)).
items.note: Cited; Theorem 5.3.1 rests on it. The precise statement of [LLHLM18, Thm 7.4] is not reproduced in this paper; the description above is what Remark 5.3.2 and §6(16) say about it. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark 5.3.2 — why semisimplicity at p is assumed
items.statement: Compared to [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.4], Theorem 5.3.1 relaxes the hypothesis that p splits completely to p being unramified, but also assumes that r̄ is semisimple at all places above p, because the connectedness of the generic fibre of R_ρ̄^τ is established here only when ρ̄ is semisimple (it is known for non-semisimple ρ̄ when all shapes have length ≥ 2). A counterpart of [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.4] for non-semisimple representations is announced as work in progress.
items.note: States (without proof here) that the generic fibre of R_ρ̄^τ is connected for non-semisimple ρ̄ when all shapes have length ≥ 2. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: W(r̄) — Serre weights of r̄ at the fixed level (§5.3.2)
items.statement: W(r̄) is the set of irreducible K-representations σ over 𝔽 such that S(U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}), W̄_{Σ₀⁺} ⊗ (σ^∨ ∘ ∏_{ṽ∈𝒮} ι_ṽ))_𝔪 ≠ 0.
items.note: Depends on the fixed U^p and W_{Σ₀⁺}. Same symbol as, but different from, W(r̄) of Definition 6.0.1 (Serre weights of 𝒢 at arbitrary level and coefficients, no contragredient). By (5.8), W(r̄) = W^BM(ρ̄_𝒮) for M∞ = M̃∞ ∘ ∏ι_ṽ. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Theorem 5.3.3 — the weight part of Serre's conjecture
items.statement: (Global setup of §5.3, including the standing nonvanishing assumption.) Let r̄ : G_F → GL₃(𝔽) be a continuous Galois representation satisfying the Taylor–Wiles conditions. Assume that ρ̄_ṽ := r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}} is semisimple and 10-generic for all ṽ ∈ 𝒮, that r̄ is automorphic, and that r̄ has split ramification. Then W(r̄) ∘ ∏_{ṽ∈𝒮} ι_ṽ = W?(ρ̄_𝒮) [as printed; since W(r̄) and W?(ρ̄_𝒮) are both sets of K-representations, the type-correct statement is W(r̄) = W?(ρ̄_𝒮)].
items.note: Proof: W^BM(ρ̄_𝒮) = W(r̄) (printed '= W(r̄) ∘ ∏ι_ṽ') by (5.8), and W^BM(ρ̄_𝒮) = W?(ρ̄_𝒮) by Theorem 3.5.2 (e(M∞(σ)) = 1 iff σ ∈ W?). Correct modulo the notational slip (issue). Previous-pass statement listed the global conventions; replaced by the printed statement. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).
items.proofOutline: Equation (5.8) identifies dual weight eigenspaces with M_infty(sigma)/m; T35 gives exactly the nonzero ones. Level lowering §6.0.2 and original automorphic patching are G05/G07.

items.name: Theorem 5.3.4 — mod p multiplicity one
items.statement: (Global setup of §5.3.) Let τ_𝒮 and σ ∈ W?(ρ̄_𝒮, τ_𝒮) be as in the statement of Theorem 5.1.1 (τ_𝒮 13-generic; σ = F(λ) with λ_{π^{-1}(i)} in alcove C₁ whenever ℓ(w̃*_i) ≤ 1). Then S(U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}), (σ̄(τ_𝒮)^σ ∘ ∏_{v∈Σ_p⁺} ι_ṽ)^∨ ⊗_{𝒪_E} W_{Σ₀⁺})[𝔪] is one-dimensional over 𝔽.
items.note: Proof: by (5.8), M∞(σ̄(τ_𝒮)^σ)/𝔪 ≅ M̃∞(σ̄(τ_𝒮)^σ ∘ ∏ι_ṽ)/𝔪 ≅ (S(U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}), (σ̄(τ_𝒮)^σ ∘ ∏ι_ṽ)^∨ ⊗_𝒪 W_{Σ₀⁺})[𝔪])^∨, and by Theorem 5.1.1 (M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ) ≅ R∞(τ_𝒮)) its dimension is one. Checked. ⊗_{𝒪_E} W_{Σ₀⁺} of an 𝔽-module is ⊗ W̄_{Σ₀⁺}. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).
items.proofOutline: Equation (5.8) is dual to the residue of a free rank-one patched module. The condition is not restricted to all-upper weights, nor true for arbitrary weights; use T40’s exact conditional bound.

items.name: Minimally ramified r (§5.3.4)
items.statement: Let r : G_F → GL₃(E) be an automorphic Galois representation as in Theorem 5.3.1. r is minimally ramified if r|_{G_{F_ṽ}} is minimally ramified in the sense of [CHT08, Definition 2.4.14] for all v ∈ Σ₀⁺.
items.note: Then the inertial type of r at ṽ ∈ Σ₀⁺ is the minimal type τ_ṽ, so the coefficient module W_{Σ₀⁺} matches r. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The Hecke ideal λ of r (and λ ⊂ R∞)
items.statement: Following [LLHLM18, §7.1], λ ⊂ 𝕋^univ is the kernel of the system of Hecke eigenvalues α : 𝕋^univ → 𝒪 associated with r, i.e. α satisfies det(1 − r^∨(Frob_w)X) = Σ_{j=0}^{3} (−1)^j (𝐍_{F/ℚ}(w))^{\binom{j}{2}} α(T_w^{(j)}) X^j for all w as above. By abuse of notation λ also denotes the prime ideal of R∞ corresponding to r (cited-hlm17-thm-5-2-1).
items.note: As with 𝔪, the formula does not specify α(T_{v₁}^{(j)}) (issue). R∞/λ ≅ 𝒪 (λ is an 𝒪-point). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: S̃(U^p, W_{Σ₀⁺})[λ] ≠ 0
items.statement: Set W := W_{Σ₀⁺} (as printed: 'as in Section 5.3.3'). Then S̃(U^p, W)[λ] is nonzero ('By Theorem 5.3.1').
items.note: Needs r minimally ramified (assumed in Theorem 5.3.5, but only in the next sentence here) and the proof, not the statement, of Theorem 5.3.1 (r is a point of Supp M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)°) at the fixed level) or local–global compatibility at Σ₀⁺ and v₁ (issue). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [HLM17, Theorem 5.2.1] — a minimally ramified r gives a prime of R∞
items.statement: Since r is minimally ramified, r corresponds to a prime ideal λ of R∞ (an 𝒪-valued point, compatible with R∞ → 𝕋^univ and with the Hecke ideal λ) as in [HLM17, Theorem 5.2.1].
items.note: Cited. Minimality matters because R∞ = ⊗̂_{ṽ∈𝒮} R_ṽ^□[[x₁,…,x_h]] has no local factors at Σ₀⁺: the minimally ramified local conditions there are formally smooth and are absorbed into the variables. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Schikhof dual ·^d and Schikhof duality
items.statement: For a ϖ-adically complete, separated, ϖ-torsion-free 𝒪-module M (e.g. S̃(U^p, W) or S̃(U^p,W)[λ]), M^d := Hom^{cont}_𝒪(M, 𝒪) with its compact topology; for a finite free 𝒪-module L, L^d = Hom_𝒪(L, 𝒪). Schikhof duality: M ↦ M^d is an anti-equivalence between such modules and compact ϖ-torsion-free linear-topological 𝒪-modules, with M^{dd} ≅ M.
items.locator: §5.3.4 and proof of Theorem 5.3.5, published pp. 125–126 (spelled 'Schikhov')
items.note: In the proof only the rank-one case matters: dualizing an inclusion 𝒪 → 𝒪 with image (γ) gives an inclusion with image (γ). Also used: S̃(U^p,W)[λ]^d ≅ (S̃(U^p,W)^d/λ)^{tf} canonically. Planned: CompletedCohomologyPartII CC.3 plans continuous and Pontryagin duals and completed homology.

items.name: The patched module M∞ and M∞(σ°) = Hom_K(M∞, (σ°)^d)^d
items.statement: M∞ (without argument) also denotes the patched module, a finitely generated R∞[[K]]-module with continuous K-action ([CEG+16, §2.8], [Le18, §4.2]), from which the patching functor is recovered by M∞(σ°) = Hom_K(M∞, (σ°)^d)^d for K-stable 𝒪-lattices σ° (continuous homomorphisms; ^d = 𝒪-dual).
items.locator: used in the proof of Theorem 5.3.5 ('Hom_{U_p}(M∞, (σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)^d)^d/λ = M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)/λ'), published pp. 125–126
items.note: Not stated explicitly in the paper; M∞ is used both for the module and the functor. The identification with the functor of [LLHLM18, Prop. 7.15] composed with ∏ι_ṽ is implicit. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [CEG+16, Corollary 2.11] — M∞/λ ≅ S̃(U^p, W)^d/λ
items.statement: With W = W_{Σ₀⁺}: M∞/λ ≅ S̃(U^p, W)^d/λ, K-equivariantly (by (the proof of) [CEG+16, Corollary 2.11]).
items.note: Cited. Left side: M∞ ⊗_{R∞} R∞/λ (λ the prime of R∞); right side: S̃^d ⊗_{𝕋} 𝕋/λ. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The lattice σ(τ)⁰ cut out by completed cohomology
items.statement: σ(τ)⁰ := σ(τ) ∩ S̃(U^p, W)[λ] ⊂ σ(τ) ∩ S̃(U^p, W)[λ] ⊗_𝒪 E ≅ σ(τ), where σ(τ) = σ(τ_𝒮) is embedded K-equivariantly (K acting on S̃ via ∏ι_ṽ) into S̃(U^p, W)[λ] ⊗_𝒪 E.
items.note: Implicit: the σ(τ)-isotypic part of S̃(U^p,W)[λ] ⊗ E is one copy of σ(τ), so the embedding and hence σ(τ)⁰ are unique up to E^×/homothety. This follows from the chain of identifications in the proof (Hom_K(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ, S̃[λ]) ≅ (M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)/λ)^d ≅ 𝒪 by Theorem 5.1.1). The paper writes σ(τ) for σ(τ_𝒮) in the statement. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Theorem 5.3.5 — Breuil's lattice conjecture for GL₃
items.statement: (Global setup of §5.3.) Let r : G_F → GL₃(E) be as in Theorem 5.3.1. Assume furthermore that r is minimally ramified. Let {τ_ṽ}_{ṽ∈𝒮} be a 13-generic tame type. The lattice σ(τ)⁰ := σ(τ) ∩ S̃(U^p, W)[λ] ⊂ σ(τ) ∩ S̃(U^p, W)[λ] ⊗_𝒪 E ≅ σ(τ) (W = W_{Σ₀⁺}) depends only on {r|_{G_{F_ṽ}}}_{ṽ∈𝒮}.
items.note: 'Depends only on' means: up to homothety, for the fixed global setup (U^p, W_{Σ₀⁺}); τ_ṽ is necessarily the inertial type of r|_{G_{F_ṽ}} from Theorem 5.3.1(3). Proof: σ(τ_𝒮)⁰ = Σ_κ γ(κ)^{-1}σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ([EGS15, Lemma 4.1.2]); (γ(κ)) is the index of the restriction of Hom's (thm-5-3-5-step-hom-index), transported by Schikhof duality and [CEG+16, Cor. 2.11] to the image of (5.9), which by Theorem 5.2.3 is the image mod λ of j_*j^*(∏p(θ)^{m(θ)}R∞(τ_𝒮)); by Remark 5.2.4 this ideal comes from ⊗̂R_ṽ^□, so its image mod λ depends only on the framed local points {r|_{G_{F_ṽ}}}. Unstated but needed: independence of the framing (the ideal of ⊗̂R^□ is stable under the change-of-frame automorphisms, since the connected framing group preserves each component p(θ) and j₀ is canonical). Previous pass's statement kept, with exact wording. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).
items.proofOutline: Choose a T40 cosocle lattice; express the automorphic lattice as sum_kappa gamma(kappa)^−1 sigma(tau)^kappa by EGS15 Lemma 4.1.2. Schikhof duality identifies (gamma(kappa)) with the image of the specialised patched map. T44–45 show each ideal is local. Integral torsion-free specialisation and the exact CHT minimal condition are unresolved G02/G07/G08. This is an abstract locality theorem, not a complete explicit Dieudonne formula. Apply T63 to the patched inclusion after choosing the free target. Exactness of patching transports a coefficient-power annihilator of the finite lattice quotient to the module cokernel. The specialized image ideal is correct after removing O-torsion; the raw source need not be O. The global Schikhof comparison is still G07/G08.

items.name: [EGS15, Lemma 4.1.2] — a lattice is the sum of its saturated cosocle lattices
items.statement: As used: let σ(τ_𝒮) have multiplicity-free reduction, σ(τ_𝒮)⁰ ⊂ σ(τ_𝒮) a K-stable lattice and, for each κ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮)), γ(κ) ∈ 𝒪 with γ(κ)^{-1}σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ⊂ σ(τ_𝒮)⁰ saturated. Then σ(τ_𝒮)⁰ = Σ_{κ∈JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮))} γ(κ)^{-1}σ(τ_𝒮)^κ.
items.note: Cited. Multiplicity-freeness of σ̄(τ_𝒮) holds for 13-generic τ_𝒮 (Theorem 4.1.9). The phrase 'for some γ(κ) ∈ 𝒪' in the paper is redundant (γ(κ) was already defined). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The scalars γ(κ)
items.statement: Fix σ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮)) as in Theorem 5.1.1, a saturated inclusion σ(τ_𝒮)^σ ⊂ σ(τ_𝒮)⁰, and saturated inclusions σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ⊂ σ(τ_𝒮)^σ for all κ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_𝒮)). γ(κ) ∈ 𝒪 is chosen so that γ(κ)^{-1}σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ⊂ σ(τ_𝒮)⁰ is saturated (well defined up to 𝒪^×).
items.note: The inclusions σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ⊂ σ(τ_𝒮)^σ are fixed independently of r; only the ideals (γ(κ)) depend on r, and the theorem reduces to showing they depend only on {r|_{G_{F_ṽ}}}. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Index of the restriction of Hom's is (γ(κ)) (step in Theorem 5.3.5)
items.statement: The image of the inclusion (restriction along σ(τ_𝒮)^κ ⊂ σ(τ_𝒮)^σ) 𝒪 ≅ Hom_{U_p}(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ, S̃(U^p,W)[λ]) → Hom_{U_p}(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ, S̃(U^p,W)[λ]) ≅ 𝒪 is given by the ideal (γ(κ)). [Hom_{U_p} as printed; K = 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) is meant.]
items.note: Checked: with ι₀ the embedding defining σ(τ_𝒮)⁰, Hom_K(σ^σ, S̃[λ]) = 𝒪·ι₀|_{σ^σ} (σ^σ ⊂ σ⁰ saturated) and Hom_K(σ^κ, S̃[λ]) = γ(κ)^{-1}𝒪·ι₀|_{σ^κ}, so the restriction has index (γ(κ)). The rank-one statements Hom ≅ 𝒪 are justified a posteriori by the duality chain and Theorem 5.1.1. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Transport of (γ(κ)) to the patched module (step in Theorem 5.3.5)
items.statement: (a) By Schikhof duality the natural inclusion 𝒪 ≅ Hom_{U_p}((S̃(U^p,W)[λ])^d, (σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)^d) → Hom_{U_p}((S̃(U^p,W)[λ])^d, (σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)^d) ≅ 𝒪, and its 𝒪-dual Hom_{U_p}((S̃[λ])^d, (σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)^d)^d → Hom_{U_p}((S̃[λ])^d, (σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)^d)^d, are given by the ideal (γ(κ)). (b) S̃(U^p,W)[λ]^d is canonically isomorphic to the torsion-free part of S̃(U^p,W)^d/λ. (c) Hence, using M∞/λ ≅ S̃(U^p,W)^d/λ, (γ(κ)) gives the inclusion Hom_{U_p}(M∞/λ, (σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)^d)^d → Hom_{U_p}(M∞/λ, (σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)^d)^d. (d) Hom_{U_p}(M∞/λ, (σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)^d)^d is isomorphic to (the p-torsion-free part of) Hom_{U_p}(M∞, (σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)^d)^d/λ = M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)/λ, and similarly for κ.
items.note: Checked: Hom_K(M∞/λ, V^d) = Hom_K(M∞, V^d)[λ] = (M∞(V)^d)[λ], whose 𝒪-dual is (M∞(V)/λ)^{tf}. Uses def-schikhof-dual, def-patched-module-and-functor, cited-ceg16-cor-2-11. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: (5.9) — the index (γ(κ)) is the specialization of the gauge ideal
items.statement: The image of (5.9) 𝒪 ≅ M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)/λ → M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)/λ ≅ 𝒪 is given by the ideal (γ(κ)). On the other hand, by Theorem 5.2.3 the image of (5.9) is (j_*j^*(∏_{θ∈W?(ρ̄_𝒮)} p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮)))·(M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)/λ). Hence (γ(κ)) is generated by (the images of) elements of the ideal j_*j^*(∏_{θ∈W?(ρ̄_𝒮)} p(θ)^{m(θ)} R∞(τ_𝒮)) modulo λ.
items.note: The left isomorphism 𝒪 ≅ M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^κ)/λ holds only for the torsion-free quotient (D25; issue); the image is unaffected because the torsion maps to zero in M∞(σ(τ_𝒮)^σ)/λ ≅ R∞(τ_𝒮)/λ = 𝒪 (T63). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Remark 5.3.6 — explicit description of σ(τ)⁰ for shapes of length ≥ 2 ([Le18, Theorem 14])
items.statement: In the hypotheses of Theorem 5.3.5, assume further that w̃(ρ̄_ṽ, τ_ṽ)_i has length at least 2 for all ṽ ∈ 𝒮 and i ∈ ℤ/f_ṽ. Then the lattice σ(τ)⁰ can be described explicitly as in [Le18, Theorem 14].
items.note: Cited, no proof. The theorem number 'Theorem 14' is in a different numbering style from the '[Le18, Theorem 4.1.5]' cited on p. 123; not checked against Le18. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: §6(1) — meaning of 'special fibre as predicted by geometric Breuil–Mézard' in [LLHLM18, Theorem 1.1]
items.statement: Under the assumptions of [LLHLM18, Theorem 1.1], the special fibre of R_ρ̄^{(2,1,0),τ} is reduced and the number of its irreducible components is less than or equal to #(W?(ρ̄^{ss}) ∩ JH(σ̄(τ))), with equality if ρ̄ is semisimple.
items.note: Stated as a clarification of [LLHLM18, Thm 1.1]; 'can be checked directly using Theorem 6.14, Tables 3, 7, 8, Propositions 8.5, 8.6, and 8.12, and the results of Section 8.2.2' of [LLHLM18]. Not proved here. Recorded also as E101. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: §6(11) — weak minimal patching functor at a fixed level and coefficients
items.statement: In [LLHLM18, Definition 7.11(2)], 'automorphic of weight V' is replaced by 'automorphic of weight V, level U, and coefficients W', where U is a fixed compact open subgroup of G(𝔸^{∞,p}_F) × 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) [sic; 𝔸_{F⁺} meant] which is unramified at places v | p, and W is a fixed 𝒪-module with a U-action on which the factor 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) acts trivially. The definition of patching functor depends on these implicit choices of U and W.
items.note: This is the notion used for M̃∞ in §5.3 (U = U^p𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}), W = W_{Σ₀⁺}). Recorded also as E111. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: §6(12) — corrected definition of e(M)
items.statement: Given a finitely generated R∞-module M with scheme-theoretic support Spec A of dimension at most d, e(M) is d! times the coefficient of the degree-d term of the Hilbert polynomial of M (considered as an A-module).
items.note: Identical to the definition used in §3.5 of this paper (p. 38): e(M) is the Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity when dim A = d and 0 otherwise. Used in Theorem 3.5.2 and hence Lemma 5.2.2 / Theorem 5.3.3. Recorded also as E112. Missing: routed as a source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.3/R03.6 (route 1).

items.name: Definition 6.0.1 — automorphic of weight V, level U and coefficients W; W(r̄)
items.statement: Let r̄ : G_F → GL₃(𝔽) be a continuous Galois representation. Let V be a Serre weight for 𝒢, U a compact open subgroup of G(𝔸^{∞,p}_F) × 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) [sic; 𝔸_{F⁺}] which is unramified at places v | p, and W an 𝒪-module with a U-action for which the factor 𝒢(𝒪_{F⁺,p}) acts trivially. r̄ is automorphic of weight V, level U and coefficients W if there exists a cofinite subset 𝒫 ⊂ 𝒫_U such that S(U, V ⊗ W)_{𝔪̄} ≠ 0, where 𝔪̄ is the kernel of the system of Hecke eigenvalues ᾱ : 𝕋_𝒫 → 𝔽 associated with r̄, and ᾱ satisfies det(1 − r̄^∨(Frob_w)X) = Σ_{j=0}^{3} (−1)^j (𝐍_{F/ℚ}(w))^{\binom{j}{2}} ᾱ(T_w^{(j)}) X^j for all w ∈ 𝒫. r̄ is automorphic of weight V (V is a Serre weight of r̄) if r̄ is automorphic of weight V, level U and coefficients W for some U and W as above. W(r̄) is the set of all Serre weights of r̄, and r̄ is automorphic if W(r̄) ≠ ∅.
items.note: Addendum to [LLHLM18, Definition 7.1]. Different from the W(r̄) of §5.3.2 (fixed level and coefficients, contragredient, K-representations). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Proposition 6.0.2 — level lowering to the minimal level and coefficients
items.statement: (Setting of [LLHLM18, §7].) Let r̄ : G_F → GL₃(𝔽) be a continuous Galois representation with split ramification outside p, which is automorphic and satisfies the Taylor–Wiles conditions. If r̄ is automorphic of a reachable weight, then it is automorphic of a reachable weight and level U and coefficients W, where U = ∏_{v∤∞} U_v with U_v = 𝒢(𝒪_v) for v which split in F except for v₁; U_{v₁} the preimage of the upper triangular matrices under 𝒢(𝒪_{v₁}) → 𝒢(k_{v₁}) ⥲_{ι_{ṽ₁}} GL₃(k_{ṽ₁}); U_v a hyperspecial maximal compact open subgroup of G(F_v) if v is inert in F; and W is an 𝒪-lattice in ⊗_{v∈Σ₀⁺} σ(τ_ṽ) ∘ ι_ṽ.
items.note: Proof (sketch as printed): pick tame types τ_v (v | p) with ρ̄_v admissible for τ_v, ℓ(w(ρ̄_v,τ_v)) ≥ 3, V_ṽ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_v)); then S(U, σ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 for a lattice σ in ⊗_v σ(τ_v)∘ι_ṽ; [EGH13, Lemma 7.1.6, Thm 7.2.1] gives r̄ ≅ reduction of r_π; choose a solvable totally real L⁺/F⁺ (prop-6-0-2-choice-L-plus); R_τ^univ is finite over 𝒪_E by the proof of [Gee11, Thm 5.1.4] (with [Gue11, Thm 3.4] and geometric integrality from [LLHLM18, §5.3]); this yields a minimally ramified potentially crystalline lift r, automorphic over L, hence (solvable base change) over F; local–global compatibility gives S(U, σ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 at the minimal level, hence S(U, V′ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 for some reachable V′ ∈ JH(σ̄). Issues: Σ₀⁺ misprinted for Σ_p⁺; existence of a lift from finiteness needs dim R_τ^univ ≥ 1. 'Level-lowering result based on techniques in [Tay08]'. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Reachable Serre weight ([LLHLM18]; as used)
items.statement: 'Reachable' Serre weights are those of [LLHLM18] (the definition is not restated in this paper). As used in the proof of Proposition 6.0.2: if V = ⊗_v V_v (V_v = V_ṽ ∘ ι_ṽ) is reachable, then for each v | p there is a tame type τ_v such that ρ̄_v is admissible with respect to τ_v, ℓ(w(ρ̄_v, τ_v)) ≥ 3, and V_ṽ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_v)); and the proof concludes that some reachable V′ ∈ JH(σ̄) (σ a lattice in ⊗_v σ(τ_v) ∘ ι_ṽ) has S(U, V′ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0.
items.locator: §6(16), Proposition 6.0.2 and its proof, published pp. 130–132
items.note: Cited notion; the reading could not consult [LLHLM18] to state the definition. The last step of the proof needs that the Jordan–Hölder factors of σ̄ contributing to S(U, σ̄ ⊗ W̄)_𝔪 include a reachable one, which presumably follows from the definition. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [LLHLM18] — admissibility of ρ̄ for τ and the shape w(ρ̄, τ) (as used)
items.statement: For ρ̄_v (the restriction of r̄ to the decomposition group at ṽ, v | p) and a tame inertial type τ_v, '[ρ̄_v] is admissible with respect to τ_v' and the shape w(ρ̄_v, τ_v) (an element of the admissible set with length ℓ(w(ρ̄_v, τ_v))) are as in [LLHLM18]; Proposition 6.0.2 uses types with ℓ(w(ρ̄_v, τ_v)) ≥ 3.
items.note: Cited. The choice ℓ ≥ 3 is presumably what makes [LLHLM18, §5.3] (geometric integrality of R^{□,τ_ṽ}) applicable later in the proof; not checked against [LLHLM18]. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: [EGH13, Lemma 7.1.6 and Theorem 7.2.1] — automorphic r̄ lifts to r_π
items.statement: If S(U, σ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 (σ a lattice in a type, W coefficients), then r̄ ⊗_𝔽 \overline{𝔽}_p is isomorphic to the reduction of r_π : G_F → GL_n(\overline{ℚ}_p) for some π as in [EGH13, Theorem 7.2.1] (n = 3).
items.note: Cited. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Base change and solvable descent of automorphy (as used)
items.statement: (a) π_F, the regular algebraic (conjugate) self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) obtained from π by base change; π_L, the base change of π_F to L. (b) 'Solvable base change': if r|_{G_L} is automorphic and L/F is a solvable Galois extension (here L = L⁺F with L⁺/F⁺ solvable Galois, L linearly disjoint from \overline{F}^{ker r̄}(ζ_p)), then r is automorphic.
items.note: Cited without references in the text (standard: base change from unitary groups to GL_n, and Arthur–Clozel solvable descent as used in [CHT08], [Tay08]). Planned: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.5 plans base change and solvable descent of automorphy.

items.name: The auxiliary totally real field L⁺ (proof of Proposition 6.0.2)
items.statement: Choose a totally real extension L⁺ of F⁺ such that: 4 | [L⁺ : ℚ]; L⁺/F⁺ is Galois and solvable; L := L⁺F is linearly disjoint from \overline{F}^{ker r̄}(ζ_p) over F; L/L⁺ is everywhere unramified; p is unramified in L⁺; v₁ splits completely in L; and if π_L is the base change of π_F to L and w is a place of L above ṽ for v ∈ Σ₀⁺, then π_{L,w} has Iwahori fixed vectors and τ_v|_{I_{L_w}} is trivial.
items.note: Existence asserted without argument (standard). Here τ_v for v ∈ Σ₀⁺ is the minimal type at ṽ, while the same letter τ_v was just used for the chosen tame types at v | p. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: The deformation rings R_τ^univ and R_𝒮^univ (proof of Proposition 6.0.2)
items.statement: Let S := {v₁} ∪ Σ⁺ and S̃ := {ṽ₁} ∪ {ṽ : v ∈ Σ⁺}; S_L (resp. S̃_L) the places of L⁺ (resp. L) above S (resp. S̃); Σ̃_{L,p}, Σ̃_{L,0}, Σ̃_{L,1} the places of L above Σ̃_p⁺, Σ̃₀⁺ and ṽ₁; Σ̃_L := Σ̃_{L,p} ∪ Σ̃_{L,0}. For ṽ ∈ Σ̃_{L,p}, τ_ṽ := τ_{ṽ|_{F⁺}}|_{I_L}; for ṽ ∈ Σ̃_{L,0}, R^{□,τ_ṽ} is the lifting ring of r̄|_{G_{L_ṽ}} parametrizing lifts whose characteristic polynomial is (X − 1)³. R_τ^univ is the universal deformation ring of the deformation problem (F/F⁺, S, S̃, 𝒪_E, r̄, ε^{−2}δ_{F/F⁺}, {R^□_{ṽ₁}} ∪ {R_ṽ^{□,τ_ṽ}}_{v∈Σ⁺}), and R_𝒮^univ that of (L/L⁺, S_L, S̃_L, 𝒪_E, r̄|_{G_L}, ε^{−2}δ_{L/L⁺}, {R^□_{ũ₁}}_{ũ₁∈S̃_{L,1}} ∪ {R_ṽ^{□,τ_ṽ}}_{ṽ∈Σ̃_L}) — analogues of those of [Gee11, §5].
items.note: Deformation problems in the sense of [CHT08] (polarized by ε^{−2}δ, δ the quadratic character of F/F⁺ or L/L⁺). Notation not defined in the paper: Σ⁺ (presumably Σ_p⁺ ∪ Σ₀⁺), Σ̃_p⁺, Σ̃₀⁺; 'characteristic polynomial is (X − 1)³' refers to the inertia action (unipotent lifts); at v ∈ Σ₀⁺ over F, R_ṽ^{□,τ_ṽ} is not separately defined. S here clashes with the set 𝒮 of §5.3. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [Gee11, Theorem 5.1.4] (proof) — R_τ^univ is finite over 𝒪_E
items.statement: The proof of [Gee11, Theorem 5.1.4] shows that R_τ^univ is finite over 𝒪_E: R_τ^univ is finite over R_𝒮^univ, and R_𝒮^univ is finite over 𝒪_E since (R_𝒮^univ)^{red} is isomorphic to an appropriate Hecke algebra, with the Fontaine–Laffaille deformation rings of [Gee11] replaced by R^{□,τ_ṽ} for ṽ ∈ Σ̃_{L,p}.
items.note: Cited. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [Gue11, Theorem 3.4] (proof) — (R_𝒮^univ)^red is a Hecke algebra
items.statement: (R_𝒮^univ)^{red} is isomorphic to an appropriate Hecke algebra, by the proof of [Gue11, Theorem 3.4] (with the local deformation rings R^{□,τ_ṽ} at ṽ ∈ Σ̃_{L,p}).
items.note: Cited. Needs the local rings at p to be geometrically integral (cited-llhlm18-geometric-integrality). Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [LLHLM18, §5.3] — geometric integrality of R^{□,τ_ṽ}
items.statement: For ṽ ∈ Σ̃_{L,p}, the potentially crystalline lifting ring R^{□,τ_ṽ} (Hodge–Tate weights (2,1,0), type τ_ṽ, shape of length ≥ 3) is geometrically integral ([LLHLM18, Section 5.3]).
items.note: Cited. L_ṽ/ℚ_p is unramified (p unramified in L⁺, L/L⁺ unramified) but need not be ℚ_p; the intro of this paper indicates [LLHLM18] treats unramified K for shapes all of whose components have length > 1 (published p. 34: nontriviality from [LLHLM18, Table 7]; only the short shapes needed K = ℚ_p), so the citation plausibly covers this case; not checked against [LLHLM18]. Missing: routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (route 2).

items.name: Existence and automorphy of a minimally ramified lift (step in Proposition 6.0.2)
items.statement: That R_τ^univ is finite over 𝒪_E implies that there is a conjugate self-dual lift r : G_F → GL₃(\overline{ℚ}_p) of r̄ which is minimally ramified outside p and potentially crystalline of type ((0,1,2), τ_v) at ṽ for each v ∈ Σ₀⁺ [sic: Σ_p⁺]. The restriction r|_{G_L}, which corresponds to a point of Spec R_𝒮^univ, is automorphic; solvable base change implies r is automorphic; local–global compatibility implies S(U, σ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 for U and W as in Proposition 6.0.2; then S(U, V′ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 for some reachable V′ ∈ JH(σ̄).
items.note: Two issues: Σ₀⁺ should be Σ_p⁺; and finiteness over 𝒪_E gives a \overline{ℚ}_p-point only together with the lower bound dim R_τ^univ ≥ 1 (standard, part of the proof of [Gee11, Thm 5.1.4]). 'Automorphic' for r|_{G_L} follows from (R_𝒮^univ)^{red} ≅ 𝕋. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Local–global compatibility (as used in Proposition 6.0.2 and §5.3.4)
items.statement: For an automorphic r with the relevant local properties: at v | p, potentially crystalline of type τ_v (Hodge–Tate weights (0,1,2)) implies that the corresponding local component contains σ(τ_v); at v ∈ Σ₀⁺, minimal ramification implies it contains σ(τ_ṽ). Consequently S(U, σ ⊗ W)_𝔪 ≠ 0 at the minimal level U and coefficients W.
items.note: Cited without reference. Planned: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.6 plans local–global compatibility at p.

items.name: §6(16) — consequence for [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.8]
items.statement: Proposition 6.0.2 shows that M∞(⊗_{v∈Σ_p⁺} σ̄(τ_v)°) is nonzero in the third paragraph of the proof of [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.8] (one cannot directly cite [LLHLM18, Definition 7.11(2)] because of the change in §6(11)).
items.note: Also: 'The proof of Theorem 7.4 [of LLHLM18], which was omitted, uses the same techniques' — relevant to Theorem 5.3.1 (issue). Recorded also as E116. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: [Tay08] — techniques for level lowering (as used)
items.statement: Proposition 6.0.2 is 'a level-lowering result based on techniques in [Tay08]', and the omitted proof of [LLHLM18, Theorem 7.4] 'uses the same techniques'.
items.note: Cited for method only; no specific statement of [Tay08] is invoked. Missing: routed to the Part II GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices (route 5).

items.name: Local-cohomology restriction exact sequence
items.statement: For Noetherian A, ideal I, U=Spec A minus V(I), and A-module M, the Ext-colimit local cohomology of L06 fits functorially into 0→H_I^0(M)→M→Sec_U(M)→H_I^1(M)→0.
items.note: Planning statement; not a formalisation. Compare the Ext colimit with derived I-power torsion using an injective resolution and exact filtered colimits. For Noetherian A this agrees with support cohomology (0955). The augmented finite localization Čech complex computes that support functor (0952/0A6T). Its first two cohomology groups are the kernel and cokernel of M→Sec_U(M). The Noetherian comparison is essential, not a theorem already provided by L06. Missing: routed as a source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 (route 7).
items.proofOutline: Compare the Ext colimit with derived I-power torsion using an injective resolution and exact filtered colimits. For Noetherian A this agrees with support cohomology (0955). The augmented finite localization Čech complex computes that support functor (0952/0A6T). Its first two cohomology groups are the kernel and cokernel of M→Sec_U(M). The Noetherian comparison is essential, not a theorem already provided by L06.
